pages.description: Proměňte to, co relace pozorovaly, v přezkoumané znalosti a v pravidlo, dovednost, dokument či test, kam která lekce patří, pak změnu dodejte a řekněte každému peerovi, co se pohnulo.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Implementovat změnu
pages.description: Provedte požadovanou změnu repozitářem nejdřív podle důkazů, od invariantu, který musí zachovat, po ověřený, sladěný, zdokumentovaný a commitnutý strom, bez rozšiřování jejího rozsahu.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Zabalit zdroje pro projekt ChatGPT
pages.description: Proměnit commitnutý strom v Markdown shardy omezené tokeny, které indexuje vyhledávání souborů projektu ChatGPT, ověřené tak, že nenesou binárku, worktree, odkaz, výstup buildu, projekci ani uniklou hodnotu, a předat je s commitem, z něhož byly vyřezány.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Zabalte repozitář pro vnějšího recenzenta
pages.description: Připravte omezený, reprodukovatelný snímek sledovaného stromu pro recenzenta, který nemůže číst repozitář přímo, s vynecháním lokální poloviny a čehokoli tajného a se zapsanými otázkami, na které musí recenze odpovědět.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Revize repozitáře
pages.description: Přezkum skutečného stavu repozitáře, nebo jedné změny v něm, řízený důkazy, než se doporučí nebo provede smysluplná inženýrská práce.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Hlásit podle stavu ověření
pages.description: Zapište výsledek práce jako tvrzení, z nichž každé je označeno VERIFIED, PARTIAL nebo BLOCKED podle skutečně pozorovaných důkazů, aby čtenář rozlišil, co bylo dokázáno a co jen uděláno či zamýšleno.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Co Majordomus dozoruje
pages.description: 11 odpovědností, jedna vrstva. Každá je soubor v .ai/ a podpříkaz, který ho čte.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Doctor
pages.description: dokazuje, že instalace je skutečná: politika se parsuje, každé deklarované vynucování skutečně vyvolá hook, který pojmenovává, bez spolknutého exit kódu, každá projekce odpovídá vlastnímu razítku, vždy načítaný soubor je pod rozpočtem
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Dokončení
pages.description: typovaný výsledek a smlouva vyhodnocená řádek po řádku; pokud selže kterýkoli řádek, nic se nezapíše
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Předávka
pages.description: záznamy jen pro připojování s vypočteným front matter a povinnými sekcemi, vytvářené atomicky, nikdy nestagované; --resolve najde ten správný pro tento worktree a větev a označí, jak daleko git od té doby došel
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Vrstva
pages.description: jeden přenosný adresář .ai/, čitelný bez nástroje: .ai/repo/ je sledovaný a kanonický, .ai/local/ je vlastní tomuto checkoutu a ignorovaný; doctor dokládá, že se manifest vyřeší, každá sekce, kterou jmenuje, existuje a nic pod local/ není sledováno
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Plán
pages.description: milníky jsou specifikace výsledků a úkoly jsou prováděcí smlouvy; stav, vlny provádění a další připravený úkol se odvozují z grafu závislostí a nikdy se neukládají
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Politika
pages.description: jedno policy.yaml nezávislé na providerovi; neznámé klíče jsou chyby
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Profily
pages.description: jeden balíček na třídu úloh, každý nastavuje třídu schopností, úsilí uvažování, rozvláčnost, prezentaci, přepínače kontextu, ověřování a interval checkpointů nezávisle
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Projekce
pages.description: update deterministicky generuje CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md nebo jakýkoli cíl, který pojmenujete, a každý označí hashem politiky a hashem vlastního obsahu; ruční úprava se zjistí a nikdy se tiše nepřepíše
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Rozsah
pages.description: start bere cesty, kterých se úloha smí dotknout; check a finish selžou na souborech mimo ně; překrývající se claimy jiných worktree se hlásí
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Stav
pages.description: jedna aktivní úloha na checkout v current.yaml, s branch, head a working_tree počítanými z gitu, nikdy ručně psanými
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Watch
pages.description: hlásí drift mezi politikou, projekcemi, stavem, rozsahem a gitem, každé zjištění s příkazem, který ho reprodukuje
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Sázka na vrstvu, ne na model
pages.description: Proč Majordomus není další AI agent: modely se stanou zaměnitelnými, koordinaci si jejich výrobci vezmou sami a co zbývá, je nestranný doklad, že práce je hotová.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: The bet on a layer, not a model
pages.description: Why Majordomus is not another AI agent: models will become interchangeable, their makers will take coordination for themselves, and what is left is impartial proof that the work is done.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Případy užití
pages.description: Co s tím lidé dělají: úloha, příkazy, které na ni odpovídají, a co vám zůstane v rukou, vše dokázáno proti nástroji. Každý krok je skutečné volání, každé pravidlo a příslib skutečný objekt a každý příklad níže byl spuštěn, aby vznikla tato stránka.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Rozhodněte, zda je dokončená práce skutečně dokončená
pages.description: Vyhodnoťte smlouvu řádek po řádku, místo abyste přijali větu, která říká, že práce je hotová.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Přidejte případ užití a nechte nástroj, ať ho doloží
pages.description: Vytvořte scaffold návrhu pro nepokrytý příkaz, zvalidujte ho, spusťte jeho scénář proti skutečnému nástroji a sledujte, jak se pokrytí posune.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Převzít repozitář, který už má vlastní pravidla
pages.description: Nainstalujte dozorovou vrstvu do repozitáře s ručně psaným CLAUDE.md, aniž by si nástroj přivlastnil soubor, který napsal někdo jiný.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Začínáme a převzetí
pages.description: Zavedení Majordoma do repozitáře, nového či starého, aniž by se ztratilo, co lidé už napsali.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Zablokujte přijetí kvůli otázce, na kterou nikdo neodpověděl
pages.description: Otevřete k úloze otázku, sledujte, jak finish odmítne dokončení, dokud není vyřešená, vyřešte ji odpovědí a teprve pak dokončete.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Uchovat prompty, které práci zahájily, pod modelem, ne kolem něj
pages.description: Zapojte hook providera, dokažte jej protažením payloadu a ověřte, že prompt, který nástroj nedokázal parsovat, se ohlásí, a ne tiše zahodí.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Předat práci s otevřenou otázkou a nechat ji blokující
pages.description: Uzavřete úlohu do předávky, zatímco je otázka nevyřešená, spusťte navazující úlohu a podívejte se, že tatáž otázka tam stále odmítá přijetí.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Odhalit agenta, který tvrdí, že je hotov, a není
pages.description: Jedna úloha od začátku do konce: worker vybočí ze svého rozsahu, prohlásí, že je hotový, předá a je přijat teprve poté, co projde vlastní ověření repozitáře.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Dlouhou práci checkpointujte, aby přerušení stálo minuty, ne celý den
pages.description: Zaznamenávejte stručný postup uvnitř aktivní úlohy v intervalu profilu, aby relace, která skončí bez varování, nechala další místo, kde začít.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Rozhodnout, co patří do AI kontextu, jako data
pages.description: Přečtěte deklarovanou politiku rozsahu repozitáře, zjistěte, které cesty jsou v indexu a které mimo něj, a nechte doctor a znalostní index aplikovat ji místo pevně zakódovaného seznamu.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Dokončit úkol, jen když existují jeho důkazy
pages.description: Podívejte se, jak úkol odmítne dokončení, dokud chybí požadovaný důkaz, přečtěte plán rozvoje, který odvozuje stav milníku, a udržte projekci na GitHubu jen projekcí.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Kontroly dokončení a kvality
pages.description: Rozhodování, zda je práce hotová, se smlouvou, jejíž každý řádek buď projde, nebo selže.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Relace a předávka
pages.description: Zastavování a obnovování práce napříč relacemi a workery z trvalého stavu, nikdy z přepisu.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Pokrytí případů užití
pages.description: Každý veřejný příkaz, zaručené tvrzení a nástroj MCP proti případům užití, které ho jmenují, spouštějí a nesou pro něj důkazy; politika říká, které mezery selhávají.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Dodávat úkoly ve vlnách, které graf vypočítá, a brát další
pages.description: Zvalidujte plán, přečtěte vlny provádění, které graf závislostí dává, podívejte se, které úkoly jsou připravené a které na čem blokované, a vezměte jeden úkol, který má worker udělat teď.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Odmítnout adresář vrstvy, který nic nedokumentuje
pages.description: Adresář přidaný pod vrstvu bez kontextového dokumentu neprojde validací, a to jmenovitě; nic se nevyřeší proti stromu, dokud neřekne, k čemu je, a tatáž hierarchie je čitelná přes MCP i API bez spuštění kontroly.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Drift a smíření
pages.description: Zjišťování, že se politika, projekce, stav a git rozcházejí, a uvádění do souladu.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Rozšiřujte, co spustitelný soubor servíruje, přidáním souboru, nikdy jeho přebuildováním
pages.description: Přidejte do .ai/ pravidlo, prompt nebo uzel znalostí a nechte ho objevit se jako zdroj MCP, trasa HTTP a položka reference, toutéž binárkou.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Rozšíření
pages.description: Přidání druhu, pravidla, příkazu nebo případu užití jako dat, s kontrolami, které z toho vyplývají.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Najít objekt vrstvy, aniž by se četlo vše
pages.description: Prohledávejte trvalé záznamy doslovně napříč druhy z shellu a stejnou otázku položte sdílenému serveru přes MCP pomocí majordomus_search a majordomus_get.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Zjistit, co se odchýlilo od doby, kdy se někdo naposledy podíval
pages.description: Ptejte se, co se pohnulo, místo zda je něco špatně.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Postupovat podle procedury, kterou repozitář definuje, a přidat další
pages.description: Přečíst dovednosti repozitáře, vzít jednu tak, jak je napsána, a přidat novou napsáním jejího souboru — žádný registr, žádný kód a kontrola, která říká, co zkoumala.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Podmínit CI samotným nástrojem, s návratovým kódem, který je smlouvou
pages.description: Spouštějte kontroly, které spouští CI, čtěte každý nález s příkazem, který ho reprodukuje, a spoléhejte na návratové kódy, z nichž každý znamená jedinou věc: žádný kód neznamená varovat a pokračovat.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Předejte repozitář někomu, kdo jej nemůže naklonovat
pages.description: Pořiďte snímek, který model přečte nebo kontrola v něm může běžet, bez odesílání čehokoli nesledovaného a bez ztráty režimů souborů cestou.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Předejte nedokončenou práci další relaci
pages.description: Zastavte uprostřed úlohy a zanechte dalšímu workerovi něco, s čím lze jednat a co není přepis.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Nainstalujte nástroj jedním příkazem na stroji bez toolchainu
pages.description: Vložte jeden řádek, získejte ověřenou binárku pro tento stroj a spusťte majordomus init — bez gitu, Rustu, Node, Pythonu, rootu a bez možnosti nainstalovat archiv, jehož otisk nesouhlasí.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Zaznamenat rozhodnutí, aby ho další pracovník našel
pages.description: Zapište, co bylo rozhodnuto a proč, jako stav, a pak to znovu najděte, aniž byste četli konverzaci.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Udržovat každý bootstrap providera tenký, generovaný a v rámci rozpočtu
pages.description: Přegenerujte AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md a další soubory providerů z jedné politiky a dokažte, že jsou orazítkované, odkazují na vrstvu, drží se pod rozpočtem řádků a vyřeší každý odkaz.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Uchovat, co se epizoda naučila, bez modelu a bez konverzace
pages.description: Zaznamenejte rozhodnutí uvnitř epizody, odvoďte ho z ledgeru do kandidátského záznamu znalostí, přečtěte důkaz, že odvození proběhlo, a sledujte, jak druhé odvození nic nezmění.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Vědět, zda je práce v tomto checkoutu dokončena
pages.description: Zeptejte se repozitáře, ve kterém stojíte, a nechte si jmenovitě říct, co zbývá dodat.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Zkontrolujte verzi, než uvěříte diagnóze
pages.description: Vytiskne verzi, kterou odvozují všechny ostatní plochy, a ukáže argument, který odmítne.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Znalosti repozitáře
pages.description: Co repozitář deklaruje o sobě: zdroje, uzly, hrany, plán a jejich vyhledávání.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Nechat relaci otevřít a uzavřít, aniž by na to někdo musel pamatovat
pages.description: Zapojit vlastní události relace poskytovatele, a epizoda se otevře, když sezení začne, předá pracovníkovi, co po sobě nechalo to poslední, zaznamená, co kompakce hodlá zahodit, a zavře se záznamem pokračování vedle své obálky.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Obsluha vrstvy pro AI klienty
pages.description: Jeden sdílený server na repozitář, každý klient je peer, tatáž vrstva přes MCP, HTTP i příkazovou řádku.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Přesunout repozitář z rozložení před .ai do vrstvy
pages.description: Podívejte se, co by migrace přesunula, přesuňte to se zálohou a dokažte, že výsledek je vrstva, kterou nástroj čte.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Zaznamenat, co jeden pracovník udělal v jednom sezení
pages.description: Otevřete relaci, odvádějte práci v rámci úloh, kterých se dotkne, a uzavřete ji do obálky, která odkazuje na to, co vytvořila, a nic nekopíruje.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Výkon
pages.description: Měření výkonu odvozená z registru, základní hodnoty jako data a rozpočty, vůči nimž doctor hlásí.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Rozdělení pracovního stromu do commitů a kontrola každé zprávy podle politiky
pages.description: Zeptejte se, co by tento strom commitnul a proč, naučte se slovník rozsahů z historie místo z tabulky a získejte verdikt k jedné zprávě nebo k celému rozsahu dřív, než ho musí dát recenzent.
pages.section: Prismatic Majordomus — odlehčená řídicí dozorová vrstva pro práci s podporou AI

pages.title: Documentation
pages.description: Every document in the repository, rendered from the same Markdown GitHub shows.

pages.title: First run in a foreign repository
pages.description: forensic finding, closed: what `doctor` reported in a repository that is not this one, why the findings tracked the tool's own distribution rather than the adopting repository, and the release stamp that now scopes them

pages.title: Adoption
pages.description: day one, week one, several workers, removal

pages.title: HTTP API
pages.description: The projection of a repository's AI layer: every rule, prompt, session and project record under .ai/, the capabilities that read them and the declared commands that change them, served over MCP, HTTP and the command line from one registry.

pages.title: HTTP API: artifacts
pages.description: What `majordomus generate` writes: every document with the encodings it is committed in — JSON for a program, YAML beside it, Markdown for a reader — each with its schema, its source and its hash, reconciled with the working tree. The declaration is the generator's own manifest; nothing here keeps a list.

pages.title: HTTP API: brief
pages.description: What surrounds one working session, in one line and in a few: its episode and task, the peers of every board, the mesh, the integration queue and the derive queue, each section asked of its owner once and saying whether it could be read. The answer a session reports on itself from without being asked, and the one a provider mod shows as its status line (ADR 0136). Writes nothing.

pages.title: HTTP API: capabilities
pages.description: The registry seen through itself: every capability with its kind, stability, provenance, exposures, benchmark and cache policy, and one capability in full.

pages.title: HTTP API: commands
pages.description: Every command this repository offers, from whichever program offers it: the Rust executable, the shell tool that carries the task lifecycle, and the workflows the repository declares for a person to run. Composed from the three declarations that already exist — the clap tree, the shipped command registry and the workflow runner's own dump — never from a list. Each command carries what running it changes, what it needs, where its argument values come from, and every surface that carries it, with the reason when one does not.

pages.title: HTTP API: commit
pages.description: The commit as a value: the scope vocabulary this repository's own history yields, what the working tree would commit and how it divides, and the verdict on one message against the repository's commit policy.

pages.title: HTTP API: continuity
pages.description: What this checkout's lifecycle is holding: the open episode, the record the next worker would resume from with the label that says how far to trust it, the newest progress note, and what is blocking acceptance. Read from the local half of the layer, which this process serves to the worker in front of it and never publishes.

pages.title: HTTP API: convergence
pages.description: Whether every unit of work in this repository is somewhere another worker could find it. A holding is anything that can hold work — a work tree with uncommitted files, a branch with commits, a stash — and each carries a disposition read from git: integrated (the trunk reaches it), published (a remote-tracking ref reaches it), local_only (committed on this disk and nowhere else) or uncommitted. The last two are at risk: they are invisible to every other worker, and a worker that stops is not a rollback. Measured offline, from this checkout alone; whether a pull request exists for a branch is a question for the forge and is not asked here.

pages.title: HTTP API: dashboard
pages.description: The Dashboard Suite as a projection of the canonical state: every card is one fact read out of an existing capability's answer, carrying the capability it asked, the input, the JSON pointer its value was read from, the Cockpit page that holds the evidence and the command that acts on it. No dashboard stores, counts or judges anything of its own (ADR 0088).

pages.title: HTTP API: delivery
pages.description: Whether each product feature exists, computed and never recorded: on the trunk, deployed, publicly verified, its required tests current, that evidence published and linked from the interface — each a verdict of pass, fail or unknown with the reason and the remediation, and unknown never a pass. A feature short of any of them is not delivered, and its development stage (implemented on a branch, on master, tested, deployed) is a different type from delivery.

pages.title: HTTP API: deploy
pages.description: The deployments this repository declares, read from the canonical objects the index holds, and whether they would work — decided against the capability registry this process built and the workspace it sits in. Every operation is a read: a deployment is changed by the trusted command line and by CI, never over HTTP and never by an MCP client.

pages.title: HTTP API: design
pages.description: The one declaration of how every surface of this tool looks — the semantic roles, the status vocabulary, the type scale, the theme contract — as this executable carries it: its fingerprint, its tokens, what any one of them means, and whether the colours it pairs are readable on one another. The stylesheets the site and the Cockpit load, the tokens the executable's own pages compile in, and the dataset the site's templates read are all projections of it; a page compares its `--mj-design` with this fingerprint to know whether it is wearing the design this executable was built with.

pages.title: HTTP API: devcontext
pages.description: The context a development session should be given, derived from the repository rather than composed by hand: given an issue, a milestone, an intent or a set of paths, the canonical objects that bear on the work, why each one is in the answer, what was left out and why, what collapsed into what, and the whole cost against a budget. The selection is structured — every entry keeps its identifier, its provenance, the selector that reached it and its confidence — because rendering a prompt is a projection of the selection and not the selection itself.

pages.title: HTTP API: devtask
pages.description: An issue and a milestone read as work to be done rather than as metadata: what a person authored, where the plan graph puts it, what happened to it locally, where its external projection stands, and whether a worker may start it — with the origin of every value on the value. Nothing here is a second project model: the records are the canonical ones, the status and the graph are `plan`'s, the branches and commits are `trace`'s, the readiness vocabulary refines three canonical statuses without replacing any, and the projection onto GitHub stays `scripts/github-sync`'s. Nothing here writes anything, which is what makes a user-authored GitHub value safe from it.

pages.title: HTTP API: directories
pages.description: The layer's directories as a hierarchy: the contract each one declares, what it owes and which contract said so, and the chain that applies to it once inheritance is resolved.

pages.title: HTTP API: distribution
pages.description: How this project is packaged, published and installed: the platforms a release builds, the artifact names the one naming function derives, the installer's canonical command, the releases that were published, and what this build itself is. Every answer comes from share/distribution.yaml and the release records; no surface here states a fact of its own.

pages.title: HTTP API: economics
pages.description: What a coding session consumes with Majordomus installed and without it, from recorded runs: matched control and treatment sessions judged by the same hidden acceptance tests, the provider's usage as it reported it, and every number labelled with its measurement class (observed, counted, derived, estimated, counterfactual). One calculator; every surface is a projection of it, and the verdict states only what the methodology's publication rule allows.

pages.title: HTTP API: editors
pages.description: The files Zed and Google Antigravity read from this repository, derived from the skills and the tracked justfile: what each product supports and on what evidence, the state and content address of every projected file, and what to do about each finding.

pages.title: HTTP API: entity
pages.description: Every object of the layer as an addressable, cross-linked node: its route, its outgoing references, the references that resolve to it, the surfaces that answer for it, and what can be said about its enforcement without running anything. Nothing here enumerates kinds, entities or routes — an object of the index has a route because it is an object.

pages.title: HTTP API: environment
pages.description: What this checkout is right now: the project and its version, the repository and its layer, version control, the toolchains it declares, what the layer holds, the workflows a person can run, the provider projections and the local services — one typed snapshot, with a provenance entry for every value in it. The direnv banner, the Cockpit's overview and this route are renderings of the same value.

pages.title: HTTP API: episodes
pages.description: The execution episodes this shared server holds: one per client that asked for one, opened when the client attaches, kept alive by its own traffic, detached rather than closed when the connection goes, and closed on a deliberate detach, on shutdown, or by the reaper when nothing came back. The episode boundary for a client with no provider hooks of its own (ADR 0103).

pages.title: HTTP API: evidence
pages.description: What actually ran, against which commit, and whether it still proves anything. The claims matrix binds a claim to a test by path; the ledger under .ai/repo/evidence records the latest execution of every test with the commit, the tree state, the digest of the test's own source, the time, the origin and the command that runs it again. Joining the two answers, per claim, whether the repository can honestly call it proven — and distinguishes a run recorded against this very commit from one whose inputs merely have not changed since, because collapsing those two is how a green badge stops meaning anything.

pages.title: HTTP API: executions
pages.description: Running a capability of this registry as work that can be watched: started, followed event by event over the live channel, read back afterwards, and asked to stop. One plane per checkout: `majordomus run` executes in its own process and reports the execution to the server already serving the checkout, so that server lists it beside its own; with no server it says that nothing else can see the run. In memory; an execution does not outlive the server that holds it.

pages.title: HTTP API: gates
pages.description: Completion as a state the repository decides rather than a claim a worker makes: the validation gates this repository declares in its CI model, which of them a task's own change set selects, what each one last reported, whether that verdict still describes the tree it was taken over, and therefore whether the task may be called finished. A gate that has never reported is `queued` and not `pass`, a run whose files have changed since is `stale` and refuses exactly as a failure does, and a gate the change cannot affect is `exempt` rather than unknown.

pages.title: HTTP API: graph
pages.description: The graphs derived from the registry and the index: the executable's own capability registry, the shape of the layer, the rule dependencies, the decisions and what they put in force, and the use cases and what they exercise. Canonical nodes and edges; a rendering library is a consumer, never the shape.

pages.title: HTTP API: guard
pages.description: Whether a write to a file of this checkout is covered by a claim: the active task's scope, or a live mesh claim of the writing session. The judgement a provider's pre-tool hook asks before every edit (majordomus guard hook), switched by session.edits_require_claim.

pages.title: HTTP API: health
pages.description: Whether what this process serves is healthy, decided by the engines that already decide it: the index's diagnostics, the registry builder, the benchmark projection's coverage, the comparison `generate --check` makes and the lease reading `server.status` answers from. No check here has an opinion of its own.

pages.title: HTTP API: integration
pages.description: Every open pull request classified against the current master — ready, needs refresh, waiting for checks, review or a dependency, draft, needs repair, conflicting, blocked, unsafe (auto-merge armed), redundant (its work is on master already), superseded (by a declared successor that landed, named in superseded_by), possibly redundant, other base or unknown — each with the master and head it was decided against, its reasons, its evidence, its risk and its overlaps, ranked deterministically; and the audit trail of the executor that merges the next provably safe one, one at a time. The relation to master is decided by git with this repository's own merge drivers, because the forge cannot run the derived-file driver. Read from the last recorded forge observation; the one exception is the dry-run proof, which observes the forge itself because the observation is part of what it proves moves nothing.

pages.title: HTTP API: intent_realization
pages.description: Which work realises which intent: every task of this checkout's ledger with the episodes, providers and handovers that carried it, every closed session record and every claim on the peer board, joined through the plan to the intents they serve, each link marked declared, observed, derived or inferred; each intent's unmet criteria with the issues serving them; and the drift between closed work and current evidence. Derived on every read and stored nowhere, so an intent outlives every session and provider that worked on it.

pages.title: HTTP API: intents
pages.description: What must become true above the milestones that realise it: each intent's statement, invariants and satisfaction criteria, its stage derived from the plan's milestone status, each criterion's state derived from the evidence ledger, and its verdict derived from those criteria alone. Nothing is stored and nothing transitions; an intent added under the project model is answered by all of these without a registration anywhere.

pages.title: HTTP API: knowledge_base
pages.description: What the knowledge deriver left for review and whether it is still writing: the candidate records awaiting promotion with the branch of the episode each came from, one record by id with every reference it names resolved against the index, the ledger and git, and the derivation status of this checkout judged against the policy's freshness thresholds. Read from the index and the ledger; written by nothing here — the deriver is the shell tool's, and a person promotes.

pages.title: HTTP API: lifecycle
pages.description: The episode lifecycle as an operator sees it: every open episode of this checkout's store rather than only the one the pointer follows, the episodes that can no longer close themselves, the commit this process is answering about against the commit the repository is on, what each provider's adapter declares it can do, and the tracked records a clone receives. Read from the local half of the layer and from the index; written by nothing here.

pages.title: HTTP API: mcp
pages.description: The MCP projection of this registry, described as one typed value: who answers `initialize` and with which protocol versions, the transports and how many sessions each holds, what of the protocol is served and what is not, every tool with the effect and the hints its annotations are derived from, the tools that write the repository, the resources, and where each declared client's configuration stands in this repository. Nothing in it is a list of its own: the tools are the registry's, the effect is the capability's classification, the clients are the distribution's providers.

pages.title: HTTP API: mesh
pages.description: The mesh of this process: discovery — authenticated observations of other running Majordomus instances in one registry — and cooperation — authenticated links to trusted runtimes of the same repository, replicating sessions, claims, handovers and reviews through one journal every runtime folds into the same state. Discovery grants nothing; a link is admitted per peer, and nothing a peer sends executes anything here.

pages.title: HTTP API: models
pages.description: The model catalogue the distribution declares — vendors, canonical model references, typed capabilities, context windows, lifecycle — and the explainable routing over it: what a stated need selects, what stands behind it, and why every excluded model fell out. Declared data; nothing here calls a model or reads a credential's value.

pages.title: HTTP API: monitor
pages.description: Everything that happens around this repository, followed in one stream: the mesh journal (sessions on every linked machine, this checkout's board among them, their claims, handovers and reviews), the executor's trail (merges, refreshes, repairs, closures, failures) and GitHub (pull requests opened, merged and closed, finished workflow runs), folded so that a session re-announcing itself unchanged and a step that decided nothing are counted rather than shown, with what is addressed to the reader marked (ADR 0133).

pages.title: HTTP API: objects
pages.description: The declarative objects of the repository's AI layer: rules, prompts, profiles, policy, documents, milestones, issues, claims, and whatever kinds the repository adds; listed, read by URI, and searched.

pages.title: HTTP API: obligations
pages.description: What a task owes before it may be called completed, and whether the evidence that discharged each obligation still describes this tree. The vocabulary is data the distribution ships and answers in any clone; the closure is read from the local half of the layer, which this process serves to the worker in front of it and never publishes. Read, never written: `majordomus evidence` records, and a second writer for one ledger would be a second account of the same events.

pages.title: HTTP API: observatory
pages.description: What the Observatory may carry to a place where no mesh runs: the mesh scenes this process has live, pseudonymized for publication, and the recording the repository carries, which the published Observatory replays and labels as a replay.

pages.title: HTTP API: pack
pages.description: The tracked tree as a few token-bounded Markdown shards a language model's file search can index, with an index that orients the reader and a manifest that proves afterwards what left the machine: the git index's blobs only, never the working tree, and never a binary, a gitlink or worktree, a symbolic link, build output or a credential, whatever the index holds.

pages.title: HTTP API: peers
pages.description: The workers of this repository, named by their own initialize, and what each announced it is working on — gathered from the board of every checkout, because a server serves a checkout and a repository worked on through linked worktrees has one board per worktree. In memory; gone with the processes.

pages.title: HTTP API: perf
pages.description: This process's work counters and phase timings: what happened once at startup and what happens per call, for the structural tests and the benchmark evidence.

pages.title: HTTP API: plan
pages.description: The milestone and issue model of this repository, and everything derived from it that nobody authored: the status of each record, the dependency graphs above and below the milestone boundary, the topological execution waves, the roadmap order, the milestone being executed and the one issue to take next. Status is never stored — a record says what happened to it and the status follows from that and from the state of its dependencies — so no file can contradict the graph. This capability reads; writing a lifecycle marker into a record is `plan.transition`, which declares that it writes the repository.

pages.title: HTTP API: product
pages.description: What this repository's product does for a person, as the features under the layer's features section declare it: each feature made of modules, commands, kinds, rules, documents, decisions, claims, use cases, Cockpit areas and web surfaces it names, with the interfaces it is exposed through, every count, the moments it answers and what is guaranteed derived from those references. The matrix of features against interfaces, the providers the tool has an adapter for, and the model's own validation. The homepage is a reader of this module and holds no inventory of its own.

pages.title: HTTP API: quality
pages.description: What this executable's own public surface is held to, measured from its syntax tree: documentation that says more than the signature, an executable example on everything that carries behaviour, a module boundary something exercises, and every command of the command line accounted for against the capability registry. The rules are project.rust-public-api-quality and project.operation-transport-parity; this is the measurement of them.

pages.title: HTTP API: reasoning
pages.description: Provider-independent reasoning (ADR 0098): which optional advisors can be asked and what they offer, what a material uncertainty calls for, the session's typed reasoning records — assessments, plans, consultations, disagreements, resolutions, conclusions, validations, attempts — and the state, timeline and provenance they derive. Nothing here talks to an advisor, and nothing here needs one: with none available, the plan is a structured local review and the session concludes on its own evidence.

pages.title: HTTP API: recover
pages.description: The stray files a killed publish, an interrupted rename or an unfinished site build leave in the record stores, classified by reading the clock and the content, and swept exactly once. This is the capability that backs `majordomus recover` (ADR 0040): the command no longer decides what a stray is, it asks.

pages.title: HTTP API: release
pages.description: What this project has shipped and what it would ship next, derived rather than maintained: the changelog composes the layer's release records, the decisions dated inside each release's window and the conventional commits in its range; the version report reads the one place the version is authored and the projection the shell tool prints, and says what the public contract requires it to become — or that it cannot be measured, and so decides nothing — with what the commits since the last release imply beside it as evidence.

pages.title: HTTP API: repository
pages.description: The repository this process serves: its layer, its git state, the state of the index built from it, and its scope: what a worker reads of it and what it never reads.

pages.title: HTTP API: rules
pages.description: What this repository refuses, and what it can actually show for each refusal. A rule declares a class — blocking, where a gate refuses the work, or advisory, where a reader is expected to have read it — and an enforcement block naming either the validator the dispatcher calls or the behavioural cases that prove it. This module joins that declaration to the tree and to the ledger of recorded runs, and reports, per rule, whether what it names is there, whether a runner owns it, whether it was ever run, whether the run passed, and whether the run is older than what it is about. A blocking rule whose proof is missing, dangling or failing is a finding, because a rule nobody can prove is a rule nobody enforces.

pages.title: HTTP API: served
pages.description: Whether a deployment serves the commit it was meant to: the build identity a site serves, read from outside the way a visitor reads it, judged by commit containment and recorded so that a later reader can re-judge it. Only `served` passes; a site that could not be reached, an identity that could not be read, a build from an uncommitted tree and a served commit this clone does not hold are each an unanswered question, never a yes. Observing reaches the network and is a command of the trusted command line; reading the recorded standing is a read on every surface.

pages.title: HTTP API: server
pages.description: The shared server of this checkout and of every other checkout of the same git repository: what each lease says, whether the server it names answers, whether what answers is the code on disk at this executable's version, and how many peers each one holds.

pages.title: HTTP API: session_domain

pages.title: HTTP API: shared types

pages.title: HTTP API: shell
pages.description: The repository's shell automation measured against the tracked migration inventory: new shell is refused unless an exemption declares why it has to be shell and when it stops being, and an exemption whose file is gone is refused too, so the list only shrinks as units move into typed and scripted capabilities (ADR 0069).

pages.title: HTTP API: skills
pages.description: Every skill the layer defines as a proven capability: whether a test names it and the evidence ledger holds a current passing run of that test, whether the site projects its page, whether a doctrine and a CI gate hold it, and whether a workflow, prompt, profile, provider template, recipe or CI workflow invokes it. All four are derived on every read and none is authored; an active skill no test names or nothing invokes is an orphan.

pages.title: HTTP API: trace
pages.description: Which branches and commits realised an issue, and which issue and milestone a commit served — derived from git and from the canonical project model on every call, stored nowhere. A branch names an issue when one of its path components is an issue id; a commit belongs to the issue whose branches hold it; a commit no such branch holds is reported as unattributed rather than left out, because work with no execution contract is what a traceability report exists to make visible. Pull requests are a GitHub fact and this executable makes no network call: `scripts/traceability` reads them and joins them to this answer over the branch name.

pages.title: HTTP API: web
pages.description: What this repository exposes over HTTP, resolved from the producers that make it rather than from a register anybody maintains: the routes the executable answers itself, the documentation build, and every generated report that declared its own mount. The same resolution serves the router, renders the home page and composes a publication.

pages.title: HTTP API: why
pages.description: The operational failure modes this tool is a response to: the moments a reader recognises, the audiences that recognise them, the areas they fall under, and what a reader's own symptoms imply. Every entry is a file under the layer's why section; nothing here holds a list, and a moment added there is answered by all of these without a registration anywhere.

pages.title: HTTP API: worktree
pages.description: Where every linked git worktree of this repository belongs and where each one is. The container is the primary checkout's sibling named with `-wt`, the path under it is the branch name with its hierarchy kept, and both are derived from git's own identity — the common directory, the registered worktrees, the branches — never from a registry, a configuration or the current directory. A worktree somewhere else is a typed diagnostic with a remedy; the migration that repairs it is a command-line operation of the same service.

Eligible only when the classification says it is behind master and its merge conflicts on no authored path; an authored conflict is refused, naming the files. A dry run by default, decided offline on the last recorded observation, like `status`. With `--apply` it takes the integration lease, observes the forge again, records the act on the trail first, and merges master in a scratch worktree, derives, commits and pushes a fast-forward leased on the observed head; it never merges into master. pages.description: the operational failure modes this tool answers, as objects of the layer: the three kinds, the flow from one Markdown file to every projection, what is authored and what is derived, and what enforces each

pages.title: Worktrees
pages.description: the branch-to-worktree topology: `<repo>-wt/<branch>` derived from git identity and never registered, the standings and diagnostic codes, the commands, the lifecycle, the layered enforcement, the fingerprint-verified migration, failure modes and recovery

pages.title: Doctrine
pages.description: A rule is enforced when it is declared, implemented, wired, executed, failure-propagating, tested and CI-blocking. Each one below shows its whole chain.

pages.title: Architecture decision integrity
pages.description: Every architecture decision the repository holds parses against the decision contract, claims an identity nothing else claims, and every relation and reference it makes resolves.

pages.title: AI layer integrity
pages.description: The repository's AI layer is real: the manifest declares a format this executable reads and every section it names exists, the checkout-local half is ignored by git and nothing under it is tracked, and no project data remains under the pre-.ai .majordomus/ path.

pages.title: Blocker resolution
pages.description: No task can be completed while any question on this branch is unresolved; it can still be finished as blocked, partial, no_match or failed.

pages.title: Bootstrap integrity
pages.description: The path from a human reader to the AI layer is unbroken — README.md names AGENTS.md, every generated instruction file points at .ai/README.md, and none of them carries a rule of its own.

pages.title: Candidates are reviewed
pages.description: A review queue that grows without bound is not reviewed. More candidates than the policy cap, a candidate that has waited longer than the policy age, or a candidate the tree does not track, is reported, not stopped; both numbers are declared once in the policy.

pages.title: Catalogue integrity
pages.description: Every use case and application describes the tool in terms the tool has — each command, doctrine and claim it names exists, and the two catalogues reference each other in both directions.

pages.title: Checkpoint freshness
pages.description: A task whose last checkpoint is older than its profile's interval is reported, not stopped.

pages.title: Every public command is exercised and refuted
pages.description: Every public command has a behavioural test and a negative test, computed from the registry and the coverage each case declares about itself rather than from a list someone maintains.

pages.title: The command surface is declared and reconciled
pages.description: Every command the binary dispatches is described by the shipped registry, every command the registry declares public is dispatched, and a command is public exactly when the usage text lists it.

pages.title: Completion is gated
pages.description: A task reaches the outcome completed only when no validation gate its own change set selects is known to be failing, and a gate's verdict discharges nothing once the files that select it have changed since the run.

pages.title: Context budget
pages.description: The always-loaded projection stays within its line budget, every reference in it resolves, it states no count that will go stale, and the assembled context fits the builder's own budget.

pages.title: Context integrity
pages.description: Every directory of the AI layer carries a context document, each one carries the contract, they compose into one deterministic chain for every path, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing.

pages.title: Dependency graph integrity
pages.description: The issue dependency graph is acyclic, every edge names an issue that exists, and no issue is executing ahead of a dependency that is not done.

pages.title: Decision records
pages.description: Every entry in decisions.md carries the task, the head and the reason, so a decision can be found by the worker who needs it.

pages.title: A deployment is described once, and every artifact built from it is generated from it
pages.description: A deployment of the executable is a canonical object of the layer against a closed contract; the container definition and its ignore file are projections of it, never a second description.

pages.title: Doctrine wiring integrity
pages.description: Every doctrine in this registry resolves to a validator that exists, is reached from every command it names, propagates failure, is proved by a test, and is run by CI — and every validator in the source is declared here.

pages.title: Enforcement wiring
pages.description: Every enforcement the policy declares is invoked by the hook it names, from a file the dispatcher will actually execute, without swallowing the exit code.

pages.title: Handover integrity
pages.description: The resolver runs and reports either the record for this worktree and branch or its clean absence; a malformed record is never silently skipped, and a record describing a history this checkout no longer has is reported.

pages.title: Knowledge graph integrity
pages.description: The graph the knowledge compiler builds from what the repository states has one node per identity, no edge with a missing end or without provenance, and no declared path or tracked source that no longer exists; a broken owned reference is a failure, a broken link an author wrote in prose is not.

pages.title: Knowledge integrity
pages.description: Every knowledge record is one evidenced, well-formed assertion. It is valid against its schema with no unknown key, its identity is unique and equals its file name, a verified record carries provenance, every reference it names resolves, a superseded record says what replaced it or why it was rejected, a candidate never claims to be verified, and no record carries a conversation.

pages.title: Knowledge observation
pages.description: While episodes keep closing, the knowledge they produced must keep being derived. A closed episode no derivation followed, once it is older than the freshness threshold, is a stopped writer; a lifecycle whose close path never calls the deriver while the policy switch is on is a writer that was never started.

pages.title: Layout integrity
pages.description: The directories the durable commands write into are installed rather than created on first use.

pages.title: Ledger integrity
pages.description: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event; the one durable record nothing else can reconstruct stays readable.

pages.title: Lifecycle observation
pages.description: A store that can be read is not a store that is being written. While episodes go on opening, the records a future worker resumes from must go on advancing, every lifecycle event received must leave evidence it arrived, and an episode that outlives the staleness threshold must be named rather than left open.

pages.title: Note integrity
pages.description: Every outcome needs a note carrying the sections that outcome requires, and no transcript.

pages.title: Obligation closure
pages.description: A task that declares obligations reaches the outcome completed only when each one is established by the tool or has evidence, and that evidence still describes the tree or the commit it was taken over.

pages.title: Policy completeness
pages.description: Every policy value the code reads is declared in the skeleton policy, and no reader carries its own default for one.

pages.title: Policy integrity
pages.description: The policy and every profile parse, declare version 1, and carry no key the schema does not define.

pages.title: Profile requirements
pages.description: A profile may demand more than the shared contract — a regression test, a decision record — and finish refuses without it.

pages.title: Project model integrity
pages.description: Every milestone and issue file parses, carries the id its filename claims, and contains no key nobody reads.

pages.title: Projection integrity
pages.description: Every generated instruction file exists, matches the stamp it carries, and is never silently overwritten after a hand edit.

pages.title: Prompt capture is proven, or reported unavailable
pages.description: A repository that declares prompt capture has it wired below the model and proven by running it; the archive stays ignored and untracked, every prompt is present as both a record and a rendering, and neither carries anything the model said.

pages.title: A prompt record carries its own identity, is bounded, and is private
pages.description: Every captured prompt names the episode it belongs to or says why it cannot; the archive is readable by its owner alone, bounded by a declared retention policy, and never holds credential material verbatim.

pages.title: Prompt integrity
pages.description: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and every token in it is one the renderer knows.

pages.title: A session does not finish behind its own published site
pages.description: A repository that publishes has a second tree — the one the public is being served — and no commit-level gate can measure it, because no change to any file can make it right or wrong. A session that lands work and leaves the publication owed has finished nothing the public can see, and every check stays green while that is true. The gates that measure a deployment are declared as such in the CI model, and finish asks them.

pages.title: Questions store integrity
pages.description: Every entry in open-questions.md parses, because a gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one.

pages.title: A record's changed_files names the work, not the tool's exhaust
pages.description: The changed_files block of a checkpoint, a handover or a closed session names what the episode produced. Paths a declaration already calls generated, projected or local are classified out, and the classification reads those declarations rather than a list of its own.

pages.title: Retention caps
pages.description: The ledger, the handovers, the checkpoints and the session records stay under the caps the policy sets, so durable state does not grow without bound.

pages.title: The roadmap is a projection, never a document
pages.description: No document is a second authority for the roadmap, and no milestone types its own version. While a hand-written roadmap table exists, it can neither list a release no milestone was released in nor hide one that carried a milestone; a milestone's release (released_in) is inferred from the release records, never typed.

pages.title: Rule package integrity
pages.description: The repository's effective rule set is real: the vendored baseline matches its manifest file for file, every rule resolves with its dependencies and no two claim one identity, and no project rule reuses the vendored namespace.

pages.title: Every object has a schema, and the rules resolve in one stated order
pages.description: The order the rules apply in is written down rather than left in the code; every kind the tool reads declares a schema, every schema is named by a kind, and every path under the repository's AI layer is claimed by a source so that nothing is carried through unvalidated.

pages.title: Scope integrity
pages.description: A task touches only the paths it claimed; work found elsewhere is not accepted as done.

pages.title: The episode boundary is drawn below the model, and its working context is local
pages.description: Where a provider fires session events, the episode is opened and closed by that provider's hook rather than by the model, the start event hands the worker the bounded briefing the policy declares, and the working context each open freezes stays under the ignored half of the layer, carries the declared keys, and never carries a conversation.

pages.title: Session records are shared objects with a closed field set
pages.description: A closed execution episode is written once, into the layer's sessions section, against a schema that admits what the repository can prove and nothing else.

pages.title: Skill integrity
pages.description: Every skill the repository declares parses against the skill contract, names the directory it lives in, carries its sections, describes itself in terms no other skill uses, and every skill or example it refers to exists.

pages.title: State consistency
pages.description: The task record still describes this checkout — same branch, and HEAD at or ahead of the recorded commit.

pages.title: Task continuity
pages.description: A task finished as partial or blocked should leave a handover record, not only a note section.

pages.title: A task on a repository whose mesh is enabled works on the mesh
pages.description: When the repository declares its mesh enabled, an active task's scope is claimed on the mesh — `start` brings the checkout's shared server up and claims it, `check` and `finish` claim it again when a server answers — and a task completed without that claim is refused.

pages.title: Use-case coverage
pages.description: Every public command, and every guaranteed claim and MCP tool the policy asks for, is named and run by at least one active use case whose scenario executes against the real tool; a gap is a failure or a report according to the policy, never silence.

pages.title: Verification integrity
pages.description: Completion requires a verification command that actually ran and exited 0 over a tree that did not change under it; its exit code, duration and tree are recorded.

pages.title: Dokumentace, kterou lze odmítnout
pages.description: Tvrzení, které nemůže spadnout, je jen dobře naformátovaná próza. Jak jsem donutil repozitář odmítat vlastní dokumentaci, co to dneska dokazuje a kde to přestává platit.

pages.title: The product, by domain
pages.description: The few things Majordomus controls for AI-assisted work, each with the failure it answers and the features filed under it. Every member, interface and count is derived from the features that name the domain.

pages.title: Completion
pages.description: Done is a contract the repository evaluates line by line. Work is not accepted while any line fails, and a refusal stays on the record.

pages.title: Context
pages.description: Every worker starts from what the repository already knows: the context that applies to its path, the handover the last session left, and the decisions already made.

pages.title: Coordination
pages.description: Every worker declares the paths it will touch, sees who else is working and where, and hears about a collision before it is committed.

pages.title: Evidence
pages.description: A claim names the test that settles it, a recorded run is judged against the commit it ran at, and a claim with no recorded run says so.

pages.title: Governance
pages.description: The rules are written once, in the repository, projected into every tool's instructions, and a blocking rule stops the command instead of advising it.

pages.title: Surfaces
pages.description: One declaration in the repository becomes the command line, the HTTP API, MCP, the UI, the Cockpit, the documentation and this site, and a projection that disagrees with it fails the build.

pages.title: Token economics
pages.description: What a coding session consumes with Majordomus and without it, from matched runs judged by the same hidden tests. Every number is generated from recorded evidence and labelled by how it was obtained.

pages.title: Everything, followed
pages.description: About a dozen sessions on five machines worked one repository, and none of them could see what the others were doing without writing a polling loop. What one stream of signals with the noise folded away changed, and what it measured on its first day.

pages.title: Evidence graph
pages.description: Every claim this project makes, wired to the document that defines it, the file that implements it, and the test that proves it.

pages.title: Features
pages.description: Every capability of the product as one object of the layer: what it is made of, the interfaces it is exposed through, the rules that hold it and the guarantees behind it. Each card is a file; every mark beside it is derived.

pages.title: Every claim about speed is a recorded measurement
pages.description: The benchmark targets are derived from the registry, so a capability nothing times cannot be merged; runs are compared with a tracked baseline per platform under a regression policy; the shell tool reports where every command's time went; and derived state is computed once per state version rather than per call.

pages.title: CI planned from one model, the site deployed from its verified run
pages.description: The gate model names every validation gate and which classes of paths select it; the workflow is a thin adapter over that plan; the publication path proves the committed derived data current by its input hash and renders it; and the tool supervises its own repository with its own hooks.

pages.title: The Cockpit: the registry rendered for a person
pages.description: At /cockpit the shared server lays out what a capability answered — the registry explorer, every object of the layer, the derived graphs, the directory contracts, the continuity of this checkout, the worktree topology, one health report naming the engine behind every check — and every page is complete HTML before any script runs.

pages.title: A commit message is a value this repository judges, not a convention it hopes for
pages.description: The same parse the changelog reads the history with decides whether a new message passes. The policy is data in the repository's own policy file, its subject width measured from the history rather than taken from the convention. The scope vocabulary is observed from at most 1500 commits of the log, so a subsystem committed today is in it today and a scope nobody uses sinks on its own. A plan over the working tree carries a fingerprint of repository, worktree, HEAD and change set, so a plan acted on after the tree moved is refused rather than applied - and a change set holding generated files is one commit, because only the last of several could carry current derived data.

pages.title: Every directory of the layer carries its contract, and a worker reads what applies
pages.description: Every README under .ai/ is a context document with an identity, a scope, the providers and audience it addresses and how it composes with its ancestors; the repository scope declares what a worker reads and what it never reads; and the briefing a worker gets is assembled from durable state within a line budget with every exclusion named.

pages.title: Sessions, prompts and handovers that outlive the conversation
pages.description: Task state, checkpoints, handovers, decisions and open questions live in files outside every conversation; a session opens and closes into an immutable record; the person's prompts are captured by the provider's own hooks; and the next episode is briefed from those records, labelled by how far git has moved since.

pages.title: Several agents on one repository, without stepping on each other
pages.description: A task claims its scope before the first edit; check and finish refuse a file outside it and report another worktree's overlapping claim; every client of the shared server is a peer that can announce its intent and paths; and each branch has exactly one worktree, derived from git.

pages.title: New code is covered, measured once and asked two questions
pages.description: scripts/rust-coverage is the one coverage authority: a single cargo-llvm-cov export, test code excluded from both sides of every fraction, one rule for lines, functions and regions. Three questions read that judgment — a crate-wide line floor, a floor over the session/continuity domain, and the changed-code differential gate that refuses new debt while leaving untouched legacy debt alone. The differential intersects the export with the lines git says a change touched against the branch's merge-base, working tree included, and distinguishes PASS, FAIL, UNKNOWN and BLOCKED so a crashed tool or an unresolvable base is never a silent green.

pages.title: Declare once, derive every interface
pages.description: One typed declaration per capability, one file per object of the layer; every interface, generated document and page is derived from the registry those declarations build, and a stale projection fails the build.

pages.title: Rules a machine decides, wired, tested and CI-blocking
pages.description: Every rule is a portable Markdown object with front matter, and it is enforced in one of three declared modes: a validator the dispatcher runs, a gate or case that proves it, or a stated reason why no program can express it. Doctor walks the dispatch chain from the source, refusing a validator nobody declares and a declaration nothing runs; the proof graph walks the other relation, joining each rule to the tree and to the runs recorded against it, so that a rule naming a case which was deleted is reported as reading enforced rather than being it.

pages.title: Token economics, measured from matched runs and never typed
pages.description: A task corpus runs in a real harness twice — without Majordomus and with it — and the provider's usage, the gate verdicts and the context compiler's counted selection are recorded as raw facts; one calculator derives pairs, distributions, seeded bootstrap intervals and the one statement the methodology's publication rule allows, projected to the CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP, the Cockpit, a generated report and the site; economics check refuses any savings number typed by hand.

pages.title: A claim is proven by a run that happened, not by a file that exists
pages.description: The claims matrix binds a claim to a test by path, and a path resolving says a file exists rather than that anything ran. The ledger records the latest execution of every test with its provenance; the join is derived on every read and answers, per claim, whether the repository can honestly call it proven, only-not-invalidated, stale, failing or never run.

pages.title: Done is a contract, evaluated line by line and refused when unmet
pages.description: A task starts with a declared scope and a profile; check reports whether the task is consistent with policy, scope and state; finish evaluates the policy's contract — scope respected, verification ran, state updated, no open blockers, a note present — and refuses with the reproducing command when any line fails.

pages.title: One command to install, one to initialise, nothing else to trust
pages.description: One distribution model owns every platform, artifact name and URL; the installer, the release build matrix, the installation guide, the website's install block and the public release metadata are generated from it, and a release publishes an artifact for every supported target or it is not published.

pages.title: One registry over the command line, HTTP, OpenAPI, Swagger UI and MCP
pages.description: The Rust executable serves the layer over stdio MCP, MCP over HTTP, routes under /api/v1/, an OpenAPI document with a Swagger UI, and a command line, all derived from the capability registry, which names what each capability changes; one shared server per repository, and every attached client is a peer the others can see.

pages.title: Decisions and knowledge that compound instead of evaporating
pages.description: Decisions are recorded with their reason and their task, open questions block acceptance until resolved, architecture decision records carry typed references to the rules, claims, files and tests they put in force, and the graph of all of it is derived from those references rather than drawn.

pages.title: Every feature against every interface
pages.description: The matrix both ways: each feature against the command line, the HTTP API, MCP, the Cockpit and the documentation, and each capability module, public command and object kind against the features that name it. Every mark is derived; a gap is shown.

pages.title: Sessions on several machines work one repository without colliding
pages.description: Each runtime is a key-authenticated participant; discovery (multicast, broadcast, rendezvous, seeds) only finds candidates, and a signed handshake admits a link only for the same repository, a compatible protocol and a trusted key. Linked runtimes replicate one signed event journal every heartbeat and fold it into the same state everywhere, so an exclusive claim on one machine refuses an overlapping claim on another, a handover published on one is consumed on another, and a runtime that crashes expires everywhere on its own. The CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and the Cockpit render the same state, and every guarantee is held by tests over real processes and a container lab on a real network.

pages.title: The models the world offers, declared once and routed with reasons
pages.description: share/models.yaml declares vendors and models in one place, in routing's preference order, with provenance stated and pricing deliberately absent; models.list and models.route project the catalogue and its explainable routing to the CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and the Cockpit, credential presence is reported without any value being read, and nothing anywhere calls a model — the crate's no-network boundary stands.

pages.title: The Observatory: the repository and its mesh, drawn for a wall
pages.description: At /ui/observatory, and at /ui/kiosk filling the window unattended, the shared server draws the machines of the mesh and their runtimes, the newest events of its journal, the milestones of the plan, the dimensions of health, the published releases and the sessions cooperating, from the same capabilities the other screens read. The published site carries it as a snapshot that says which commit it was read at.

pages.title: Milestones and issues as data; status derived, never stored
pages.description: Milestones are outcome specifications and issues are execution contracts, one YAML file each; the dependency graph decides execution waves and the next ready issue; a milestone whose dependencies are not accepted is blocked whatever its own issues say; and the GitHub projection is rendered offline from the same model.

pages.title: One policy, projected into every tool's instruction file
pages.description: A provider-neutral policy and four execution profiles are the one source; majordomus update renders each provider bootstrap from its template, stamps it with the policy hash and the hash of its own content, and doctor fails a bootstrap that was hand-edited, that carries a rule corpus of its own, or that exceeds the always-loaded budget.

pages.title: Every record names the commit, the branch and the episode that made it
pages.description: The ledger records every durable event with its task and its head; identity fields on any record are computed from git and refused when authored; a closed session is an immutable record of what one episode produced; the person's prompts are captured by the provider's hooks; and retention is capped by policy rather than by forgetting.

pages.title: Reasoning that works with or without advisors, and review that is recorded rather than claimed
pages.description: share/advisors.yaml declares advisory roles by reference to the provider table and the model catalogue; availability is derived from presence and recorded outcomes, with no network; a pure policy plans review by capability and treats no advisor as a structured local review; one writer records assessments, consultations, disagreements settled by experiment, conclusions with computed review counts, and validations; and the state reaches the command line, HTTP, MCP, the Cockpit, the environment banner, doctor, the context briefing and the derived handover.

pages.title: Skills are procedures as data, discovered and checked, never registered
pages.description: A skill is a provider-neutral procedure for one bounded kind of work, front matter under a schema over a body with a purpose, a procedure and an output contract; the source class discovers it, skills check holds every one to its contract, and nothing loads a skill unless the task is about it.

pages.title: majordomus ui: the delivery, for a person
pages.description: At /ui the shared server lays out the delivery in the project's own words, composed only of what capabilities answered, asked together so the first screen paints in the time of its slowest source; a panel whose source is slow arrives on its own route, and the Cockpit beneath it is one click away for the source of any value.

pages.title: Every use case is executed against the tool, not described
pages.description: A use case names the commands, rules, claims and applications it relies on and carries a scenario as data; usecase run executes it in a disposable repository and records normalised evidence; maturity is observed from the evidence; coverage of commands, guaranteed claims and MCP tools is tallied and the policy says which gaps fail.

pages.title: The failure modes it answers are objects, not marketing pages
pages.description: Moments, audiences and areas are kinds of the layer; a moment names the commands, capabilities, claims, rules and use cases that answer it, each reference validated; the catalogue, the questionnaire, the diagnosis and every page and filter are derived from those files.

pages.title: One branch, one worktree, at a path derived from git
pages.description: The container is the primary checkout's sibling named with -wt, a branch's worktree is the branch name under it with its hierarchy kept, both derived from git identity and registered nowhere; a pre-commit guard refuses a feature branch committed from anywhere else, and migration moves a misplaced worktree with its uncommitted work, fingerprinted before and after.

pages.title: Getting started
pages.description: From nothing to a supervised repository. Every command below exists in the CLI reference; nothing here is a target.

pages.title: Guaranteed, advisory, planned
pages.description: What Majordomus does today, row by row, with the file that implements it, the test that is to prove it, and what that test's recorded run says.

pages.title: Every candidate derived from an observation carries a route — platform, enforcement, generator, documentation or project — derived from its subject's structure and never from its wording, and in a repository that adopted the tool its own share/ routes project
pages.description: A candidate derived from an observation says which owner should look first — platform, enforcement, generator, documentation or project — read from its subject's structure and never from its words. In a repository that adopted the tool, the project's own share/ is the project's, and a project's defect is never routed into the tool's governance.

pages.title: Every Mermaid diagram of the built site gets an id (diagram-<name>), the list of its nodes, the viewer's controls and a link for each node that is the identity of an object the site has a page for, all derived at build; a link to
pages.description: A diagram on the site is a  mermaid  fence in a document, or Mermaid source a template

pages.title: Every finding a command reports names the command that reproduces it
pages.description: A finding without a way to see it again is an opinion. The reproduce command is what lets

pages.title: knowledge observe records one observation.recorded ledger line with its kind, subject, statement and typed evidence references, inside an open episode, inside a task or outside one, and refuses any other shape, or the absence of an episode, without writing
pages.description: A worker records friction it met — a workaround, a defect, a drift, a repeated manual step — with one command, majordomus knowledge observe, and the ledger gains one observation.recorded line carrying the kind, the subject, the statement and the evidence references. The command works inside a task and outside one. Anything not of that shape is refused with exit 2 and nothing is written.

pages.title: A test case that declines to run is reported as a skip and recorded as one, so the evidence ledger can never read a case that asserted nothing as the proof of the claim it names
pages.description: A case in test/cases/ may be unable to run where it finds itself: no jq, no zola, no

pages.title: An architecture decision is one file under the layer's adrs section, validated against the decision contract, with an identity nothing else claims, reciprocal supersession, and every reference it makes resolving
pages.description: A decision is data, not prose the tool happens to store. .ai/repo/adrs/<NNNN>-<slug>.md

pages.title: majordomus adr propose writes a decision with status proposed and refuses to write any other status, allocates its identity under a lock so concurrent workers never collide, and records what the decision was derived from
