pages.description: Every reference a feature makes is typed and resolves against the registry that owns it: a

pages.title: Which interfaces a feature is exposed through, what stands behind it and what it answers are derived from the registries that own those facts, never authored, and a source file that writes one down is refused by its schema
pages.description: A feature file holds two things: **references** naming what the feature is made of, and

pages.title: Capability class, reasoning effort, output verbosity, context and verification are five independent axes
pages.description: A profile sets five things separately: which capability class of model the task deserves, how much reasoning effort, how verbose the output should be, which context to load, and what verification is required — plus a checkpoint interval and an output contract. None of them implies another. A debugging task can want high effort and concise output; a deep-work task detailed output and a decision record.

pages.title: Every profile is parsed, its unknown keys rejected, and the default profile proven to exist
pages.description: Each file under .ai/repo/profiles/ must parse, must carry only known keys, must have a name equal to its filename, and the profile the policy names as default must exist as a file. A policy that points at a profile nobody wrote is a failure, not a fallback to something else.

pages.title: Milestones and issues are canonical repository files, and a key nobody reads is an error
pages.description: A milestone is one file under .ai/repo/project/milestones/, an issue is one file under .ai/repo/project/issues/, and both are hand-written YAML in the same restricted subset the policy uses. Every key in them is checked against an allowlist in share/allow/. A key that no code reads is a failure of majordomus plan validate and of majordomus doctor, not a comment.

pages.title: Issue and milestone status is derived from recorded facts and is stored nowhere
pages.description: There is no status: field in an issue or a milestone. Writing one is an unknown key. An issue records what happened to it — started_at, verified_at, completed_at, cancelled, and its evidence — and BLOCKED, READY, ACTIVE, VERIFY, DONE or CANCELLED follows from those facts together with the state of the issues it depends on. A milestone's status follows from its issues and its own evidence.

pages.title: A pull request that edits a projected plan record is not refused because GitHub does not show the edit yet, and the trunk is refused for it once a declared window has passed
pages.description: GitHub's issues and milestones are a projection of the plan on the trunk. A pull request

pages.title: Every generated instruction file carries its own stamp, and a hand edit is detected
pages.description: When update writes a projection it stamps it: the first line of a file-mode target, or the begin marker of a region-mode target, names the hash of the policy it was rendered from and the hash of the content the stamp covers. doctor and watch hash the content on disk and compare it with the stamp; a difference means somebody edited a generated file by hand, and it is reported by name. Nothing is recorded anywhere else, so a fresh clone is checked exactly as the checkout that generated the file was.

pages.title: Provider instruction files are generated from the one policy, deterministically
pages.description: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md and any other target the policy names are not written by hand. majordomus update generates them from one canonical policy, the profiles, and one shared body text, through a small template per provider. Running it twice with the same inputs produces byte-identical files.

pages.title: A repository-local prompt renders against a closed set of state tokens, and an unknown token is an error
pages.description: .ai/repo/prompts/<name>.md holds a small reusable framing — how to frame a defect so the fix is proven, how to write a continuation record, how to review a diff against its claimed scope. They are versioned with the repository, provider-neutral, and rendered against the current task's state.

pages.title: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and an unknown token is a failure
pages.description: A repository can keep prompt assets under .ai/repo/prompts/, and the generated instructions point workers at them. An asset that no longer renders — an unknown token, broken front matter — is a broken reference, and is reported as a failure rather than discovered by the worker who tried to use it.

pages.title: A declared provider hook captures the person's raw prompts below the model, and doctor proves it by running it
pages.description: .ai/local/prompts/ holds the prompts a person actually submitted, written by the provider's own hook before the model was invoked, each one kept twice under a single stem: a .json record and the .md rendering of it. A repository that declares the enforcement is held to it: if the hook stops capturing, doctor fails, and because doctor runs on pre-commit, the commit stops with it. A provider whose prompts cannot be observed is reported as unsupported, not treated as one that had nothing to say.

pages.title: A captured prompt names the episode it belongs to or records that none could be resolved; the archive is private, bounded and free of credential material
pages.description: Every record under .ai/local/prompts/ says which execution episode it belongs to, and says how it knows. Where no episode can be established, it says that instead — it is never attached to whichever episode happened to be nearest in time. The archive is readable by its owner alone, directory included; it is bounded by a declared retention policy that takes prompt bodies and never records; and the credential shapes the writer knows are replaced before anything reaches the disk.

pages.title: What each provider can do about the session lifecycle and prompt capture is one declaration with a citation per cell, every surface projects it, and no provider the declaration names goes unreported
pages.description: A tool that says what somebody else's product can do is making a claim about a third party. This repository was making two of them wrong at once.

pages.title: The provider bootstraps the policy declares (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, ...) are a target of majordomus generate, rendered from the policy and the provider templates byte for byte as the shell tool renders them, and generate --check refuses a hand-edited or stale one in CI
pages.description: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and every other target the policy's projections[] declares are caches of two inputs: .ai/repo/policy.yaml with its profiles, and the provider template (.ai/repo/providers/<provider>.tmpl, else the distribution's share/providers/<provider>.tmpl). The Rust executable's majordomus generate providers writes them; majordomus generate --check, which CI runs on every push, derives them again, compares byte for byte, writes nothing, and exits 10 naming every file that differs or is missing. A rule typed into AGENTS.md by hand therefore does not merge.

pages.title: A page of the published site written in a reader's language is declared with that language and a reason, and is refused unless the page declares the same language itself
pages.description: project.english-only binds this repository to one working language, and version 2 names one

pages.title: A decision and its provenance survive the session: the next session finds them in its context and handover, reuses a standing conclusion instead of consulting again, and reopens it only on new evidence
pages.description: Consultation reduces repeated reasoning instead of multiplying it. A later session reads

pages.title: Majordomus reasons, decides, implements and validates with no advisor at all: absent advisors are reported as ordinary state, material uncertainty gets a structured local review, and the conclusion claims no independent review
pages.description: With none of the declared advisors installed, configured or reachable, a session still

pages.title: The right prior record is resolved by worktree and branch, and an unrelated one is never offered
pages.description: handover --resolve, checkpoint --show and context all answer the same question: of the records on disk, which one is about the work happening here? The answer is deterministic, it is explained, and when there is no safe answer it says so instead of offering the nearest thing.

pages.title: Rotating the ledger archives the oldest lines and never deletes them
pages.description: ledger.retention_max_lines has always been reported by doctor and watch when exceeded. majordomus history --rotate is the action that resolves it: the oldest lines move into a dated archive file beside the ledger, and the newest stay.

pages.title: Durable records are searchable literally, across kinds, without an index
pages.description: majordomus search "callback" looks through handovers, checkpoints, decisions, open questions, prompt assets and the ledger, and prints the kind, the path, the line number and the matching line. A worker can find what was decided about a subject without reading every record.

pages.title: A projection can own only the region between its markers, leaving the rest of the file untouched
pages.description: A projection declared with mode: region owns the text between <!-- majordomus:begin <policy hash> <content hash> --> and <!-- majordomus:end --> and nothing else. Everything outside those two lines belongs to the repository, is never read as input, and is never rewritten. update splices the rendered body into the region; doctor and watch compare the region body with the content hash in its own marker, never the file.

pages.title: Rejected capabilities
pages.description: Considered and deliberately refused, with the reason recorded.

pages.title: A release archive carries every path once and carries nothing but files and directories
pages.description: The tar that a release publishes holds regular files and directories and nothing else: no

pages.title: A release publishes an artifact for every supported target or it is not published
pages.description: share/distribution.yaml marks a target supported, experimental or unavailable. A

pages.title: A tag with a pre-release part is published as a prerelease, recorded on the prerelease channel, and never resolved as the stable release, so an unpinned installer and a node that follows stable keep the highest stable version
pages.description: Publishing v1.0.0-alpha.1 does not change what curl -fsSL https://majordomus.dev/install.sh | sh installs. The alpha is a GitHub prerelease, its record says channel: prerelease, and releases/latest.json keeps naming the highest stable release. A person who wants the alpha names it with --version 1.0.0-alpha.1.

pages.title: Every finding carries the command that reproduces it
pages.description: When doctor, check, watch or finish report a failure or a drift, the line ends with [reproduce: <command>] — a shell command a person can run to see the same fact without Majordomus. A finding that cannot be reproduced independently is treated as a bug in Majordomus.

pages.title: The append-only ledger and handover store have retention caps that are checked
pages.description: state/ledger.jsonl and state/handovers/ only ever grow. The policy sets a cap for each (ledger.retention_max_lines, handover.retention_max_files); doctor and watch report when a cap is exceeded. Nothing is deleted by Majordomus; the cap makes growth visible before it becomes a problem.

pages.title: A session cannot claim review it did not get: a consultation must name an advisor its recorded plan selected, a conclusion's review is computed, and reasoning check and doctor refuse a forged record, provider coupling, a model credential in CI and a refused claim in a document
pages.description: "Reviewed by" is a fact about records, never a sentence someone wrote. The design's other

pages.title: The roadmap is derived from milestone state, and no document may be a second authority for it
pages.description: There is no roadmap file. The roadmap is the milestone graph read in dependency order, and

pages.title: Routing recommendations will be derived from measured cost and outcome data
pages.description: **Planned.** Once cost per accepted outcome exists per profile and task class, Majordomus can say which profile produced the best acceptance rate per unit cost for a class of work — as a recommendation to change a profile, never as an automatic model choice.

pages.title: A rule that no program can express says so in its own front matter, with the reason, and is counted apart from every rule that has a gate
pages.description: Some rules genuinely have no machine expression. *The provenance of what was written* is

pages.title: Every rule names what proves it, and every path it names is in the tree
pages.description: A rule of this repository declares a class. blocking means a gate refuses work that

pages.title: The effective rule set is resolved as a dependency graph in a deterministic order, and a set that does not resolve is applied by nothing
pages.description: A rule is a Markdown file with YAML front matter: identity (id and version, never the file name), class, status, depends_on as exact id@version references, and for the rules the tool enforces an x-majordomus block naming the validator, the commands and the tests. The effective set is every active vendored rule plus every active project rule, ordered so that each dependency precedes the rule that depends on it. Any defect in that graph stops the command that needed the set, with the reason, and no rule is applied partially.

pages.title: A rule's proof state is derived from the tree and the ledger together, and a mechanism that refuses violations is never reported as a run that passed
pages.description: There are two questions about a rule and they are not the same question.

pages.title: Opt-in runtime adapters will clamp read size, output size and fan-out from profile-derived limits
pages.description: **Planned.** Optional, provider-specific hooks into a worker's runtime that clamp how many lines a single read may return, condense oversized tool output (head, diagnostic lines, tail, with a note that it was truncated), and cap how many sub-workers a session may spawn — with every limit derived from the task's profile rather than a global constant.

pages.title: The Rust executable the rust gate built is published as an artifact with its provenance, and every Rust case drives the executable MAJORDOMUS_BIN names instead of building one
pages.description: The debug executable the rust job builds does not vanish with the runner: it is the artifact majordomus-cli-<target>, with a majordomus-cli.json beside it naming the commit, the target triple, the toolchain and the Cargo.lock digest, so a later job or a later phase (a release, a scenario runner over the real binary) can download it, set MAJORDOMUS_BIN, and never run cargo build. Every case that drives the executable honours that variable, as the launcher bin/majordomus-mcp already did.

pages.title: Coverage of the Rust crate is measured with test code out of the denominator, on every change that can affect the crate and on every push to master, and the build fails under the floor in scripts/rust-coverage-threshold or under the session/continuity domain's own floor in scripts/session-coverage-threshold
pages.description: The crate's coverage is a number with a committed floor, and a push that drops under the floor does not go green. Two floors, each one integer in a file of its own: scripts/rust-coverage-threshold over the whole executable, and scripts/session-coverage-threshold over the canonical session/continuity domain declared in scripts/session-coverage-domain. Both are read by every place that measures — the coverage job in CI, scripts/rust-check when cargo-llvm-cov is installed, and just coverage — so there is no second copy of either number to drift.

pages.title: Every gate the Rust executable must pass is one script, scripts/rust-check, and CI runs that script on every change that can reach the crate
pages.description: Whatever the Rust executable must satisfy before it is merged is written down once, as an executable script, and CI runs the same list in the same order. A person runs just rust-check and sees exactly what the pull request will see: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings (a public item without documentation is a warning, so it is an error here), cargo test --no-fail-fast with the unit, integration and doc-example suites, cargo doc --no-deps with warnings denied, cargo bench --no-run, majordomus capabilities validate, majordomus generate --check, majordomus bench coverage --check, and cargo llvm-cov failing under the committed floor. CI runs one gate more, majordomus bench --profile ci --check --no-write, the benchmark check against the baseline committed for its own profile; a baseline is per platform and profile, so the script has none to check locally. Nothing in that list is advisory and nothing is skipped on a branch.

pages.title: The paths of the Rust executable that scale with the repository carry criterion benchmarks that build on every push, and every executable capability declares its benchmark policy, required or waived for a typed reason
pages.description: The work that grows with the repository is measured, not assumed: the YAML subset and front matter parse of one object, one glob match, the index built from a filesystem walk, the registry composed over it, the OpenAPI document, one MCP resources/list and one capability call (benches/projections.rs); the router, the bridge and the shared server over a real socket (benches/shared.rs). Every benchmark is a criterion target declared in Cargo.toml without the default harness, and CI builds them on every push so a hot path cannot lose its measurement silently. Separately, every executable capability carries a benchmark policy: required with the cases its input type provides, or waived with a typed reason; a resource is waived as not_executable.

pages.title: Every item the crate exports has its rustdoc page at the route derived from its path and kind, no item page exists without its item, and a module added to the crate becomes a required page with no list edited
pages.description: The published reference is complete with respect to the crate: every item the crate exports has

pages.title: The site build composes every published static surface into its output at that surface's mount, read from the committed topology with no surface named by hand, and refuses, naming the producer, when a published surface's artifact is absent
pages.description: The published site is more than what Zola renders. Every static surface the topology publishes,

pages.title: The crate's rustdoc is a web surface at /rustdoc declared by discovery from the crate, present in the topology, its committed projection and the home page whether or not its producer has run, and a running server answers /rustdoc/ from the tree its producer wrote
pages.description: The reference rustdoc renders from the crate is one of the surfaces this repository serves, with

pages.title: The crate's rustdoc is published at /rustdoc with the site, built from the commit the site names, and is never committed
pages.description: https://majordomus.dev/rustdoc/ serves the crate's reference as rustdoc rendered it, from the

pages.title: Every builtin module's page on the site links the page the crate's reference documents that module on, from the one module-to-page mapping the rustdoc check holds the published tree to, and only in a build that composed the reference
pages.description: Each builtin module has a page on the site, under /registry/modules/, and each module the crate

pages.title: A rustdoc tree built from another commit than the one it is checked or deployed as is refused, by the integrity check before publication and by the public verification after it
pages.description: The reference is stale when it was built from a commit other than the one it is presented as. That

pages.title: How each declarative kind is read and which keys it may carry is data read at run time, and a repository adds a kind with its JSON Schema without a code change
pages.description: The Rust executable compiles nothing about kinds or keys. On every start it locates the tool distribution's share directory and reads kinds.yaml (for each kind: the format, the front-matter rule, the identity, title and description fields, the version field and its supported values, the schema it must satisfy) and schemas/<name>.schema.json, one JSON Schema per contract, validated with a JSON Schema validator. A repository adds kinds under .ai/repo/knowledge/kinds.yaml and schemas under .ai/repo/knowledge/schemas/, declares a class for them in sources.yaml, and the objects are served; a kind or schema the distribution already declares cannot be redefined.

pages.title: What a worker reads of the repository is declared once in .ai/repo/scope.yaml, out wins over in, and the Rust executable discovers, indexes and serves nothing outside it
pages.description: A repository says, in one tracked file, which paths a worker reads (in: pathspecs such

pages.title: A touched file outside the claimed scope is a failure, not a warning
pages.description: If a task's changes — uncommitted or committed since the task started — include a file outside the declared scope, check and finish fail on it by name. Files under .ai/ and the generated instruction files are always allowed, because the tool itself writes them.

pages.title: A task is started with a declared file scope and a profile, and only one task is active per checkout
pages.description: majordomus start requires --scope: the repository paths this task may touch. It records the scope, the profile, the owner and the git state in state/current.yaml. While that record's outcome is active, a second start in the same checkout is refused with exit code 15. A task ends by finish or by handover --close; the next start archives the old record rather than discarding it.

pages.title: Ranked or semantic retrieval over durable records is deliberately not implemented
pages.description: There is no vector store, no embedding, no relevance score and no index. search is a literal grep across the record kinds in a fixed order. This is a decision, published so that a reader can see it was refused rather than forgotten.

pages.title: A provider hook opens the episode below the model and hands the worker what the last one left, records what a compaction is about to discard, and closes the episode with a continuation record beside its envelope
pages.description: Where a provider fires session events, the episode boundary is drawn by that provider's own hook rather than by the model working inside it. SessionStart opens the episode and hands the worker the briefing the policy declares, PreCompact records what the conversation is about to stop holding, SessionEnd writes a continuation record and closes the episode into the shared record under .ai/repo/sessions/, and none of it depends on a worker remembering to run a command. At the open, the context the builder resolved is written to .ai/local/session-contexts/ and kept for the episode, so what the worker was told is evidence rather than recollection.

pages.title: The session subsystem has a reading of itself — every open episode of the store and not only the one the pointer follows, the episodes that can no longer close themselves, the commit the serving process is answering about, and what each provider's adapter declares
pages.description: Reading the lifecycle back is two different questions with two different answers, and until this existed only one of them had a surface. A worker asks *what am I resuming from?* and continuity.state answers it: one episode — the one .ai/local/state/session-current.yaml resolves to — one handover, one checkpoint, the blockers. An operator asks *is this subsystem working?* and that question is structurally unanswerable from the first, because the pointer is a symlink that the most recent start event re-aims. lifecycle.episodes, lifecycle.recovery, lifecycle.runtime, lifecycle.providers and lifecycle.closed read the store rather than the pointer and answer the second question, over MCP, over GET /api/v1/lifecycle/<name>, and on the Cockpit's Continuity page, which holds no session model of its own and is a projection of exactly these five and continuity.state.

pages.title: A closed execution episode is a shared object of the layer, written by the tool from git and the ledger, valid against a contract that admits no conversation and no absolute path, and discovered rather than registered
pages.description: A stretch of work ends, and what it did becomes a file the whole repository can read: when

pages.title: A bare claude in a supervised repository starts with the repository's session-start prompt as its first message, and a run with an argument, outside such a repository, with the opt-out, or with a prompt that cannot be rendered is left exactly as it was
pages.description: A hook can only add context to a session; nothing but a first message starts a turn. So claude opened in this repository used to receive the whole briefing and then wait for a person to type. With the wrapper sourced, a bare claude here starts with the repository's own prompt as its first message: say how you are attached, read the board, find the work that is owed, check for collisions, announce, then work inside the task's scope and keep everything local.

pages.title: One policy will be shared across repositories and workers
pages.description: **Planned.** One canonical policy distributed to many repositories, with the same projections, the same finish contract and the same drift checks everywhere a team's workers run.

pages.title: The site is deployed by one script, scripts/site-deploy, from a terminal or from the publication workflow; it refuses a dirty tree, a commit master does not contain and a build that is not HEAD's, pushes site/public to gh-pages with the source commit named, and pushes nothing when the output is unchanged
pages.description: scripts/site-deploy is the only way the site reaches GitHub Pages. The Pages workflow runs it after its gate; a person runs it when the operator wants the site live without waiting for the Actions queue (.ai/repo/skills/deploy-site/SKILL.md, just site-deploy). Either way the same checks run and the same branch is pushed: gh-pages, which GitHub Pages serves.

pages.title: Publication is gated on everything that can make the published site wrong and waits for nothing else; the checks that decide whether a change may merge run beside it on the same commit, not in front of it
pages.description: A push to master that can change the site starts one job, and that job publishes as soon as the bytes are proved: the committed derived data is current for the tree, the site builds from it, and every static check over the output passes. It does not wait for the behavioural suite, the crate's gates, coverage, the macOS suite, the benchmark check or the browser probe. Those run on the same commit, in parallel, in the validation workflow, and they gate merging through the ci status — they guard the repository, not the published bytes. Nothing that can make the published bytes wrong was moved off the publication path; what was removed from it is what could only ever have delayed it. Deployments are serialised and the one in flight is never cancelled: GitHub keeps only the newest pending run, so a newer push supersedes every older *pending* deployment, while cancelling the running one would starve publication whenever merges arrive faster than a run completes. Publication is measured from outside rather than assumed from a green job: the site serves the commit it was built from, the workflow waits for the public URL to name this one, and it reads GitHub's own build of the branch it pushed — a build that errored is a failure of the run that published, because publishing is two steps and only the first is this repository's.

pages.title: The site's Registry page is rendered from site/data/registry/registry.json, a dataset majordomus generate site derives from the registry and the index with their fingerprints, and generate --check refuses a stale one in CI
pages.description: GitHub Pages has no content model of its own for the registry. /registry/ reads site/data/registry/registry.json; the Rust executable writes that file from the capability registry and the index (majordomus generate site), and majordomus generate --check, which CI runs on every push, derives it again and exits 10 when the committed file differs. A number on that page that disagrees with the executable is a stale generated file, and the build refuses it.

pages.title: A skill is one directory under the layer's skills section holding SKILL.md, discovered by the source class `skill` the shell tool and the Rust executable both read, so that adding the file is the whole registration and the catalogue, the command, doctor, MCP and the site all derive from it
pages.description: A skill is .ai/repo/skills/<id>/SKILL.md: YAML front matter satisfying share/schemas/majordomus/skill/skill.v1.schema.json over a Markdown body that is the procedure, with optional examples/*.md beside it. Nothing registers it. The source class skill in .ai/repo/knowledge/sources.yaml says which tracked files are skills, and that one declaration is what the shell tool, the Rust executable and the site generator all read. Adding the directory and tracking it makes the skill exist for majordomus skills list, for doctor, for the website and for MCP; removing it makes it vanish from all of them.

pages.title: Every skill is validated against the allow-list generated from its schema, its directory, its sections and its references, a violation names the file and every reason, and a repository with no skills is reported rather than passed
pages.description: majordomus skills check, and doctor and watch through the doctrine majordomus.skill-integrity, examine every discovered skill: no front-matter key outside the schema, schema: skill/v1, an integer version of at least 1, a status from draft, active, deprecated, an id equal to the directory name, and non-empty # Purpose, # Procedure and # Output sections. Across the catalogue: no two skills claim one id, every related id names a skill, and every tracked example opens with a level-one heading. Every violation is a FAIL naming the file and every reason at once, and the command exits 10. The result ends with what was examined — skills, examples, references — and a repository with no skills gets a WARN, never an OK over nothing.

pages.title: The website's skills section is rendered from the skills catalogue, one page per skill carrying the skill's own body and examples, and a removed or renamed skill leaves no page, entry or link behind
pages.description: The site's skills section lists every skill, and each skill has a page of its own that renders its front matter as metadata, its own Markdown body as the page, its examples, its related skills and the path of the file it was read from. Nothing on those pages is typed into the site. When a skill is added, renamed or removed and the site data regenerated, the index, the page and every link follow, and scripts/generate-site-data --check, which CI runs before the site builds, exits 10 while the committed data is behind the files.

pages.title: The behavioural suite runs a bounded number of cases at a time with the serial runner's semantics, a case that writes into the checkout declares itself exclusive and runs alone, and the parallel phase fails naming the paths when the checkout changed under it
pages.description: MJ_TEST_JOBS=4 bash test/run.sh runs the cases four at a time and means exactly what bash test/run.sh means: every case runs, in a disposable repository each, a failing case turns the run red with its own output in front of its verdict, the summary is one deterministic block in name order, a filter that matches nothing is a usage error, and so is an empty case directory. Each case runs in its own repository already, which is what makes them independent; the one thing they share is the checkout they read from, so a case that must write into it says so with # majordomus-exclusive: <reason> and runs after the pool, alone.

pages.title: A task will know which commits it produced, rather than inferring them from a range
pages.description: **This is not implemented.** It is published so that a known gap is visible rather than assumed to be covered.

pages.title: A task record has no dependencies; sequencing between sessions is not represented
pages.description: **Rejected, and narrowly.** A task is the record of one session's work — what a worker

pages.title: Execution telemetry will be recorded once a provider exposes it honestly
pages.description: **Planned.** Per task: input, output and cached tokens, the model and effort actually used, elapsed time and tool-call count — recorded into the ledger next to what it already holds. Only from providers that expose these numbers; nothing estimated is ever labelled as measured.

pages.title: Whether a task added debt, left a branch or a worktree behind, or grew the backlog is answered by the done invariant from git, the debt baselines and the recorded forge observation, measured from where the task started; a reading that was not taken is unknown, never a pass
pages.description: When a person asks at the end of a session whether everything is done, whether any debt was

pages.title: Majordomus will state a total-token change only from matched, verified runs that meet the methodology's publication rule
pages.description: **Planned.** Majordomus will state how much it changes total token consumption only when matched live runs, with and without it, judged by the same hidden acceptance tests, meet the methodology's publication rule. Until then, the statement every surface shows is that no verified total-token-savings claim is available, beside whatever preliminary observation the runs support.

pages.title: The tool runs read-only from any location, and two locations of one version agree about one repository
pages.description: The distribution — bin/, lib/, share/ — is not part of the repository's data. It may be a checkout under ~/tools, a package on PATH, or a copy inside the repository, and every form behaves the same because nothing writes into it. Two copies of one version, pointed at one repository, read the same files under .ai/ and produce the same findings.

pages.title: An outcome is a value from a closed vocabulary, not free text
pages.description: A task ends with exactly one of completed, partial, blocked, no_match, failed (plus handed_over when it continues elsewhere and active while it runs). no_match means the work was done and the thing sought does not exist; failed means the work could not be done. They look alike in a chat — "we found nothing" versus "we could not search" — and are different facts a supervisor must tell apart to decide whether to retry, escalate or accept.

pages.title: The UI's dashboard at /ui links every capability it read to that capability's page, serves under the Cockpit's security policy, and never waits for the pull-request queue, which is a page and a fragment of its own
pages.description: majordomus ui, the primary surface at /ui (ADR 0135), shows a person how the delivery

pages.title: Every public command is named and run by an active use case, a guaranteed claim or an MCP tool without one is a named gap, and the policy says which gaps fail doctor, check and finish
pages.description: A capability that nobody has written a use case for is a named gap, not a silence. For

pages.title: A use case's scenario executes against the real tool in a disposable repository, every step's exit code and output are asserted, and the normalised evidence is what the site shows
pages.description: A use case carries a scenario: a prepared repository and real invocations of

pages.title: From the files a change touched, the tool names the commands, rules, use cases, scenarios and behavioural cases affected, and scaffolds a draft for a capability no use case covers
pages.description: A worker who changed a file does not have to remember which use cases describe it.

pages.title: The rule baseline is vendored into the repository with a manifest naming every file and its hash, and a hand edit is detected and refused
pages.description: The rules Majordomus ships are not read from the executable at run time. init copies the package from share/standard/majordomus/ into .ai/repo/rules/vendor/majordomus/, manifest included, and from then on the repository's copy is the one that applies. The manifest names every rule file with its identity and its content hash, so an edit under vendor/, a listed file that is missing, or a stray file beside the manifest is detected by name. A newer executable reports that it ships a different package and never applies it; the baseline changes only when majordomus rules vendor update is asked for.

pages.title: /docs serves this repository's documentation and /swagger serves the Swagger UI, and neither may take the other's mount
pages.description: /docs is this repository's own documentation — the Zola site, served by the running executable from the same source that is published to GitHub Pages. /swagger is the Swagger UI. /openapi.json is the document the viewer reads, derived from the capability registry. / is the landing page. Each of those names belongs to exactly one producer, and a change that gives one of them to something else is refused rather than merged.

pages.title: Every web surface is declared once at its producer and resolved into one topology, from which the router, the landing page and the machine-readable index are each projected
pages.description: Everything this repository exposes over HTTP is one resolved object: an identity, a mount, a kind, a category, a visibility, the producer that made it, and the provenance of each of those values. The routes the executable answers itself come from the capability! declarations that already exist and are already projected to the CLI, MCP and OpenAPI. A generated directory — a test report, a benchmark report, the documentation build — declares itself beside its own output rather than in a list somewhere else. The application's site is read from the site generator's configuration. There is no central manifest of surfaces, and the resolved manifest written for diagnostics is disposable: nothing reads it as truth that could not be recomputed.

pages.title: An operational moment is one file under the layer, discovered rather than registered, and answered by the command line, the HTTP API, the OpenAPI document, MCP, the derived graph and the website with nothing else changed
pages.description: One Markdown file under .ai/repo/why/moments/ with schema-valid front matter is the whole

pages.title: A diagnosis of a reader's own symptoms is deterministic counting over the catalogue's metadata, and every recommendation names the moments that produced it
pages.description: majordomus why diagnose and the questionnaire on /why/ answer "what is my operational

pages.title: Every reference a moment makes resolves against the thing it names, and one that does not is an error carrying the nearest candidate
pages.description: A moment names things: the audiences that recognise it, the operational areas it falls

pages.title: Every enforcement the policy declares is reconciled against what actually runs
pages.description: The policy has an enforcement list: things that are supposed to run Majordomus (a pre-commit hook running doctor, a pre-push hook running finish --check). For each entry, doctor proves four things: the executable exists, it is executable, the hook or CI file named in wired_by exists and is executable, and that file actually invokes the command — without discarding its exit code. A declaration that fails any of these is reported as not wired. This is the single most important check in the tool.

pages.title: A misplaced worktree is brought to its canonical path with its modified, staged, unstaged and untracked work intact, verified by a fingerprint taken before and after the move, and a step is reported as moved only when the two are equal
pages.description: majordomus worktree migrate brings a worktree to its canonical path exactly as it is:

pages.title: A task record names the checkout it belongs to, and another checkout is never held to its scope
pages.description: Before the .ai layout, the state directory was tracked by default, so the active task record travelled with the branch. A second worktree checking out that branch read a record it never wrote — and, before this, was held to a scope it never claimed. Its pre-push hook ran finish --check against someone else's task and refused every file outside that task's paths.

pages.title: A branch's worktree path is derived from git identity and the branch name alone — the primary checkout's sibling named with -wt, then the branch with its hierarchy kept — and is the same answer from every directory of every worktree, with nothing registered or configured
pages.description: Given the repository and a branch name there is exactly one path for that branch's

pages.title: Component kit
pages.description: The components every page of this site is composed of: tones, atoms, panels, lists, terminals, tabs, a dashboard and diagrams. Each is shown here rendered from the repository's own data, written once in share/design/kit.css and site/templates/kit/.

pages.title: Architecture
pages.description: One repository, many interfaces: what the layer reads, the model it builds, and every surface derived from it.

pages.title: Command line
pages.description: The command line as the design draws it: the top-level commands read from the generated reference, a recorded run, and examples the reference documents.

pages.title: Cockpit
pages.description: A picture of the Cockpit that majordomus serves at /cockpit: its areas, the layer's counts, decisions per release, the latest changes and what is declared, from the same data.

pages.title: Documentation
pages.description: A documentation page as the design draws it: where the documents are, the first four commands of a supervised repository, and a briefing the generator recorded.

pages.title: Key features
pages.description: Six surfaces around one model: the command line, the HTTP API, OpenAPI and Swagger UI, the Cockpit, MCP and the documentation, each shown with what it really serves.

pages.title: How it works
pages.description: From repository to every surface: discover what the repository declares, build one typed index, derive every interface, present the same facts on each, and what that buys, with measured figures only.

pages.title: Integrations
pages.description: One repository, every interface: what the layer reads, the snapshot it builds, and the command line, HTTP API, Swagger UI, Cockpit, MCP, this site and CI that read it.

pages.title: Landing
pages.description: One repository, many perspectives: what Majordomus discovers, the model it builds, the surfaces it derives, and what a person gets from them.

pages.title: Limitations
pages.description: What Majordomus does not do, stated as plainly as what it does. Rendered from the README.

pages.title: Program map
pages.description: Every module of the CLI, every file it reads and writes, scanned out of the shell sources rather than drawn by hand.

pages.title: The method
pages.description: Doctrine states the invariant. Policy applies it. A rule makes it decidable. Enforcement makes ignoring it impossible. Everything below is this repository's own governance, measured.

pages.title: The full argument
pages.description: The long form behind the homepage: why prompt-driven development does not scale with a repository, what an intent is, the execution model with an honest mark of what exists, why governance has to be executable, and the doctrine.

pages.title: Four axes
pages.description: A profile is not a workflow, a workflow is not an interface, and none of them is a model. Four independent axes, one declaration each, every projection derived.

pages.title: The plan
pages.description: Milestones as executable outcome specifications, issues as execution contracts, and the dependency graph that decides what may be executed next. Every figure is derived from .ai/repo/project.

pages.title: a-change-is-judged-in-minutes — A change is derived in under a second and judged in minutes, and nothing that could have changed is skipped
pages.description: The owner should never wait on the toolchain for a change that touched little. An ordinary derive finishes in under a second. A pull request's required verdict arrives within five minutes. Both are measured and enforced, and the speed comes from not repeating work whose inputs did not move, never from weakening a gate.

pages.title: a-claim-stands-only-on-its-evidence — A claim that something is enforced, tested or delivered stands only on recorded evidence that would have caught it being false
pages.description: The owner wants every rule, guarantee and delivered feature that Majordomus states to be backed by a recorded execution at the revision being shown. For a blocking rule, that execution shows a violation being refused. Every way around a gate (an override, a disabled protection, a proposed decision cited as law) must be visible. Any statement that lacks this evidence reads as not proven on every surface, never as done.

pages.title: a-derivation-computed-once-is-reused — A derivation computed once is reused by every worktree and by CI, and the incremental path becomes the default on evidence
pages.description: A node's outputs are kept under its key outside every work tree, restored only after their digests are verified, bounded in size and age, and shared by the worktrees of one machine and by CI runs. The machine lock covers the moment a worktree's files are written and no longer the computation. The incremental path is the default only after the differential case, the measurements and a rollback case exist, and scripts/derive --full remains.

pages.title: a-derive-answers-within-a-second — An ordinary derive answers in under a second, runs independent nodes in parallel, and a budget gate holds it
pages.description: Derive scenarios (no-op, one input, batch, plus the ten of c255#7) are bench targets under the existing benchmark policy. bench --check refuses a regression. Independent nodes run in bounded parallel against one immutable snapshot, with output identical under any order, and a derive's whole output set is published atomically.

pages.title: a-derive-does-only-the-work-its-inputs-changed — A derive does only the work its inputs changed, and can say why
pages.description: The derivation is a typed graph the executable owns: every producer is a node with declared inputs and outputs, every node has a key computed from the bytes it reads, a read-only plan says for each node whether it would be reused or regenerated and why, and an incremental run regenerates only the nodes whose keys moved. The full derivation stays as the oracle, and a test holds the incremental result byte-identical to it.

pages.title: a-finish-reads-the-criteria-its-work-serves — A finish reads what its work serves
pages.description: The completion policy asks the intent engine what stands for the work a task named, refuses completed while a served criterion is unmet or a guard is violated where the policy says completed means complete, and decides nothing about any intent.

pages.title: a-foreign-repository-is-adopted-and-measured — A repository not built around Majordomus is adopted from the published installer to an accepted finish, and its overhead and friction are recorded without exposing what its basis does not permit
pages.description: A declared protocol says which repository may be adopted, what is recorded and what may be published. At least one admitted foreign repository has a committed T1 trial record from the published installer to an accepted finish, with step times, overhead against declared budgets, footprint classes and every friction tied to an observed event and cited by an issue. The record is published whatever its outcome.

pages.title: a-newcomer-reaches-a-first-verified-intent — A newcomer reaches an intent whose verdict is satisfied, in a repository of their own, using only what the getting-started page shows
pages.description: A criterion can cite the repository's own declared verification; documented commands take a newcomer from a proposal to a satisfied verdict; a scripted stage proves the path with zero undocumented commands; newcomer trials under a registered protocol are published on the T6 row.

pages.title: a-paste-is-decomposed-by-a-skill — A pasted brief is decomposed into the plan by a skill, and never kept verbatim as an intent statement
pages.description: A multi-paragraph, Markdown or over-length paste given to intents.propose on any transport writes nothing and answers invalid_input, naming the skill decompose-a-brief and the digest of the paste's canonical text. The /intent alias, the domain skills, the Cockpit runner and the intent workspace lead to that skill instead of stopping at the refusal. The skill keeps the paste as a campaign whose digest equals the refused one, maps it to the existing plan, drafts only what is new, has the draft critiqued, derives and validates it, and offers its first wave on the mesh without claiming it. A test holds a decomposition of the skill's output shape valid under plan validate and intent validate.

pages.title: a-promoted-record-opens-its-message — Every record promoted from a workspace cites the message it came from, and the UI opens it for the operator who holds it
pages.description: A typed workspace: reference on every record kind, valid in every checkout, resolvable where the store is held, drawn as a link on /ui and as text on the published site.

pages.title: a-prompt-reaches-the-work-it-serves — A captured prompt is matched to the existing intent and recorded on the task that follows it, joined to that task's outcome and evidence, shown with the intent's knowledge on /ui and the Cockpit, read only on its own machine and never published
pages.description: The first vertical slice of the pack, with the privacy gates landed before the first reader of the prompt archive: UserPromptSubmit, then capture with a namespaced idempotency key, a deterministic match against existing intents, the task that records the prompt it followed (the validated state change, through the task lifecycle that owns it), that task's outcome and verify command, the evidence state of the criterion it serves, and the matched intent's knowledge on /ui/idd and the Cockpit, pushed on the live channel.

pages.title: a-provider-carries-the-contract-natively — Each agent client carries the contract through its own extension points, generated once and checked for drift
pages.description: One generated Claude plugin, the edit guard wired and then refusing, a Stop-time owed report, extension provenance in doctor, bounded hooks and MCP listing, Codex hook parity where Codex offers the hook, Zed schema associations.

pages.title: a-registered-corpus-judges-majordomus — The registered corpus judges the same agent with and without Majordomus, by an exact task-level test on accepted results, and the verdict is published with its losses
pages.description: The blocking chain is cut or re-scoped by recorded decisions; the calculator decides the primary outcome by an exact task-level test and reports secondary outcomes without a verdict word; the corpus is run in both arms and the verdict, losses included, is published on the T2 row.

pages.title: a-release-is-proven-end-to-end — Whether a commit may be released, and whether its release arrived, is proved by one read and one case
pages.description: release.readiness answers before a tag from the functions the workflow runs; site-deploy never goes back a commit; one case walks a fresh clone to published evidence; the first record commit after I2717 lands is observed with a green evidence job.

pages.title: a-second-adopter-is-served — A second adopter is served: what a foreign repository met on its first day is fixed in the tool
pages.description: Each finding is fixed generically, with no test of whether the repository is this one: by a declaration, a derivation or a default that an adopter can state. Each fix carries a case that fails without it, its derived files regenerated and its page of the documentation corrected.

pages.title: a-session-leaves-what-it-observed — A session leaves what it observed, and the repository routes it
pages.description: Any worker records an observation in one command; the episode boundary derives a candidate that says what it is about and who should look; reading groups recurrence by subject; an episode with nothing to say records that it found nothing.

pages.title: a-stranger-adopts-it-unaided — A stranger installs Majordomus and is stopped from a false done in ten minutes, and every outside first run teaches the tool
pages.description: The stranger's first ten minutes are one measured gate, init tells an adopter something true about their own repository, and each real outside run is recorded unedited and turned into cases.

pages.title: a-test-fails-when-the-code-is-wrong — The suites that guard critical predicates are shown to fail when those predicates are wrong
pages.description: Declared critical predicates carry a scheduled mutation run with published survivors, and the compatibility analyzer's algebraic invariants are property tests.

pages.title: a-visitor-understands-and-checks-majordomus — A first-time visitor of majordomus.dev understands what Majordomus does and can check every claim it makes
pages.description: The hero links every recorded refusal and the challenge, every problem and step leads to its derived features and evidence, and the published page is probed after deploy.

pages.title: a-workspace-reaches-the-repository — A vendor workspace reads the repository, and proposes to it only where the owner has decided it may
pages.description: Read-only connector first; a proposal path only after an ADR amends ADR 0126.

pages.title: adopter-upgrades — An adopting repository survives a Majordomus upgrade, and what the tool vendors into it is adopter-neutral
pages.description: An adopter can upgrade the tool, or vendor its rules, and be told exactly what to migrate before anything refuses its commits. The migration is a command, not a hand replay. What the tool writes into an adopter (rules, skeleton, scope, candidates) is neutral to this repository and keeps a PR-only trunk clean.

pages.title: an-authorised-node-connects-from-anywhere — An authorised node reaches another across LAN, tailnet or NAT, and says how
pages.description: Two trusted Majordomus nodes cooperate whether they share a LAN, a tailnet or neither, choose a working path by themselves, fall back to a relay when no direct path exists, and every surface shows the path in use and why it was chosen.

pages.title: an-entity-says-how-it-is-known-and-what-it-affects — One entity read names how its record says it is known and when it was observed, identically on every surface, and what a change affects is derived from the same index
pages.description: entity.show answers, on every surface from one declaration, a class read from the record and the observation envelope repository.info already uses. Proof stays a pointer (entity.rs:181-185). A test fails on any divergence between surfaces. entity.affected answers what a path set or a revision range touches, with reasons, from the loaded index.

pages.title: an-inference-names-its-source-and-budget — Every inference a decision rests on names its model and source, stays inside a declared budget, counts independent sources rather than answers, and is never reached from a hook path
pages.description: Each consultation is attributable, and independence is counted by a defined source. Peer critique reviews the evidence. A spent budget decides locally and says so, and consultation usage is economics data with its class. The pack's routing levels are documented as the existing plan outcomes. Hook closures are checked to reach no model. Reuse holds only while its evidence holds, and a poisoned answer stays data.

pages.title: an-outcome-becomes-a-reviewed-plan — A desired outcome becomes a draft plan that is checked before a record is written
pages.description: A desired outcome enters as a typed draft: one document holding a draft intent, its gap, its milestones and the issues with what each serves and depends on. intent draft brief derives what the repository already holds about the outcome; intent draft check judges a draft with the same derivations that judge the tree, as if it were written, and writes nothing; intent draft apply writes a checked draft as records with identities allocated above the high-water mark, and refuses an unchecked one. An advisor may write the draft from the brief; without one a person or a worker writes it, and the check is the same.

pages.title: an-unmet-criterion-is-drafted-into-work — An unmet criterion is drafted into work from the evidence, and the draft is the same on every run
pages.description: `majordomus-cli intent draft gap <intent>` prints a gap record whose conditions are derived from the evidence at the presented commit, with every observation citing the ledger execution or claim it read; `majordomus-cli intent draft plan <intent>` prints one issue draft per criterion no live issue serves, with an identity derived from the intent and the criterion, so a rerun on unchanged inputs prints the same bytes and a criterion already served prints nothing; `majordomus-cli intent next` names the next READY issue that serves an unmet criterion and whose binding would be accepted, with why each issue ranked above it was passed over; and an intent under which tasks keep finishing while no criterion changes state is named stalled. Every draft is a read: nothing is written, and a draft becomes a record only through the worker's own commit.

pages.title: architecture-is-enforced — A violated invariant fails a gate, and green means every required check ran
pages.description: A deliberate architectural violation fails a named gate; a red or cancelled full run is raised the day it happens; a rule is reported proven only when its proof ran; a credential shape never leaves through a response, log or frame; an installed release is proven to serve a repository that is not this one.

pages.title: automation — Repository automation is scripted capabilities over typed Rust, not shell
pages.description: A capability may be scripted (ADR 0069): a Rhai script inside the Rust executable orchestrates typed capabilities through the one registry, reaches every surface by the projections that already exist, runs in a sandbox with a declared and enforced effect ceiling, and shell shrinks by migration under a gate that refuses new shell without a declared exemption.

pages.title: campaigns-are-read-as-provenance — A prompt pack is a campaign the index serves and the plan cites
pages.description: campaign is a kind; records cite campaigns through provenance and campaigns list what cites them; one command adds a pack safely; an execution of a record that cites a campaign pins the revision it ran.

pages.title: capability-graph — One capability graph, two projections, and no second inventory of what this repository can do
pages.description: One typed, deterministic capability graph composes the registries that already own their facts — it does not replace them — and adds typed relations between them that are inferred where a stable convention exists and declared where it does not. Both the running server and the published site render from that one graph: the static projection is the snapshot, the runtime projection is the snapshot plus live state. Navigation, overview, detail, search, the relation view and the coverage matrix are all derived, a dangling relation fails generation rather than rendering as a missing section, and a capability that exists with no documentation, no test or no enforcement is visible as such rather than indistinguishable from one that has them.

pages.title: ci-critical-path — The critical path from a change to its verdict, and from a merge to its verified deploy, runs under a minute warm
pages.description: The change-to-verdict path runs p50 under 40 s and p95 under 60 s warm, and merge-to-verified-deploy p50 under 45 s and p95 under 60 s, measured on GitHub with warm, partial and cold reported apart, every skip of a gate explained by the repository's own impact model, and no required test removed, skipped or made advisory to reach the number.

pages.title: command-and-deployment-criteria-are-judged — A command or deployment criterion is met by a recorded run of exactly that command, or an observation of exactly that deployment, current at the presented revision
pages.description: A deployment criterion is met when a recorded observation of that deployment served a build containing the newest commit that changed the criterion's serving scope, and reads stale, failing or not_run otherwise, never met on an unreachable, malformed, dirty or undecided answer. A command criterion is met when a recorded execution of exactly the argument vector the criterion names exited 0 at a revision the evidence module's one freshness function judges current, with the scope it serves as its inputs; a different command exiting 0 meets nothing. Both carry the same evaluation a test criterion carries. The negative cases are executable, the claim is guaranteed with its test, and intent-lifecycle can be satisfied.

pages.title: cost-per-accepted-outcome — Cost per accepted outcome, only on measured data
pages.description: The cost of an accepted outcome is computed from measured telemetry and the finish contract that accepted it, and is reported only where both exist.

pages.title: Dependency graph
pages.description: Every issue, every dependency, and the execution waves the graph implies — drawn from the canonical edges, never by hand.

pages.title: delivery-economics-are-measured-over-declared-windows — Delivery economics are measured on corpus runs and on real work over a window registered before it opens, and published with their denominators and losses
pages.description: Corpus runs answer the economics.tasks shape; a delivery window registered in the proof plan before it opens is measured at its close into a committed T3 record that the scorecard reads.

pages.title: delivery-flow-is-measured — The way from a pull request to a verified publication is measured per phase, and its bounds are read where work starts
pages.description: Queue time, run time and lead time per phase are derived readings; the backlog bound is policy and the brief says when it is passed; finish names the pull request it hands on; budgets exist per phase without turning runner wall time into a correctness gate.

pages.title: derived-data-integrity — A committed derivation describes something it can be a projection of
pages.description: A committed derived artifact is a projection of inputs the commit owns. Landing an unrelated change on the trunk does not invalidate it, a fixture whose object database has no history can still evaluate it, and the staleness refusal exists on the path merges actually take - so the first thing that says no is a check rather than the published site.

pages.title: development-runtime — The runtime has a development surface
pages.description: A development transition is decided in exactly one place — a `capability!` of kind `command` in the Rust registry — and every surface that offers it is a projection: the CLI, the MCP tool, the HTTP route, the OpenAPI operation and the Cockpit's generated runner form, none of them written by hand. The lifecycle stops being a second program with no surfaces, and the execution history a development surface would show exists somewhere durable.

pages.title: entry-proves-what-it-handed — An episode records the governance and briefing it was handed, and a change is told
pages.description: One governance digest computed by one function, recorded per episode with the briefing digest, compared at the next interaction, carried by handovers, identical across every entry surface; every route around the preflight is a case or a stated limit; task start states how far its base is behind the remote's master.

pages.title: every-session-joins-the-mesh — Every LLM session joins the Majordomus mesh at start, told the mesh as work
pages.description: Any LLM session that starts in a repository with an enabled mesh is on the mesh from its first turn, told who works where on every machine and what waits for it, and a task built outside the mesh is refused by the repository's gates.

pages.title: every-sessions-usage-is-observed — What every AI session consumed is observed from the provider, attributed to the work it served, and never estimated into a fact
pages.description: Token consumption, model and cost of every session of a declared provider (docs/generated/providers.md) on this repository are recorded automatically from what the provider itself reports, and recorded as not observed, with the reason, where the provider reports nothing Majordomus can receive; they are attributed to session, task, issue and intent, shown in /ui with a click-through to the reported event, and used to judge what Majordomus costs and saves, with no estimate shown as a measurement.

pages.title: every-surface-follows-what-changed — Every surface follows what changed in the repository by push, and a surface that does not says so
pages.description: Executions are a monitor source; the Observatory is told over /events; a write by any client reaches the workspace; every live surface states its transport in ADR 0158's words; a follower converges after loss; a kiosk keeps following for days.

pages.title: every-task-states-its-delivery-economics — Every task states its delivery economics: wall time, typed human interventions, CI reruns, spend and acceptance, each from a named record or said not observed
pages.description: One capability, economics.tasks, served by CLI, HTTP and MCP, answers one record per task with every field either a value with its class and record ids or not observed with a reason, never zero for an absence.

pages.title: everything-is-followed-in-one-stream — Everything that happens in the repository is followed in one stream
pages.description: majordomus monitor is the one stream: a typed, cursor-paged feed of signals from every source, with the heartbeat noise folded away and what is addressed to the reader marked and listed first, served by the running server over HTTP, MCP and the command line (with --follow), shown live in the Cockpit, printed at every session start, named by the provider bootstrap, documented and released.

pages.title: execution-telemetry — Execution telemetry, only from providers that expose it honestly
pages.description: Execution telemetry is recorded for providers that report it truthfully, and absence is recorded as absence rather than estimated.

pages.title: external-workspaces — An external workspace is read the way this repository reads anything else, and its content never becomes public by accident
pages.description: A workspace is a declared object of the layer — vendor, identity, what the operator authorised, which browser profile reaches it, which capabilities it is expected to have — and rides the existing kind pipeline onto every surface with no code that special-cases it. Its content is synced by the Node tooling layer that already drives the system browser, lands under `.ai/local/workspaces/`, carries provenance and a support level on every record, and is read back through exactly one capability shaped like `continuity`: served, never published. A sync is incremental from a durable checkpoint, idempotent on replay, fails closed when an observed contract breaks, and never writes a credential anywhere.

pages.title: failure-is-visible — Every failure the runtime can suffer is bounded, tested or stated, and changes the health it reports
pages.description: A client can tell running from ready from mesh-healthy from degraded on one endpoint; no client can hold a worker past a declared deadline; each failure class in a published table names its test or its stated limitation.

pages.title: finished-work-reaches-a-verified-release — Finished work reaches a verified release at the pace it is finished
pages.description: Work does not end when it is written or merged. A finished change flows to master, to a release whose version the public contract decided, and to every surface that publishes it, at the pace work is finished; the flow is measured, its backlog is loud before it is large, a red trunk holds it, and nothing calls a change delivered before its publication is observed.

pages.title: fly-deployment — The container image is a projection of the repository model, and its smoke is its evidence
pages.description: One canonical deployment object under .ai/repo/deployments/ describes the image; a typed Rust model parses and validates it; the Dockerfile, its ignore file, the GHCR image that docker-image.yml and release.yml build, its smoke derived from the route registry, the doctor checks, the documentation and the cockpit view are projections of that object and of the capability registry, each checked for drift. The published image runs as a non-root user, carries no secret and no developer path, answers live and ready in its smoke, and has measured size, cold-start and memory baselines. Re-scoped 2026-10-14 from a Fly.io deployment, which the owner disconnected on 2026-10-12.

pages.title: foundation — A supervisory control layer that is real rather than described
pages.description: A repository carries one policy, a small set of profiles, durable task state, and a set of commands that refuse work which does not meet a declared contract — with every rule dispatched from a registry that proves it reaches the command claiming to run it.

pages.title: I0001 — Audit what actually plans work in this repository
pages.description: Establish an evidence-backed map of how work is currently planned, tracked and remembered here, so that the model that replaces it is built against reality rather than against the README.

pages.title: I0002 — Define the canonical milestone and issue schema
pages.description: Define the smallest repository-native representation of a milestone outcome specification and an issue execution contract, and enforce it the way every other configuration file here is enforced: a key nobody reads is an error.

pages.title: I0003 — Implement the model loader and the status derivation engine
pages.description: Load every canonical file into one normalised model and derive issue and milestone status from recorded facts, in exactly one implementation that every surface calls.

pages.title: I0004 — Implement DAG validation and execution waves
pages.description: Validate the dependency graph and derive topological execution waves, refusing every malformed graph with a named finding rather than a guess.

pages.title: I0005 — Implement the plan command surface
pages.description: Give a worker one command that answers what is ready, why something is blocked, what the graph looks like, and that moves an issue through its lifecycle while refusing illegal transitions.

pages.title: I0006 — Generate the Mermaid DAG from the graph
pages.description: Render the dependency graph as Mermaid from the same edges the engine derives, so that no diagram anywhere is drawn by hand.

pages.title: I0007 — Enforce the canonical model as doctrine
pages.description: Add the project model to the doctrine registry so that doctor reports a broken model and watch reports a model that has drifted, through the same dispatcher every other rule uses.

pages.title: I0008 — Project the model to GitHub milestones and issues
pages.description: Create and update GitHub milestones and issues from the canonical model, report drift instead of overwriting human edits, and keep every network call out of the tool itself.

pages.title: I0009 — Project the model into the website
pages.description: Generate the roadmap, every milestone page, every issue page and the DAG page from the canonical model through the existing site data pipeline.

pages.title: I0010 — Behavioural tests for schema, status, graph and command
pages.description: Prove each rule of the model with a case that fails when the rule is removed, in a disposable repository, the way every other rule here is proven.

pages.title: I0011 — Cross-surface consistency and mutation tests
pages.description: Prove that the CLI, the generated site data and the GitHub projection describe the same graph, and that changing one canonical dependency changes all of them.

pages.title: I0012 — Make CI refuse an invalid model or a stale projection
pages.description: Add the model validation and the projection freshness check to the blocking CI job, with no advisory pass.

pages.title: I0013 — Document the semantics and the dogfooding rule
pages.description: Write the human documentation that explains why the model exists and what its terms mean, and leave every current fact to be generated.

pages.title: I0014 — Make the worker instructions require the model
pages.description: Change the always-loaded provider instructions so that a fresh worker of any provider selects work through the model rather than from conversation or a TODO list.

pages.title: I0015 — Open the first real milestone and execute one issue through it
pages.description: Prove the system on real repository work: open a milestone that exists because the repository needs it, and take one of its issues from READY to DONE entirely through the model.

pages.title: I0101 — Reproduce the escaped blocker as an executable case
pages.description: Write a behavioural case that runs the documented sequence — open a question, hand over, start a new task, finish completed — and records what happens today, so that the gap stops being a sentence in a claim note and becomes something a command demonstrates.

pages.title: I0102 — Decide whether a question transfers or the gate widens
pages.description: Choose between the two alternatives the claim names, record the decision with what was rejected and why, and state which case the chosen behaviour is deliberately wrong in.

pages.title: I0103 — Implement the decision and prove it holds
pages.description: Make the chosen behaviour real in the question store and the blocker gate, and turn the characterisation case from I0101 into a case that fails when the behaviour is removed.

pages.title: I0104 — Move the claim from planned to guaranteed
pages.description: Update docs/CLAIMS.yaml and the claim's detail page so the public surface states what is now true, with the file that implements it and the test that proves it.

pages.title: I0201 — Declare which profile axis may become which runtime limit
pages.description: Add one canonical file beside the profiles that maps a profile axis to the runtime limit it may derive, so that a limit has a single source, an axis nobody can enforce cannot be listed, and a limit no adapter applies is a validation error rather than a comment.

pages.title: I0202 — Resolve a task's effective limits and print them as data
pages.description: Add a read-only command that resolves the limits the active task's profile derives and prints them, in text and as JSON, so that a worker, a wrapper or a test can read the same numbers the enforcement will use.

pages.title: I0203 — Make enforcement opt-in, and prove a repository that declines is unaffected
pages.description: Add one policy key that turns runtime enforcement on, default it to off, and prove with a case that a repository which never sets it behaves exactly as it does today.

pages.title: I0204 — Apply one derived limit for real and prove it changes what happens
pages.description: Implement the first adapter: one limit, derived from the profile through the resolver, applied where a provider can honestly apply it, with a behavioural case that fails if the limit stops being applied.

pages.title: I0205 — Declare the clamp as a doctrine so the mapping and the adapter cannot drift
pages.description: Declare the rule that every applied limit is derived from the declared mapping as a doctrine with its own validator, dispatched from the registry, reaching the command that claims to run it, covered by a case and run in CI.

pages.title: I0206 — Publish the runtime-adapters claim with the test that proves it and the limits it does not cover
pages.description: Move the runtime-adapters row from planned to guaranteed, citing the adapter and the case, and state on its detail page which axes remain advisory and why, so that the guarantee is narrower than the milestone title rather than as wide as it.

pages.title: I0301 — Define the execution record, including what an absence looks like
pages.description: Define the durable shape of a task's execution facts: which fields exist, who reported each one, and how a provider that reported nothing is recorded, so that absence is a value with a reason rather than a missing key or a zero.

pages.title: I0302 — Record telemetry a provider reports, and refuse anything it did not
pages.description: Add the command that attaches measured execution facts to the active task, accepting only values a provider actually reported and refusing any field the caller cannot attribute to a reporter.

pages.title: I0303 — Prove a silent provider produces an explicit absence, never a guess
pages.description: Write the case that runs a whole task under a provider that reports nothing and asserts that the completed record carries an explicit absence with a reason, and that no field anywhere in the surfaces shows an estimated number.

pages.title: I0304 — Read the measurements back through the history surface, under a bound
pages.description: Make recorded execution facts readable through the surface that already answers questions about past tasks, with the same retention bound the other durable stores carry.

pages.title: I0305 — Publish the telemetry claim and record what remains unmeasured
pages.description: Move the telemetry claim to guaranteed for the providers that report honestly, name the implementation and the case, and state in the economics document which providers report nothing and what that costs the analysis.

pages.title: I0401 — Define an accepted outcome, and join it to its measurements without storing the join
pages.description: Define precisely which finishes count as accepted outcomes, and derive the join between an accepted outcome and the execution facts of the work that produced it from records that already exist, storing no third record.

pages.title: I0402 — Report cost only where measurement and acceptance both exist
pages.description: Add the command that reports what accepted outcomes cost, computed only from measured facts, and reports no figure at all where either half is missing, saying which half.

pages.title: I0403 — Make a thin denominator say so rather than average it away
