pages.description: Make every reported figure carry the number of accepted outcomes it rests on, refuse to present a single observation as an average, and prove both with cases.

pages.title: I0404 — Publish the cost-per-outcome claim with its unit defined beside it
pages.description: Move the cost-per-outcome claim to guaranteed, define the unit and the denominator where a reader meets the figure, and state what the number cannot be used to compare.

pages.title: I0501 — Group comparable work from what the records already carry
pages.description: Derive the grouping that makes two pieces of work comparable from facts the records already hold, so that a recommendation compares like with like without anybody inventing a taxonomy of task types.

pages.title: I0502 — Recommend a profile from measured cost, naming the measurements
pages.description: Add the command that recommends a profile for a class of work from measured cost per accepted outcome, and prints the measurements the recommendation was derived from alongside it.

pages.title: I0503 — Return no recommendation where the data is too thin, and say why
pages.description: Make insufficient data produce no recommendation rather than a weak one, with the threshold declared as data and the reason printed, proved by cases on both sides of it.

pages.title: I0504 — Prove the recommendation is advisory and publish it as such
pages.description: Prove with a case that a recommendation never changes the profile a task runs under, and publish the routing claim stating that Majordomus recommends and does not route.

pages.title: I0601 — Let a policy name a shared source it does not copy
pages.description: Let a repository's policy name a shared policy source and resolve it offline from the filesystem, so that one statement of a rule can govern more than one repository without being pasted into each.

pages.title: I0602 — Make a local override explicit and prove it survives an update of the shared source
pages.description: Define how a repository overrides part of a shared policy, require the override to be declared rather than inferred from a value differing, and prove with a case that updating the shared source leaves the override standing.

pages.title: I0603 — Report drift from the shared policy in one command
pages.description: Report, in one command, every way a repository's effective policy differs from the shared source it names, separating declared overrides from undeclared divergence.

pages.title: I0604 — Prove the offline guarantee survives sharing
pages.description: Prove with cases and a doctrine that no path introduced by shared policy reaches a network, and that an unavailable shared source degrades to a named refusal rather than a fetch or a silent local fallback.

pages.title: I0605 — Publish the shared-policy claim and what sharing still cannot do
pages.description: Move the shared-policy claim to guaranteed, cite the implementation and the cases, and state plainly what a shared policy does not provide: no service, no registry, no cross-machine visibility, and no enforcement of a repository that never adopts it.

pages.title: I0701 — Reproduce the misattribution as an executable case
pages.description: Write a behavioural case in which two workers share one checkout — one starts a task, the other records a decision — and assert what happens today, so that the defect stops being an anecdote and becomes something a command demonstrates.

pages.title: I0702 — Decide how a record is attributed, between named alternatives
pages.description: Choose between the alternatives that actually exist — attribute to the session that ran the command, refuse to write when the active task belongs to somebody else, or require the task to be named explicitly — and record the choice with the case each rejected option gets wrong.

pages.title: I0703 — Implement the decision and prove it holds
pages.description: Implement whatever I0702 decided across every command that writes a durable record, and turn the characterisation case into one that asserts the new behaviour.

pages.title: I0704 — Publish what attribution guarantees, and what it still cannot
pages.description: State on the public surface what a record's attribution now means, and state plainly what it does not: that a worker's identity is supplied by the session, not verified, and that nothing here proves who a worker was.

pages.title: I0801 — Narrow the Clean Extraction Boundary and record what was adopted
pages.description: Rewrite the Clean Extraction Boundary in docs/DESIGN.md so that it permits a generic deterministic provenance graph derived from this repository's own artifacts while continuing to exclude everything it excludes today, and record in docs/EXTRACTION_REPORT.md which architectural ideas from the studied prior art were adopted by re-derivation and which were refused, each with its reason.

pages.title: I0802 — Specify the session record before writing one
pages.description: Define the session object in docs/SCHEMAS.md and docs/CONTINUITY.md: what a session is, how it differs from a task and from a handover, the filename grammar of a closed record, the exact field list, which fields are computed from git, and the rule that the reference envelope is derived rather than accumulated.

pages.title: I0803 — Open a session and report its status
pages.description: Implement lib/session.sh with `session start` and `session status`: one active session per worktree in .majordomus/state/session-current.yaml, its identity and git facts computed, a second start refused rather than silently replacing the first, and a status that reports the active session against current git or says plainly that none is open.

pages.title: I0804 — Close a session into an envelope derived from the ledger
pages.description: Implement `session close`: read the active record, derive the episode's references from the ledger between its start and now, write an immutable closed record with computed end-state git facts and an optional authored summary body, remove the active record, and append the close event to the ledger.

pages.title: I0805 — Read sessions back with a divergence label
pages.description: Implement `session list`, `session show <id>` and `session latest`, each resolving with the established rule — same repository, same worktree, same branch, then same branch — and each printing the existing divergence label of the record against current git.

pages.title: I0806 — Make the session rules doctrines, with retention and archiving
pages.description: Finish the session rules: the record and lifecycle rules are declared in share/standard/majordomus/ and dispatched by doctor and watch; what remains is a reference to a record that does not exist, retention over a declared cap, and policy-driven archiving that never deletes and never overwrites.

pages.title: I0807 — Discover knowledge sources from git, not from the filesystem
pages.description: Implement the discovery stage of lib/knowledge.sh: a declared list of source classes, each with a scope of shared or operational, resolved through git ls-files for tracked repository artifacts and through the known state paths for operational records, producing a deterministic ordered list of sources with their content hashes.

pages.title: I0808 — Extract nodes with identities that survive a rebuild
pages.description: Implement the extract and normalise stages in lib/knowledge.awk: one node per canonical object, with an identity derived from its canonical id or its repository path, a kind that is only asserted when a structural fact establishes it, and a title taken from the record or from the document's first heading.

pages.title: I0809 — Record only edges that a file states, each with where it was observed
pages.description: Implement the resolve and graph stages: edges derived from the explicit relationships the canonical files already declare — claim to source, implementation and test; issue to milestone and to its dependencies; evidence to issue; doctrine to validator, claim and test; record to task — each carrying the file and field it was observed in, and none carrying a relationship inferred from prose.

pages.title: I0810 — A content-hash manifest that makes a second sync cheap
pages.description: Implement the manifest: one row per source with its path, content hash, extractor version and the node ids it produced, written beside the generated graph, compared on every sync, and used so that a sync with no source change does no extraction and says so.

pages.title: I0811 — Read-only knowledge lookup with an ordering that can be explained
pages.description: Implement `knowledge search`, `knowledge show` and `knowledge related`: deterministic lookup over the generated index with a documented, tested match order, JSON output that names the field each result matched on, and no write of any kind.

pages.title: I0812 — Validate the graph, and let doctor and watch ask the same validator
pages.description: Implement `knowledge validate` detecting duplicate node ids, dangling explicit references, source paths that no longer exist, hash mismatches, edges with a missing end, edges without provenance and a stale generated index, each with a severity and a reproduce command, and declare the rule in the doctrine registry so doctor and watch dispatch the same validator rather than reimplementing it.

pages.title: I0813 — A closed session becomes a node that points at its episode
pages.description: Extract closed sessions as knowledge nodes whose edges point at the tasks, issues, checkpoints, handovers, decisions and questions they name, so that the graph answers which sessions touched an issue, which decisions affected it, and which handover continued a task — without any session body being copied anywhere.

pages.title: I0814 — Give the worker a bounded slice of knowledge, not the knowledge base
pages.description: Add a knowledge section to `majordomus context`, selected deterministically from what the active task and issue already reference, capped by a profile toggle and an item limit, dropped before any immutable fact when the budget is short, and named under EXCLUDED whenever it is dropped or switched off.

pages.title: I0815 — Say what is now true in the claims, the documentation and the worker instructions
pages.description: Add the behavioural claims this milestone earns to docs/CLAIMS.yaml with real implementation and test paths, document the commands in docs/CLI.md, correct the sentence in docs/CONTINUITY.md that says no index is maintained, write docs/KNOWLEDGE.md, and extend the provider-neutral instruction source so a fresh worker knows the session and knowledge steps of the lifecycle.

pages.title: I0816 — Prove the loop on a real issue, without a transcript
pages.description: Execute the whole lifecycle against a real issue of this repository — session start, plan next, plan show, context, knowledge retrieval, work, checkpoint and decision, evidence, plan done, session close, knowledge sync, watch — and record as evidence what a following session could determine from the records alone.

pages.title: I0817 — Phase timing and work counters behind MJ_TIMING
pages.description: Time every validator and count every YAML flatten and git call when MJ_TIMING is set, and report them ranked at exit.

pages.title: I0818 — The command registry is read in one pass
pages.description: Replace the per-index, per-field awk lookups in mj_cmdreg_public, mj_cmdreg_ids and the event registry with one awk pass each, and read them once per process.

pages.title: I0819 — The project model is loaded with one flatten per file and no per-file lookups
pages.description: Make mj_project_load and mj_project_unknown_keys read each milestone and issue once, checking ids and unknown keys inside awk rather than with a subprocess per file and per key.

pages.title: I0820 — Catalogue, DAG, context and command-surface validators read their inputs once
pages.description: Rewrite the remaining validators that loop mj_yget or mj_git per item so that each reads its inputs with one pass.

pages.title: I0821 — Flattened YAML is cached under .ai/local/cache by content hash
pages.description: Cache the output of mj_yaml_flatten under .ai/local/cache/flat/<sha256>, keyed by the file's content hash and the flattener's own version, so a second command on unchanged files does no parsing.

pages.title: I0822 — Every canonical file is flattened at most once per command
pages.description: Add a case that runs doctor, watch, context and plan validate under MJ_TIMING and asserts the yaml_flatten count never exceeds the number of distinct canonical files a command reads.

pages.title: I0823 — majordomus bench: targets derived from the command registry
pages.description: Add the bench command: every public command in share/commands.yaml is a target, run against a disposable installed repository, with warmup and samples from the policy, reporting min, p50, p90, p95, p99, max, mean and stddev per target and mode.

pages.title: I0824 — Bench persists local runs and keeps a latest projection
pages.description: Write every run to .ai/local/benchmarks/runs/<run-id>.json and .ai/local/benchmarks/latest.json atomically, and append one line per run to history.jsonl.

pages.title: I0825 — An explicit committed baseline
pages.description: Add bench --write-baseline, which refuses a dirty tree unless forced, prints old, new and delta per target, and writes .ai/repo/benchmarks/baseline.json with schema majordomus/benchmark-baseline/v1.

pages.title: I0826 — bench --check refuses a regression by policy
pages.description: Compare a fresh run against the baseline under the policy's benchmark.regression thresholds (relative p50, p95, p99) and exit non-zero naming the command, the metric, both values and the threshold.

pages.title: I0827 — The benchmark policy block
pages.description: Declare benchmark.samples, benchmark.warmup, benchmark.timeout_seconds, benchmark.cache_max_entries, benchmark.regression.p50/p95/p99 and benchmark.budget.doctor_ms in the policy, its allow-list and the skeleton, with no reader-side default.

pages.title: I0828 — doctor under a declared budget, and the hook inherits it
pages.description: Report doctor's own wall time against benchmark.budget.doctor_ms as a finding, advisory, and record the measured value on this repository as the budget's rationale in docs/PERFORMANCE.md.

pages.title: I0829 — Performance doctrine as project rules
pages.description: Add project rules: derived state is computed once per state version, a command's hot path does not re-parse canonical files, every public command is benchmarkable from the registry, cacheability never changes observable behaviour, and performance claims need benchmark evidence.

pages.title: I0830 — docs/PERFORMANCE.md, README, CONTRIBUTING and CLI reference
pages.description: Write the reference: goals, phases and counters, batch reads, the flatten cache, cold versus warm, result and baseline schemas, the policy block, the regression workflow, the contributor workflow and the limitations; add the README section and the bench section of docs/CLI.md.

pages.title: I0831 — Performance claims at their proven status
pages.description: Add claims to docs/CLAIMS.yaml for derived benchmark targets, separated cold and warm distributions, flatten-once, cache equivalence and regression refusal, each naming its case, and regenerate the site data.

pages.title: I0832 — generate-site-data instrumented and its hot spots removed
pages.description: Declare phases per section of the site generator, rank them, and remove the repeated work in the two most expensive sections.

pages.title: I0833 — knowledge nodes and edges read each source once
pages.description: Time the knowledge stages, then remove the per-file subprocesses in discovery and extraction so that nodes and edges take one pass per source.

pages.title: I0834 — The test runner reports per-case time and the suite budget
pages.description: Print each case's wall time in test/run.sh, sort the slowest at the end, and record the suite's total in the benchmark history as a system target.

pages.title: I0835 — CI runs the structural performance checks
pages.description: Add the flatten-once case, the cache-equivalence case and bench --check with the CI profile to validate.yml, with the wall-clock thresholds conservative and the counters exact.

pages.title: I0836 — A synthetic repository generator for scaling cases
pages.description: Add a test helper that builds a repository with N issues, N milestones, N rules and N context documents from the skeleton, and a case that runs doctor and plan validate at three sizes and asserts the yaml_flatten count grows linearly.

pages.title: I0837 — Timing report as JSON
pages.description: Under --json, print the timing report as one JSON object on stderr with phases and counters, so bench can carry a phase breakdown per sample.

pages.title: I0838 — bench compare and the top regressions report
pages.description: Add bench compare <run-a> <run-b> and make the human report rank the largest regressions, the largest improvements and the slowest targets by p95.

pages.title: I0839 — watch inherits every doctor fix and its own budget
pages.description: Confirm watch dispatches the rewritten validators, time it, and declare benchmark.budget.watch_ms next to doctor's.

pages.title: I0840 — context and its subcommands under a second
pages.description: Time context resolve, validate, affected and check-sync, and remove the per-document git and awk calls so each runs under a second on this repository.

pages.title: I0841 — Cache equivalence proved by property-shaped cases
pages.description: For every read-only command in the registry, run it with the cache cold, warm, and disabled, on this repository and on a synthetic one, and assert byte-identical output and exit code; then mutate one file and assert the changed output is served.

pages.title: I0842 — Before and after evidence for every optimisation
pages.description: Record, for each hot spot removed, the phase time before and after and the counter before and after, in the benchmark history and in the commit message, and summarise them in docs/PERFORMANCE.md by pointing at the baseline file.

pages.title: I0843 — The performance workflow is discoverable and complete
pages.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion of M004 has evidence, the README workflow runs as written, the site is regenerated, and the final report is a plan record rather than a conversation.

pages.title: I0901 — The deployment description is a kind of the layer, not a provider file
pages.description: Register `deployment` as a kind of the AI layer — allowed keys, schema, directory contract — and describe this repository's own deployment as one object under .ai/repo/deployments/, so that every later projection reads one file and no provider file is ever authoritative.

pages.title: I0902 — The deployment object becomes typed Rust that refuses nonsense
pages.description: Parse the canonical deployment object into strongly typed Rust — enums and newtypes rather than strings — and validate it so that a deployment that cannot work is refused before anything is built.

pages.title: I0903 — Deployment reads are declared once and projected everywhere
pages.description: Declare the read-only deployment operations as canonical capabilities so that the CLI, the HTTP API, MCP, OpenAPI and the generated documentation all derive from one declaration.

pages.title: I0904 — The listen address is one fact with two projections
pages.description: Make the deployment bind an externally reachable interface on the port the canonical object declares, without changing the loopback default that local use depends on, and without the port existing as a literal in more than one place.

pages.title: I0905 — Liveness and readiness are registered capabilities, not router hacks
pages.description: Expose cheap liveness and readiness endpoints through the capability registry, so that the provider health check, the container test and the smoke suite all point at routes the registry knows about.

pages.title: I0906 — Termination is graceful and proved against the real container
pages.description: Handle SIGTERM and SIGINT so that a Machine that is being stopped, redeployed or autostopped finishes its in-flight responses and exits inside the platform's timeout.

pages.title: I0907 — The running process says what it is, from an allowlist
pages.description: Expose the version, revision, build profile, target and the safe platform facts of a hosted process through the existing metadata surface, with every field explicitly allowlisted.

pages.title: I0908 — A hosted process has no repository, and says so instead of failing
pages.description: Separate the local mode that inspects a developer's repository from the hosted mode that serves a packaged layer, and report the capabilities that are unavailable in hosted mode from capability metadata rather than from a hand-written list.

pages.title: I0909 — The production image is a generated projection of the build specification
pages.description: Generate a multi-stage container build and its ignore file from the deployment object's build specification: a pinned Alpine runtime holding the binary, the runtime assets and nothing else, executed by an unprivileged user.

pages.title: I0910 — The release profile is chosen by measurement, not by folklore
pages.description: Measure the size, startup, memory and latency consequences of the candidate release configurations and select the smallest one that does not regress runtime behaviour materially, recording the decision and the numbers.

pages.title: I0911 — A source change does not rebuild the world, and the context stays small
pages.description: Make the container build reuse dependency layers and caches so that a source-only change does not rebuild every dependency, and keep the build context to the inputs the deployment object declares.

pages.title: I0912 — The image serves the site the canonical pipeline produced
pages.description: Build the served documentation and site assets in the container with the same pipeline local development and the Pages deployment already use, and carry exactly those outputs into the runtime stage.

pages.title: I0913 — The provider configuration is generated, and the cheap profile is declared
pages.description: Generate the Fly configuration from the canonical object — application, region, port, resources, autostart and autostop, health check, concurrency — and declare the cheap cost profile as data that a reader and a check can both see.

pages.title: I0914 — One deployment core, one command, and a dry run that mutates nothing
pages.description: Implement the deployment operations — validate, plan, generate, build, status, deploy, smoke — once in the typed core, expose them through thin adapters, and provide one ergonomic command that performs the whole sequence safely and can be asked to change nothing.

pages.title: I0915 — Deployment joins the diagnostics that already exist
pages.description: Add the deployment checks to the health and doctor architecture the repository already has, so that the answer to whether a deployment can succeed comes from the same diagnostic surface as every other verdict.

pages.title: I0916 — The smoke suite is derived from the route registry, never written twice
pages.description: Generate the deployment smoke tests from the authoritative route registry, extending route metadata only where smoke testing genuinely needs it, and cover the surfaces that a plain status code cannot verify.

pages.title: I0917 — A bad deployment can be undone deterministically
pages.description: Record the deployed image reference before changing production and provide a rollback that rests on what the provider actually supports, so that a failed smoke run has an exit.

pages.title: I0918 — The bootstrap credential is used once and belongs to nothing
pages.description: Define and implement how a deployment credential is discovered for an interactive first deployment, so that it is consumed in one process, never persisted, and leaves no trace of where it came from.

pages.title: I0919 — Nothing secret and nothing local leaves in the image
pages.description: Automate the verification that no credential material and no developer path appears in the image, its metadata, the generated artifacts, the site output, the API documents or the deployment report.

pages.title: I0920 — The image's dependencies are known and its advisories are policy
pages.description: Record what the production image contains, obtain a dependency audit and a vulnerability verdict, and state a severity and fix-availability policy so that the gate is meaningful rather than permanently red.

pages.title: I0921 — Size is measured first and budgeted second
pages.description: Measure the binary, the assets, the image and the build context, declare budgets with headroom over the measured baseline, and gate unexplained growth.

pages.title: I0922 — The memory hypothesis is tested, not asserted
pages.description: Run the production image under the intended memory limit, measure resident memory through a representative request sequence, and let the evidence decide the memory the deployment declares.

pages.title: I0923 — Cold start and endpoint cost are benchmark targets like everything else
pages.description: Measure the cold start of the container and the cost of the cheap endpoints through the benchmark infrastructure the repository already has, and record them as baselines.

pages.title: I0924 — The decision is recorded where architecture decisions are recorded
pages.description: Write the architecture decision record for deploying as a generated projection of canonical deployment metadata, with the alternatives that were genuinely considered and the consequences that follow.

pages.title: I0925 — Every deployment rule is a check that runs
pages.description: State the durable deployment constraints as project rules in the repository's rule system, and give each one an executable check that CI runs.

pages.title: I0926 — The deployment documentation is generated and reachable
pages.description: Produce the deployment documentation from the canonical object and the implementation — architecture, container, resources, workflow, CI, security, cost, troubleshooting and scaling — and make it reachable from the surfaces that are already generated.

pages.title: I0927 — The cockpit shows the deployment from the same data
pages.description: Add a deployment view to the existing cockpit that reads static policy from the canonical object and live facts from the running process, using the projection the cockpit already is.

pages.title: I0928 — A pull request cannot merge a deployment that would not work
pages.description: Extend the existing verification workflow so that a pull request runs the deployment validation, the projection drift check, the production image build, the container smoke run, the resource policy assertions and the security checks.

pages.title: I0929 — Production deploys from CI with a token scoped to one application
pages.description: Deploy production from CI on the repository's existing branch policy, using an application-scoped deploy token rather than an account-wide one, with concurrency that stops two pushes racing the same application.

pages.title: I0930 — The real image runs under the real limits before anything is deployed
pages.description: Build the actual production image and run it under the resource limits of the cheap profile, verifying the process, its user, its port and its routes without fixed ports and without sleeping.

pages.title: I0931 — The application exists, one machine runs it, and the URL answers
pages.description: Create or resolve the production application, deploy the cheap profile without accidental redundancy, verify the machine inventory and the resources against the declared policy, run the route-derived smoke suite against the public URL, and write the deployment report.

pages.title: I0932 — The milestone is accepted on its evidence
pages.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion carries evidence, the measured baselines are documented with the environment they were taken on, the workflow in the documentation runs as written, and the outcome is a plan record rather than a conversation.

pages.title: I1001 — One typed graph composes the registries that already own their facts
pages.description: Extend the executable's graph derivation into a typed, deterministic model that composes the existing authoritative registries — capabilities, commands, routes, MCP exposure, skills, rules, decisions, documents, use cases, benchmarks — without any of them ceasing to be authoritative.

pages.title: I1002 — Relations are typed, inferred from stable identities, and never dangle
pages.description: Give the graph typed relations — implements, documents, exposes, generated from, enforced by, tested by, benchmarked by, depends on, projects to, served at — inferred where a stable convention exists, declared where it does not, and resolved or refused.

pages.title: I1003 — Skills, rules, decisions, documents, use cases and benchmarks enter the graph as themselves
pages.description: Bring the layer's own kinds into the graph through the registries that already index them, so that a rule, a skill, a decision, a document, a use case, a benchmark and a deployment are navigable next to the capabilities they govern.

pages.title: I1004 — Availability and visibility are metadata, not conditions in a template
pages.description: Model where a capability is available — always, only in a static build, only with a running backend, only when authenticated, only at build time — and whether it is public or internal, so that every surface derives its behaviour from that rather than from its own conditionals.

pages.title: I1005 — The graph is a generated artifact with a schema and no unsafe field
pages.description: Serialise the graph as a deterministic generated artifact with a schema, carrying safe metadata only, produced by the generation the repository already runs.

pages.title: I1006 — The runtime reads the graph through the registry, like every other read
pages.description: Expose the graph to the running Cockpit as a declared capability, so that its route, its schema, its documentation and its benchmark coverage all follow from the declaration.

pages.title: I1007 — The site renders the same graph, generated once
pages.description: Produce the static projection of the graph through the existing generation and site pipeline, so that the published site renders the same model the server does without a backend and without a second generator.

pages.title: I1008 — The two projections are proved to be the same model
pages.description: Test that the static and runtime representations of the graph are equal once runtime-only fields are removed, so the published site and the running server cannot become alternate realities.

pages.title: I1009 — Every menu in this repository comes from one derivation
pages.description: Derive the desktop navigation, the mobile navigation, the Cockpit sections, the documentation navigation and the landing links from one projection of the graph, with deterministic grouping and ordering.

pages.title: I1010 — The overview is what exists, counted rather than claimed
pages.description: Generate the Cockpit overview and its summary numbers from the graph, showing a section only when the repository actually holds that kind of thing.

pages.title: I1011 — The coverage matrix reports evidence, and never a green cell without one
pages.description: Generate a matrix showing, for every capability, whether it is documented, tested, enforced, benchmarked and exposed, where each cell resolves to an artifact or a relation rather than to a claim.

pages.title: I1012 — One detail view, assembled from what a node actually has
pages.description: Render a capability's detail page from its populated sections and its resolved relations, with a stable deep link and a repository-relative reference to where the information came from.

pages.title: I1013 — Search over the graph, generated, with nothing to run
pages.description: Provide one search over identities, titles, descriptions, tags, categories, commands, routes and documents, from a generated index that works in the static build with no service behind it.

pages.title: I1014 — The relation view reads the graph and holds no data of its own
pages.description: Render the relation graph interactively from the generated data, with filters, focus, neighbour highlighting and deep links, loaded only where it is used and bounded in cost.

pages.title: I1015 — A surface with no server behind it is not offered as if it had one
pages.description: Make the exposure of backend-only surfaces — the API console, live status, runtime reads — follow from availability metadata, and prove both projections behave correctly.

pages.title: I1016 — The Cockpit works on a phone and before JavaScript runs
pages.description: Make the Cockpit genuinely usable at narrow viewports and keep its core information present in the served HTML, with JavaScript adding filtering, the graph, live state and search rather than being required to read anything.

pages.title: I1017 — Live state is an overlay that degrades to nothing
pages.description: Let the running Cockpit overlay live state — health, peers, runtime metrics, deployment status — over the same graph, through the transport the process already has, degrading cleanly where there is none.

pages.title: I1018 — The surface rules exist as checks, proved by making them fail
pages.description: State the durable constraints of this architecture as project rules with executable checks: derived surfaces stay synchronised, a public capability is discoverable, a behavioural capability carries verification, a developer-facing capability resolves to documentation, and the two projections stay equal.

pages.title: I1019 — One skill runs the whole loop, and is itself in the graph
pages.description: Provide a skill that discovers capabilities, validates the graph, reports what is missing documentation, tests, exposure or enforcement, regenerates the projections and reports drift — registered, documented, tested and visible like any other.

pages.title: I1020 — The graph's health is answered by the doctor that already answers everything else
pages.description: Add the graph's diagnostics to the existing health and doctor surface: the graph builds, identities are unique, relations resolve, projections are synchronised, required documentation and verification are present, and nothing unsafe is exposed.

pages.title: I1021 — A browser proves the interface, at the widths people use
pages.description: Extend the existing browser checking to cover navigation on desktop and mobile, search and filtering, the detail view, graph initialisation, conditional runtime exposure, link integrity and console errors.

pages.title: I1022 — Drift in any derived surface fails the build
pages.description: Extend the generation check to cover every artifact this milestone introduces — the graph, the static projection, the navigation, the indexes, the search data — so a stale committed projection cannot merge.

pages.title: I1023 — Nothing private reaches a published page
pages.description: Scan the published graph, the static site and everything the client receives for credential material, private environment values and machine-absolute paths, and fail on a finding without printing it.

pages.title: I1024 — The interface has a weight, and it is measured
pages.description: Measure the generated data, the served HTML, the initial scripts and styles and the graph's initialisation, and hold them to budgets through the benchmark infrastructure the repository already has.

pages.title: I1025 — The federated model and its two projections are an architecture decision
pages.description: Record the decision to compose the authoritative registries into one typed graph and to render it as two projections, with the alternatives that were real and the consequences that follow.

pages.title: I1026 — The architecture explains itself, from inside itself
pages.description: Document the graph, its sources, its relation model, its two projections and the contributor workflow, and let the interface say how it was generated and from what.

pages.title: I1027 — A synthetic capability proves the architecture instead of describing it
pages.description: Register a synthetic capability at its authoritative source alone, and prove it reaches the graph, the interface, the search, the navigation and the static projection with no other edit — and that omitting its required evidence fails enforcement.

pages.title: I1028 — The inventories this replaces are removed, not left running beside it
pages.description: Find the hand-maintained inventories this architecture replaces — menus, landing cards, route lists, documentation indexes, rule and skill catalogues — and remove them, so that one derivation is the only one.

pages.title: I1029 — The gate refuses what would silently break the interface
pages.description: Put the drift check, the enforcement rules, the parity test, the browser checks and the public-data scan into the existing verification workflow, so that a change leaving any derived surface stale or unsafe cannot merge.

pages.title: I1030 — The milestone is accepted on its evidence
pages.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion carries evidence, the measurements are recorded with their environment, the contributor workflow runs as written, and the remaining gaps are stated.

pages.title: I1031 — A served surface says which checkout it is serving
pages.description: Make every surface a process serves name the repository it is serving — its root and its identity — so that a reader can tell at a glance whether the answers in front of them come from the tree they are working in.

pages.title: I1101 — What this tool leaves behind, established by inspection rather than by memory
pages.description: Establish, from the repository rather than from recollection, every path Majordomus writes, generates or mutates when a project adopts it — where each lands, which subsystem writes it, whether anything records it, and which are canonical, derived or accidental.

pages.title: I1102 — The two namespaces are a typed contract, not a habit
pages.description: Declare the canonical layout of `.ai/` and `.majordomus/` as typed, versioned data — what each namespace holds, what it must never hold, and which lifecycle each directory's contents carry — so that the boundary can be checked rather than remembered.

pages.title: I1103 — Whether a file is authored or derived is a field, not a naming convention
pages.description: Give every machine-processable artifact an explicit provenance and lifecycle — authored, derived, generated, cache or runtime — with its generator, its inputs and whether it is disposable, so that no consumer has to infer from a path what a file is.

pages.title: I1104 — Both namespaces carry their contracts, all the way down
pages.description: Extend the directory-contract discipline that already governs `.ai/` to `.majordomus/`, so every directory of either namespace explains its purpose, its ownership, its lifecycle, the schemas that apply and how its contents are discovered.

pages.title: I1105 — The repository is discovered once, into one model
pages.description: Build the one typed model of a repository — identity, structure, capabilities, the layer's registries, workflows, environments, providers, services and version-control state — discovered once and read by every consumer.

pages.title: I1106 — The registries are views of the model, not separate discoveries
pages.description: Make the typed registries — skills, rules, decisions, workflows, use cases, providers, capabilities — views over the one repository model, so that adding a valid artifact under a discoverable namespace registers it everywhere with no second edit.

pages.title: I1107 — Discovery is deterministic, cached, and its cost is known
pages.description: Make one discovery over one tree produce one answer, cache it by what it was derived from, and measure what it costs — because everything downstream now pays that cost.

pages.title: I1108 — The desired integration is a value, and the plan is a diff
pages.description: Compute what a repository's Majordomus integration should look like as a typed value, diff it against what the repository actually holds, and make the apply the smallest mutation that closes the gap.

pages.title: I1109 — Everything placed outside the two namespaces is recorded, with what it was
pages.description: Record every mutation Majordomus makes outside `.ai/` and `.majordomus/` in a typed ledger: the path, the kind of mutation, the content hash as written, the generator and version that wrote it, and what was there before.

pages.title: I1110 — The second run changes nothing, and a test says so
pages.description: Make reconciliation idempotent: running it against a conforming repository produces no change at all, and prove it with a test rather than with an observation.

pages.title: I1111 — Uninstall gives back exactly what was taken
pages.description: Implement removal that reverses every recorded mutation, refuses anything a person has since edited, and leaves authored knowledge in place unless removal is asked for separately and explicitly.

pages.title: I1112 — What touches the root is two small blocks, and they never change again
pages.description: Reduce every root-level integration to a small, stable, machine-owned bridge: a managed block in the agent document that points at the layer, and — when direnv is wanted — one line that sources the environment integration.

pages.title: I1113 — Entering a directory is local, bounded and silent about the network
pages.description: Keep environment entry — the direnv hook, the banner, the shell integration — local, bounded and free of build and network work, and measure it against a declared budget.

pages.title: I1114 — A provider is an adapter over the model, and adding one is an implementation
pages.description: Make every provider-specific representation a derived adapter over the repository model, so that supporting another provider is one implementation rather than a copy of the instructions in another file.

pages.title: I1115 — Completion comes from the command model, not from a second list
pages.description: Derive shell completion from the same command model the CLI and its documentation already come from, so that a new command is completable without anything being listed.

pages.title: I1116 — This repository's own footprint moves, through the reconciler
pages.description: Migrate what this repository itself scatters — root scripts, provider files, configuration beside configuration, generated state outside the namespaces — into `.ai/` and `.majordomus/`, using the reconciler and its migrations rather than a move script.

pages.title: I1117 — The hand-maintained lists are removed, not left running beside the derivation
pages.description: Find every list that enumerates what discovery already finds — indexes, menus, route tables, provider lists, documentation catalogues — and remove it, so that one derivation is the only one.

pages.title: I1118 — Every invariant of this milestone is a rule with a check that runs
pages.description: Turn the invariants — bounded footprint, no manual registration, disposable derived artifacts, reversible managed mutations, idempotent reconciliation, root files as adapters, zero-registration extension — into project rules, each with an executable check that CI runs and a negative test that proves it fires.

pages.title: I1119 — The budgets are measured, and a regression fails rather than being noticed
pages.description: Measure what this architecture costs — discovery, reconciliation, the environment entry, the generated artifacts — and hold each to a budget derived from its measured baseline.

pages.title: I1120 — A refusal says what to do about it
pages.description: Make every refusal in this subsystem name the source of truth, what was observed, what was expected and the command that repairs it — through the diagnostics framework that already exists.

pages.title: I1121 — Every surface shows the integration from the one model
pages.description: Project the integration state — what is adopted, what is owned, what is generated, what would change — through the CLI, the API and its document, MCP, the Cockpit and the documentation, from the one model and with no parallel definition.

pages.title: I1122 — A foreign repository, adopted, upgraded and given back
pages.description: Prove the contract against a repository that is not this one: adopt it, verify the footprint, run it again, upgrade the tool, edit a bridge by hand, then remove the adoption and compare what is left against what was there before.

pages.title: I1123 — The milestone is accepted on its evidence
pages.description: Close the milestone: every acceptance criterion carries evidence, the measured baselines are recorded with the environment they were taken on, the adoption and removal run as documented on a clean checkout, and the remaining limitations are stated.

pages.title: I1201 — An identity provider is a declarative object, and Google and Facebook are two of them
pages.description: Introduce the identity-provider kind: a JSON Schema, an entry in share/kinds.yaml, the generated allow-list, a directory contract under .ai/repo/identity/providers/, and the first two objects — google and facebook — each stating its issuer, its endpoints or discovery document, the scopes it is asked for, the claim that carries a stable subject, the environment variable names its client id and client secret arrive in, its display name and its order in the sign-in offer.

pages.title: I1202 — One typed provider model reads the objects, and no code names a provider
pages.description: Add apps/majordomus-cli/src/identity with the typed model of a provider object: discovery of every object under .ai/repo/identity/providers/, validation against the schema, resolution of the credential environment variables at use rather than at load, and a deterministic ordering of the sign-in offer. Expose the read as a capability so the provider list reaches the CLI, the API, OpenAPI, MCP and the Cockpit through the registry rather than through five readers.

pages.title: I1203 — One flow serves every provider, and it refuses everything it did not start
pages.description: Implement the authorisation-code flow with PKCE once, over the typed provider model: a start route that issues state and nonce and redirects to the provider's authorisation endpoint, a callback route that refuses a state it did not issue or that has expired, exchanges the code, verifies the issuer, the audience, the expiry and the nonce of the returned identity token, and resolves the stable subject from the claim the object names.

pages.title: I1204 — The session is signed, short, and revocable from the server
pages.description: Issue the session as a signed cookie carrying an opaque identifier, keep the server-side record needed to revoke it, set HttpOnly, SameSite and Secure according to how the surface is served, expire it, and implement sign-out as a server-side revocation rather than a cleared cookie.

pages.title: I1205 — Identity is resolved once, in the router, and every surface reads it from there
pages.description: Resolve the caller once, where the request enters, and carry the result to every surface: the HTTP API, the Cockpit's rendering, the OpenAPI document's security scheme and the MCP surface. No handler parses a cookie, and no surface decides for itself what an absent identity means.

pages.title: I1206 — What an anonymous reader may do is derived from the effect classification, not from a list
pages.description: Derive the exposure decision from the capability registry: a read-only capability stays open to an anonymous reader, anything that mutates requires an identified one, and the decision is stated once in policy over effect classes rather than per route. Project the decision into the OpenAPI security scheme, the Cockpit's disabled controls with their reason, and the generated documentation.

pages.title: I1207 — No credential reaches any output, and hostile provider metadata renders safely
pages.description: Prove the negatives. Place sentinel values in the client-secret and signing-key environment variables and exercise every output this repository produces — API responses, the Cockpit's HTML, the generated site, OpenAPI and its examples, MCP answers, the artifact manifest, the caches, the logs and the doctor report — asserting no sentinel appears anywhere. Separately, give a provider object a display name carrying control characters, ANSI sequences and markup, and assert it renders as text in the terminal, in the HTML and in the JSON.

pages.title: I1208 — Adding a provider is one file, removing one is one deletion, and both are executed rather than described
pages.description: Document how a provider is added and how one is struck, and make the documentation executable: a test that adds a synthetic provider object and asserts it appears in the sign-in offer, in the capability read, in the generated documentation and in the Cockpit with no other edit, and a test that removes one of the two shipped objects and asserts every one of those surfaces loses it.

pages.title: I1301 — A workspace is a declared object of the layer; only its content is local
pages.description: Register `workspace` as a kind — allowed keys, schema, directory contract — and declare the first workspace under .ai/repo/workspaces/, so that the catalogue of what may be synced is the repository's own tracked statement while the synced content stays out of the tracked tree.

pages.title: I1302 — Identity, provenance and support level are typed fields, not prose
pages.description: Define the record model every synced item carries: upstream identity, local identity, content hash, the transport that produced it, the acquisition mode, the support level and the tombstone, as a schema with a version, before any adapter writes a byte.

pages.title: I1303 — The store is bounded, measured and invisible to every published projection
pages.description: Declare the layout of .ai/local/workspaces/, its checkpoint file, its retention cap in policy and the doctor stanza that measures it, and prove with a gate that nothing published ever reaches it.

pages.title: I1304 — The browser transport is the one this repository already drives
pages.description: Implement the authenticated browser transport in the Node tooling layer beside scripts/lib/ui-audit.mjs: Playwright over the system Chrome, an explicitly named profile, observation scoped to the vendor's own origins, and sanitisation before anything is persisted.

pages.title: I1305 — An observed contract has a fingerprint, a compatibility state and a fixture
pages.description: Record what the browser observed as a versioned contract: a fingerprint of the shape, a compatibility state, and a sanitised fixture that CI replays — so that a private surface changing is a diagnosable event rather than a silent wrong answer.

pages.title: I1306 — A sync resumes, repeats itself without harm, and says how fresh it is
pages.description: Implement the sync: incremental from a durable checkpoint, idempotent on replay, bounded in what one run may fetch, and honest about how each change was acquired.

pages.title: I1307 — The ChatGPT shape is mapped from evidence and never becomes the canonical model
pages.description: Map what a ChatGPT Project actually exposes — the project, its conversations, the message graph, content parts, attachment metadata, project instructions — onto the canonical record model, mapping only what an observation supports.

pages.title: I1308 — The executable's share is one capability, shaped like continuity
pages.description: Add one capability to majordomus-cli that reads the store and reports what is declared, what is synced, how fresh each workspace is and at what support level — served, never published, with no site or documentation projection.

pages.title: I1309 — The boundaries this milestone asserts are gates, not sentences
pages.description: Add the gates that make ADR 0025 enforceable: the dependency boundary of majordomus-cli, the credential leak check over the store and the fixtures, the retention cap, and the publication boundary.

pages.title: I1310 — The subsystem is documented where a person looks, and the plan is closed against the repository
pages.description: Write docs/WORKSPACES.md, add the row to the documentation index, and re-audit the repository against this milestone: what was reinvented, what legacy duplication survives, and which of the pack's phases turned out not to apply here.

pages.title: I1401 — The identity of a projected record is what the record carries, not what its title says
pages.description: Make the adapter find a remote record by an identity the record itself carries, so that a person may rename an issue on GitHub without the projection losing it or creating a second one, and make reconciliation provable without a network.

pages.title: I1402 — A finding says which of six states it found, and the state that could hide a person's edit is no longer one of them
pages.description: Derive a typed state for every projected record from two independent questions — has a person rewritten the generated region since it was posted, and has the canonical record moved since — and report the answer instead of collapsing both into one word.

pages.title: I1403 — Backfill the projection once, deliberately, and record what it created
pages.description: Apply the projection so that every canonical record exists on GitHub exactly once, adopt the 19 records that already exist rather than duplicating them, and record the run as evidence.

pages.title: I1404 — The drift check is a gate, so a projection that stops being applied cannot stay silent
pages.description: Run `scripts/github-sync --check` from CI on every change that can move the canonical model or the adapter, and fail the build on drift with the record and the remedy named.

pages.title: I1405 — A pull request names the issue it realises, and the edge is derived rather than remembered
pages.description: Derive the relation between an issue and the pull requests, branches and commits that realised it, from git and from GitHub, and make it traversable in both directions.

pages.title: I1406 — The plan's derivations are capabilities, so every surface reads the readiness the terminal reads
pages.description: Make status, ready, blocked, waves, next and roadmap answerable through the capability registry, so that MCP, HTTP, OpenAPI and the Cockpit read the derived plan rather than only the raw documents.

pages.title: I1407 — One issue travels the whole path and back, as an executable case
pages.description: Prove the milestone with a case that carries one synthetic issue from outcome to accepted completion and then traverses the same chain backwards, offline, against fixtures.

pages.title: I1408 — The documents stop claiming a projection nobody runs
pages.description: Bring the prose in line with what the gates prove, and keep it there by citing the gate rather than the intention.

pages.title: I1409 — Derived data stops hashing inputs it cannot control
pages.description: Make a committed derivation describe something it can be a projection of, and put the staleness refusal where merges actually happen.

pages.title: I1501 — An execution a person starts is an execution the server can see
pages.description: Make `majordomus-cli run` reach the server that serves this repository, so that the execution plane a surface shows and the execution plane a person uses are the same plane — or record the decision that they are not, and stop every surface from implying otherwise.

pages.title: I1502 — A server serving code that no longer exists stops calling itself ready
pages.description: Make a running server's own root and health documents carry the identity of the code it is serving, so that a stale server is detectable by the client reading it rather than only by an outside reader holding a newer executable.

pages.title: I1503 — A closed session is not closed a second time under the same identity
pages.description: Stop the session closer from writing a second record for a session that already has one, so that a session identity names one record and the index does not exclude every claimant of it.

pages.title: I1504 — One development transition is a capability, end to end
pages.description: Declare one development transition — the plan's `done` — as a single `capability!` of kind command in the plan module, with a typed input schema, benchmark cases and a registered ledger event, and point lib/plan.sh at it instead of letting it write the YAML itself.

pages.title: I1505 — A mutating capability leaves a durable event, and the ledger can be read back
pages.description: Give a capability of kind command one way to record what it did: append a ledger event whose name share/events.yaml declares, publish the same change to the execution stream, and add a read capability for the ledger so a surface can show history at all.

pages.title: I1506 — The lifecycle commands become non-interactive capabilities
pages.description: Move task start, checkpoint and finish, session open and close, handover and evidence into the pattern Phase A establishes, each one non-interactive, so that the exposure policy stops withholding them from every machine surface.

pages.title: I1507 — Issues, milestones, sessions and peers reach the Cockpit as projections
pages.description: Give the Cockpit the development areas it has none of — issues, milestones, sessions, peers and the current task — each one rendering what a capability answered and computing nothing of its own.

pages.title: I1508 — The navigation is derived from the dispatcher, not kept beside it
pages.description: Reconcile the Cockpit's area list against the routes the dispatcher actually answers, and derive or check the route table in docs/COCKPIT.md, so that a routed page cannot be invisible.

pages.title: I1509 — A detail page that pages nothing has outgrown the reason it pages nothing
pages.description: Reconcile the two things the Cockpit's largest page is trying to be — complete before any JavaScript loads, and usable by a person — without giving up the first, and bring the page under the test sweep that covers every other one.

pages.title: I1510 — A gap the audit calls planned names a plan object that exists
pages.description: Check docs/COCKPIT_IDE_AUDIT.md's gap matrix against the plan, so that a row whose status is `planned` must name an issue that exists, and a row cannot quietly claim to be scheduled when nothing schedules it.

pages.title: I1511 — The documentation surface answers in a checkout that has not built the site
pages.description: Make /docs/ say what it needs rather than fail, so that a developer entering a fresh worktree does not meet a broken documentation surface as their first impression of the runtime.

pages.title: I1512 — Gate state is something the runtime can answer
pages.description: Give the runtime a capability that answers what the repository's gates are and how the last run of each one went, so that CI status stops being the one observability subject with no reader on any surface.

pages.title: I1516 — The adapter composes a projected body in one place
pages.description: Make the body scripts/github-sync posts to an issue the same text it prints for that issue, by composing it once, so that a body the adapter wrote is a body the adapter recognises as its own.

pages.title: I1520 — A step that runs out of time says so itself
pages.description: Make a CI step that exceeds its time report a failure naming the bound and the elapsed time, instead of being killed by its job and reported by GitHub as a cancellation that every reader in this repository treats as not-a-failure.

pages.title: I1600 — The challenge is one recorded run, and every public surface replays it
pages.description: Record one scenario in which a worker strays outside its scope, claims it is done, hands over, and is refused until the repository's own test passes; render that run on the homepage and on /challenge/; make README.md's first transcript a step of it; and verify the public site serves it after publication.

pages.title: I1800 — The sandboxed engine a scripted capability runs in
pages.description: Embed Rhai in the Rust executable as one engine constructor that every scripted capability runs under: eval disabled, no clock, limits on operations, call depth, expression depth and the sizes of strings, arrays and maps, and cancellation checked on every operation.

pages.title: I1801 — A scripted capability is a kind, discovered and registered, runnable and projected like any capability
pages.description: Make a capability declared in a file of the layer, with a Rhai script as its handler, a capability of the one registry: discovered by the index as a kind, validated with errors naming file and field, runnable through majordomus run, and projected onto the command line, MCP, OpenAPI and the generated reference by the projections that already exist.

pages.title: I1802 — Nothing runs Perl
pages.description: Remove every invocation of Perl from tracked files, including indirect ones such as shasum on macOS, and hold the absence with a gate.

pages.title: I1803 — New shell is refused without a declared exemption, and the migration inventory is tracked
pages.description: Refuse a new shell file under a governed path unless a machine-readable exemption list names it, and track the inventory of existing shell with each unit's disposition.

pages.title: I1804 — The first shell scripts become scripted capabilities over typed Rust
pages.description: Migrate the baseline-ratchet logic copied into ten scripts/ci gates to one typed Rust capability, and the gates that use it to scripted capabilities that orchestrate it.

pages.title: I1900 — An intent is a typed record whose stage and satisfaction are derived
pages.description: Deliver slice 1 of the intent-lifecycle milestone: the intent kind and schema, the read-only capabilities intent.list, intent.record, intent.validate and intent.preflight on every surface, and the intent-check gate.

pages.title: I1901 — An issue names the intent criterion it serves, and coverage is derived
pages.description: Add `serves` to the issue record and derive, in intent_plan::coverage, the coverage of every intent criterion and the origin of every issue, reported by intent validate.

pages.title: I1902 — The gap and the critique of an intent are typed records the plan is held to
pages.description: Add the gap and critique kinds, their schemas, and intent_review::review, so intent validate refuses an incomplete gap and execution on an uncritiqued plan.

pages.title: I1903 — The work realising an intent is joined across episodes, providers and handovers
pages.description: Join every ledger task, closed session record and peer claim to the intents it realises with each link's provenance, record each episode's provider on the ledger, explain an intent's standing, and refuse closed work the evidence contradicts.

pages.title: I1945 — The test-evidence decision and its plan are recorded
pages.description: Record the test-evidence design as ADR 0087 with status proposed, create the milestone test-evidence, and give every slice of the design one issue, so that `majordomus plan` tracks the work and each slice is held to one written definition.

pages.title: I1946 — The verdict words are status words of the design system
pages.description: File the proof-state verdict words as hyphenated status tokens with a declared role, so that every surface renders a verdict through the design system and a verdict added later must get a role before it can render (ADR 0087 decision 13).

pages.title: I1947 — Every feature reaches a test, and every use case has a feature
pages.description: Give every active use case an owning feature, and give the cockpit and deployments features a claim naming their own tests, so that a homepage panel routed to a use case reaches a feature and every feature reaches a test through the subject index (ADR 0087 decision 9).

pages.title: I1948 — Evidence is judged at the presented revision, by one freshness function
pages.description: Write the freshness table, the presented revision, containment and aggregation of ADR 0087 once each (decisions 4, 5, 7 and 8), so that evidence show can judge the checked-out commit by the ledger committed in it and every verdict comes from one derivation.

pages.title: I1949 — CI evidence is recorded clean, and its report is the tracked ledger's verdict
pages.description: Fix PR #577 on its own branch so that the CI evidence job derives its report from the tracked ledger before it records the run's executions, every job that runs tests measures its tree where it ran, and the site publishes current only under ADR 0087's interim rule (decision 1).

pages.title: I1950 — Text a run printed is redacted by one rule set
pages.description: Port the credential table that lib/capture.sh applies into one Rust redactor, held equal to the shell table by one fixture, so that every text the evidence publication carries passes through one rule set (ADR 0087 decision 14).

pages.title: I1951 — Evidence runs are typed, and a recording carries what its run measured
pages.description: Add the run record, the measured provenance, the coverage record and the crate count rule of ADR 0087 decisions 2, 6 and 12, and feed run records to the one monotone rule, so that a recording states the commit and tree its run measured and only what ran.

pages.title: I1952 — Evidence subjects are derived once, in Rust
pages.description: Derive the subject index of ADR 0087 decision 9 from existing declarations, compute a subject's verdict over its members through the one aggregation, and have majordomus generate write it as site/data/registry/evidence-subjects.json.

pages.title: I1953 — Evidence answers by subject, on every surface
pages.description: Add the evidence.subject, evidence.coverage, evidence.runs and evidence.run capabilities, so that the CLI, HTTP and MCP answer by subject from the one authority and read supplementary records only through the monotone rule (ADR 0087 decision 3).

pages.title: I1954 — Every runner reaches the ledger, through the recording branch
pages.description: Wire the trunk's runs to the recording branch of ADR 0080 and every runner to a measured report, so that a merge to master is followed by one recording pull request that changes only the ledger (ADR 0087 decisions 1, 6 and 16).

pages.title: I1955 — The evidence publication is an allow-listed projection
pages.description: Add evidence publish, which reads the ledger committed at the presented commit, the run records and coverage, applies the monotone rule, and writes an allow-listed publication with its publication state, carrying text only through the one redactor (ADR 0087 decisions 3 and 14).

pages.title: I1956 — The Cockpit shows evidence by subject
pages.description: Show every subject's verdict in the Cockpit, read through the subject index from the tracked ledger at the working tree, with a separate, advisory local-run column that can only weaken it (ADR 0087 decision 3).

pages.title: I1957 — Every test line is read, and a local run stays local
pages.description: Read each runner's per-test lines into the execution (case results, detail and dropped lines), add evidence record --run suite and the local run index, and move the web report onto the same typed adapters.

pages.title: I1958 — Evidence has one route per subject, and every panel is joined to its subject
pages.description: Generate one evidence route per subject from site/data/registry/evidence-subjects.json, as sections of the one evidence template, and join every homepage panel to its subject by its route, failing generation for a subject the index does not have (ADR 0087 decision 9).

pages.title: I1959 — The evidence publication is typed, bound to its build, and kept on gh-pages
pages.description: Make scripts/pages call evidence publish in the build's checkout, refuse a dataset that is not bound to the build, and keep each deployed revision's evidence on gh-pages under evidence/<sha>/, retiring the interim publication of PR #577 (ADR 0087 decision 3).

pages.title: I1960 — Every widget names its proof
pages.description: Render one evidence badge on every widget that states behaviour, linking to its subject's route with the verdict at the published commit, and compute the delivery report's required_tests_current and test_evidence_published dimensions as ADR 0087 decision 3 says.

pages.title: I1961 — A deploy verifies the evidence routes it publishes
pages.description: Make pages-check probe the evidence routes a deploy published, deriving the probes from the published evidence-subjects.json rather than from a hand-written list.

pages.title: I1962 — The evidence gates read subject findings and widgets
pages.description: Make subject findings refusing, rewriting the evidence baseline in the same change, and make the evidence validator read every rendered widget, so that a widget without a subject or a count hard-coded into a template fails CI (ADR 0087 decision 10).

pages.title: I1963 — Evidence is tested end to end
pages.description: Prove across every surface that no surface is greener than the ledger, that the badge works in a browser, that tampered evidence is refused, and that coverage is shown with its commit.

pages.title: I1964 — The evidence reference is documented and held to the tree
pages.description: Rewrite docs/EVIDENCE.md as the reference of the finished model, with the pipeline drawn in mermaid and a case named on every row of the matrix, and hold it to the tree with a case; cite ADR 0068, 0080 and 0087 structurally once they have landed.

pages.title: I1965 — The entry preflight reads the one verdict
pages.description: Move the entry preflight's verification.tests check onto the freshness function and its verification.enforcement check onto the rules corpus verdict, ending the one known exception ADR 0087 names in decisions 3 and 4. It depends on PR #578 as well as on I1948, because the preflight exists only on #578.

pages.title: I1966 — The composed graph is whole or its generation refuses
pages.description: Stop docs/generated/graph.json from silently dropping nodes and edges at the MAX_NODES cap. Either the cap is raised or removed under a measured size budget, or generation refuses a truncated graph and names the count and the cap. The committed graph must never be a prefix of the repository that still passes as whole.

pages.title: I1967 — A reporter that sets a flag is a reporter
pages.description: Make the pipeline-count guard discover a reporter that records a failure by setting a flag, not only one that increments a counter, so a call to it inside a construct that discards the flag is refused like a lost count.

pages.title: I1980 — A layer names the tool version it was written for, and doctor tells version skew from defects
pages.description: Record in .ai/manifest.yaml the tool (or layer) version a layer was last migrated with. doctor then classifies findings that a newer tool raises against an older layer as version skew, naming the migration that clears them, instead of failing as defects. A layer written by a newer tool is refused by an older one with a message, not with a cascade.

pages.title: I1981 — A command's effect class is declared per subcommand and flag, and live scenarios judge the whole argv
pages.description: Declare read-only or state-mutating per subcommand and per flag in share/commands.yaml where a command has both, and make live use-case validation and runs judge the full argument vector against that declaration.

pages.title: I1982 — Plan stamps written before seals existed are re-sealed by a command that keeps their original times
pages.description: Provide a migration step (for example `plan seal --backfill`) that seals the stamps an older tool wrote, keeping each stamp's original time and recording who sealed it and when. Make the seal cutoff a per-repository value rather than one global constant.

pages.title: I1983 — Upgrading the vendored rules reports or applies the policy and source keys those rules depend on
pages.description: When `rules vendor update` brings in rules that read policy keys or knowledge source classes the adopter's layer lacks, report each missing key with its skeleton default, or apply it, and have doctor name the gap.

pages.title: I1984 — Knowledge candidates never leave untracked files on a trunk that only pull requests change
pages.description: Decide and implement where knowledge candidates are written so that deriving them at an episode boundary on the trunk never leaves the trunk's working tree dirty.

pages.title: I1985 — A knowledge candidate relates to its own decision and commit, not to the whole episode
pages.description: Derive each candidate's relates_to and derived_from from the decision or event it records, deduplicate against facts the ledger already states, and skip decisions a later decision superseded.

pages.title: I1986 — The vendored rule package says nothing that is only true of this repository
pages.description: Rewrite the baseline rules that describe Majordomus's own history as rules about any adopter. Mark their x-majordomus.tests as upstream proofs so an adopter is not pointed at test/cases it does not have, and give the package manifest a real source revision.

pages.title: I1987 — A knowledge record's file provenance survives the file's deletion
pages.description: Let derived_from name a file at a commit (`file:<path>@<commit>`), or resolve `file:` at the record's own commit, so that deleting a cited file does not break knowledge check.

pages.title: I1988 — A use case's setup scripts live where the adopter declares, and its scenarios may run the adopter's own commands
pages.description: Declare the use-case setup directory in the manifest instead of hard-coding this repository's test/fixtures/commands/setup, and allow a scenario step to run commands the adopter declares, judged by the same effect classes as I1981.

pages.title: I1989 — init seeds a scope for the stack it finds, not for this repository's
pages.description: Make the scope skeleton neutral, or detected from the adopter's files, rather than seeded with Elixir and Rust paths and a size cap that excludes committed build output.

pages.title: I1990 — The pre-push check judges the refs being pushed, or says why the checkout's task binds them
pages.description: Decide whether `finish --check` in the pre-push hook should read the refs git passes on stdin and judge only those carrying the active task's branch, and implement or document the decision.

pages.title: I1991 — A comment-only edit of the policy regenerates no bootstrap
pages.description: Derive the policy fingerprint stamped into generated bootstraps from the parsed policy rather than its bytes, so that editing a comment does not rewrite AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md.

pages.title: I1992 — A rebuild that fails consumes no change: the next request retries it
pages.description: When a long-lived server's rebuild of its repository picture fails, keep the change it noticed unconsumed, so that a later request retries the load (bounded, not on every request) instead of serving the previous generation until git happens to move again.

pages.title: I1995 — Work a session left uncommitted in a worktree is named, not found by luck
pages.description: Make doctor and the worktree status name a linked worktree whose index or working tree holds changes no commit carries and no live session holds, with how many files and how old, so that finished work on one disk is seen before the disk is.

pages.title: I1996 — doctor does not fail an adopter on a check written for this repository
pages.description: Stop `majordomus doctor` from failing an adopter's repository on the reasoning design's own coupling rules, and stop its reproduce hints from naming paths only this repository has.

pages.title: I1997 — The peer board can be read from the command line
pages.description: Project the peers capability onto the command line, so that a worker with no MCP tools can still ask who else is working in this repository and on which paths.

pages.title: I1998 — A health command in an unsupervised repository does not exit 0
pages.description: Make `majordomus doctor`, `session list` and the other read-only commands exit with the missing-artifact code when the repository has no .ai/manifest.yaml, so a caller can tell a healthy repository from one the tool is not installed in.

pages.title: I1999 — A tracked file a hook regenerates does not refuse a task that never touched it
pages.description: Let a repository declare the tracked paths its own tooling rewrites, have `check` and `finish` judge them as the machine's and not the worker's, and make the scope finding and the note finding say what settles them before `finish` refuses.

pages.title: I2000 — What a piece of work serves is one derivation, with a revision
pages.description: Add Intents::binding over the preflight: the work named by an issue, an intent, paths or a declared exemption resolves to a standing (bound, maintenance, exempt, refused), the intents and criteria served, and two pins of what was resolved — plan_revision, a hash of each served intent's statement, invariants and criteria, the links that reach it and its critique, and evidence_standing, a hash of the served criteria's evidence states; answer it as the read-only capability intents.binding on the command line, HTTP and MCP.

pages.title: I2001 — start asks what the task serves and refuses a refused binding where the policy requires it
pages.description: Give start the flags --issue, --intent, --exempt and --because; ask intents.binding through the built executable; under policy intent.binding: required refuse a refused or unreadable binding, under advisory report it, and when the key is absent change nothing. Record what was named and the revision in the task record and the task.started ledger event.

pages.title: I2002 — The context of a bound task says what the intent asks of this work
pages.description: Add an INTENT section to majordomus context for a task that named an issue or an intent: statement, invariants, the criteria served with the state of their evidence, the critique's open blocking findings and the gap's conditions, each read from intents.binding and bounded by the context budget.

pages.title: I2003 — A handover pins the binding it was written under, and resolving it reports drift
pages.description: Write issue, intent and binding_revision into a handover's front matter when the task is bound, and have handover --resolve ask intents.binding again and say whether the plan revision or the evidence standing changed since.

pages.title: I2004 — plan start refuses an issue whose binding is refused, in both engines
pages.description: Where the policy requires binding, have the start transition ask the binding of the issue before it stamps: plan::check in the Rust engine through the intent engine, and the shell engine through the built executable, with the same refusal text; where the policy does not require it, neither engine changes.
