pages.title: I2054 — A tag does not turn every other pull request red until its record lands
pages.description: From the moment a release tag is pushed until its release record is on master, a pull request that changes nothing about releases keeps a green structure job. Either scripts/ci/release-check holds a published tag without a record only when no open pull request proposes that record, or the record is proposed before the tag is pushed; the choice is the implementer's and is written down with what it costs.

pages.title: I2059 — A rebuild never replaces the executable a live lease names
pages.description: Stop an entry point from rebuilding the executable in place under a running shared server, and make the server that follows a superseded one bind the address the old one was serving, or say that it did not.

pages.title: I2068 — A verdict that depends on the runner says so, and one cold sample is not a regression
pages.description: Make the timing verdicts this repository's CI and its adopters' hooks hand down distinguish a slower change from a slower machine: a benchmark regression is judged from more than one cold sample and against the load it was measured under, and a case whose cost sits within a few percent of its kill bound is reported as a budget risk before it fails a suite whose every case passed.

pages.title: I2073 — A worker records an observation in one command
pages.description: Register observation.recorded in share/events.yaml (emitted_by knowledge; requires task_id, kind, subject, statement, evidence) and add `knowledge observe --kind <friction|workaround|defect|drift|repetition> --subject <ref> [--evidence <ref>]... <statement>` to lib/knowledge.sh, writing one ledger line, refusing malformed input without writing, inside or outside a task, and only inside an open episode; write ADR 0118.

pages.title: I2074 — An observation becomes a candidate that says what it is about, and reading groups recurrence
pages.description: Add the observation.recorded row to mj_knowledge_evidence with ADR 0091's per-episode id over kind, subject and statement; add optional about and route to knowledge/v1 (proto, generate); have knowledge candidates and the Rust knowledge_base.candidates group by about, listing each record and its episodes.

pages.title: I2075 — A candidate is routed by what it is about
pages.description: Derive route for every observation candidate from its subject, in ADR 0118's order: command:, capability:, rule:majordomus.*, the vendored rules directory, or the tool's share/ when inside the repository -> platform; another rule: or gate: -> enforcement; a path the scope declares generated or .gitattributes marks merge=derived -> generator; docs/ -> documentation; anything else -> project.

pages.title: I2114 — A task's scope admits what its derive writes
pages.description: Stop the pre-push scope check from refusing a branch for the projections its own derive wrote, and give a task one supported command to widen its scope.

pages.title: I2115 — The slowest case costs a fraction of its budget, and its budget is never raised to follow runner load again
pages.description: Cut case 95_executable_reference to a fraction of its cost instead of raising the slowest-case budget again. Measure first where its time goes: it runs scripts/generate-site-data eight times over a full fixture copied by fixture_repo. Then reduce what each run regenerates or how many runs the case needs, keeping every assertion it makes, so the case proves the same things in a fraction of the time.

pages.title: I2123 — A caller beyond loopback reads, and changes nothing it cannot authenticate
pages.description: Refuse every capability that changes something to a request from an address that is not loopback, unless the capability's input is a signed message its handler verifies, on the HTTP routes and on MCP over HTTP alike.

pages.title: I2124 — An event reloaded from disk meets the trust policy in force, and no stamp outruns the clock
pages.description: Apply the same trust predicate to events reloaded from the journal file as to events arriving over a link, and refuse an event whose Lamport stamp is further ahead of the receiver's clock than a declared bound.

pages.title: I2126 — A server busy with tool calls is never taken over as if it were dead
pages.description: Make the lease probe reach a server whose HTTP workers are all running tool calls, and make it prove it reached the leaseholder, so that a client deciding whether the owner is alive is never answered by a full worker pool or by another process.

pages.title: I2127 — A server that lost its lease hands its sessions on and ends
pages.description: Make a server that lost or was superseded in its lease answer its existing MCP sessions with session-not-found after a bounded in-flight grace, so their bridges re-attach to the current leaseholder and the old process reaches its own end.

pages.title: I2128 — A lease is removed only by the process that holds it, and serve stop stops the server in order
pages.description: Make every removal and every rewrite of the lease file conditional on the actor still holding it, and turn the SIGTERM that serve stop sends into the ordered stop the server already has.

pages.title: I2129 — The lease timings the policy declares are the ones the mcp and serve elections use
pages.description: Load the policy before mcp and serve elect, make every reader of a lease timing read the declared value, and declare the idle timeout beside the other server timings.

pages.title: I2131 — A server in use through the Cockpit or HTTP is not stopped as idle, and a checkout keeps one address
pages.description: Count every surface's use toward the idle timeout, and bind a port derived from the checkout's identity before falling back to a random one.

pages.title: I2132 — A hello names the runtime it is meant for, and no other runtime accepts it
pages.description: Bind each link hello to its intended recipient inside the signed bytes, refuse a hello addressed elsewhere, and make the documented check order the one the code runs.

pages.title: I2133 — Every mesh input and answer has a bound, and a refused registration learns nothing
pages.description: Bound the discovery channel, every reply a runtime reads and the candidates it accepts; answer a refused registration with its refusal alone; and give every link retry a floor and jitter.

pages.title: I2134 — A key removed from the trust list loses its links without a restart, and a node key can be rotated
pages.description: Re-read the trust declaration while the runtime runs, drop the links and admission of a de-listed key, offer a key rotation that peers can follow, and create the node key file private from its first byte.

pages.title: I2135 — The trust root is read from the default branch, not from whatever the checkout holds
pages.description: Let a working tree narrow the mesh's trust and never widen it: obey the working tree's declaration with every widening of the trunk's committed copy removed, report each ignored line, and refuse a committed declaration that trusts on first use.

pages.title: I2137 — An accepted mesh event is on disk before it counts, and a damaged journal line is reported, never fused or dropped silently
pages.description: Make journal appends and compaction rewrites durable and failure-reporting, and make reload survive a torn tail without losing or fusing a complete event.

pages.title: I2139 — A sync message stays under the link bound whatever the marks weigh
pages.description: Budget each sync message as the link bound minus its marks, and stop sending tombstone marks the peer does not hold.

pages.title: I2140 — Paging mesh.events returns every event exactly once
pages.description: Page mesh.events by the causal key and return the last key returned as the next cursor.

pages.title: I2145 — A tool call that may have run is never sent a second time
pages.description: Make the stdio bridge resend a message only when the server provably did not receive or run it, and report every other failure as the error it is, so no tool call executes twice.

pages.title: I2147 — The MCP transports bound what they read and follow the Streamable HTTP rules they claim
pages.description: Apply one declared message bound to stdin lines, request bodies and every response the bridge reads, validate MCP-Protocol-Version, issue unpredictable session ids, and never reap a session whose request is still running.

pages.title: I2151 — A page served beside the write routes runs only script it shipped, and a rebinding host reads nothing
pages.description: Give /swagger the Cockpit's security headers and integrity-checked scripts, refuse a GET whose Host names another server, and escape script-breaking sequences where the site embeds JSON.

pages.title: I2156 — A slow or silent HTTP client cannot hold a server worker
pages.description: Put a declared deadline on reading each request's head and body, close and count a connection that misses it, and keep handler time off the workers the probe needs.

pages.title: I2157 — Ready means ready: a lost lease, a degraded layer or a failing mesh is not reported ready
pages.description: Fold lease loss and a degraded index into readiness with a named reason, add a mesh check to health.report, and make majordomus doctor report the runtime or say that it does not.

pages.title: I2161 — No answer, log line or mesh frame carries a credential the redactor knows
pages.description: Pass every response reason, logged request field and replicated mesh text through the one redactor, bound the fields a mesh event may carry, and make the redaction module's documentation name the callers that exist.

pages.title: I2162 — A released archive, installed, serves a foreign repository over the shared server in CI
pages.description: Make the install check and the release smoke start a shared server from the installed binary in a fresh repository that is not this one, and stop the smoke from swallowing the launcher's failure.

pages.title: I2163 — A client never attaches to a server of another version without saying so, and a newer client replaces an older server
pages.description: Make the election compare versions through the one standing verdict: a newer client takes over in an ordered hand-off, an older client attaches and says it is older.

pages.title: I2165 — A released archive carries a provenance attestation the installer can check
pages.description: Attest each release archive in the publish job, verify the attestation in install.sh when the tooling is present, and state in docs/DISTRIBUTION.md what each install path verifies.

pages.title: I2282 — The record pull request's dispatched verdict does not satisfy branch protection
pages.description: Make the record pull request a release proposes mergeable without a person closing and reopening it, or stop docs/DISTRIBUTION.md and case 996 from saying that it is.

pages.title: I2288 — A task is on the mesh while it works
pages.description: majordomus start claims the task's scope on the checkout's running server as an advisory claim of the mesh session task-<id>, with the task's title as intent and its issue, and keeps the key on the task record; finish closes that session.

pages.title: I2289 — A task built off the mesh is refused
pages.description: Rule majordomus.task-on-the-mesh, dispatched by check and finish: on a repository whose tracked mesh declaration is enabled, a completed finish of a task whose scope was never claimed on the mesh is refused and recorded; finish claims the scope again before it judges; partial and the other outcomes are not refused.

pages.title: I2296 — The executor reopens a record pull request no run was started for
pages.description: Let `majordomus prs drain` close and reopen a release's record pull request itself when the workflow's token opened it and it therefore has no check of its own, so the record lands one validate cycle after publication without a person noticing.

pages.title: I2298 — A pull request stacked on one that landed merges on the verdict its head already has
pages.description: Give the integration queue a typed relation for a head that lacks master's commits and whose merge writes its own tree, so that the links of a stacked train land one after another in a single run of the required check, and record the train as a decision.

pages.title: I2300 — A head is judged against what it changes, not against GitHub's live state
pages.description: Make scripts/ci/github-check report as pending, and not refuse, the drift an apply would write on the records a head changed since its merge base, and on the trunk on the records that changed in a landing younger than a declared window; refuse the same drift on every other record, and on the trunk past the window with the remedy named.

pages.title: I2301 — Whether the work is done is answered by measurement: the done invariant asks about debt, what was left behind and the backlog
pages.description: Add to the done invariant the three questions a person asks when a session ends that it does not yet ask — did the recorded debt grow, is a branch or worktree created since the task started still there, is a pull request opened since still open — each read from the record that holds the fact, and state as a project rule that a closing question is answered by that reading and never by a worker's recollection.

pages.title: I2303 — A release publishes its metadata to the site before its record lands, and the site never goes back a release
pages.description: Make majordomus.dev serve a release's releases/latest.json and releases/<tag>.json from the release run itself, minutes after its archives are published, instead of after its record's pull request has passed its ci, without the site ever going back a release.

pages.title: I2348 — A gate's result is reused only for the exact inputs it judged, and a skipped gate carries the proof that nothing it reads changed
pages.description: Join the path-class gates and their implications with the affected closure, a cache key, a proof for each skipped gate, integrity of a remote against a local cache, concurrency and precise invalidation, so that a stale verification is never reused.

pages.title: I2350 — One gate model names what a local check, a pull request, an integration and a release must run, and no second inventory exists
pages.description: Model the fast local, the pull-request impacted, the complete integration and the release-level checks as selections of the existing gate dispatch and claim and evidence system, with a conservative, reproducible affected-test selection that falls back to the full plan when impact cannot be proved, and diagnostics that name the cause, the reproducing command and the owner.

pages.title: I2396 — The CI critical path of 2026-10-10 is measured, recorded, and explained before anything is changed
pages.description: Record what a pull request's verdict costs today, from the forge's own runs, so that every change of the V4 delivery work is compared with a measurement rather than with a belief.

pages.title: I2398 — A derive offloaded to another machine waits its turn in a declared queue
pages.description: Make the derive offload a capability of the executable: the hosts and their limits declared once under .ai/repo, the host chosen by free disk and queue length, a FIFO queue on the host in which a dead waiter's ticket blocks nobody, a build directory of each derive's own, and the bundle-in/bundle-back round trip with its refusals, tested without a network and documented.

pages.title: I2399 — Every session briefs itself on an interval, without being asked
pages.description: Give every worker of a supervised repository one short, typed brief of what surrounds it (its own episode and task, the peers of every board, the mesh, the integration queue and the derive queue), projected to the command line, HTTP, MCP and the Cockpit, and have a Claude Code provider mod the policy switches keep that brief in front of the session on its own: as the status line, injected on an interval, and with the session told at its start how to keep itself awake.

pages.title: I2400 — A signal model and a fold join every source the server already records
pages.description: Add src/monitor: a Signal (cursor, at, source, kind, severity, actor, subject, summary, for_you), one reader per source (mesh journal, board, executor trail, executions) and the fold that drops unchanged session re-projections.

pages.title: I2401 — monitor is one read capability with three projections
pages.description: Declare capability monitor (MCP majordomus_monitor, GET /api/v1/monitor, CLI majordomus monitor) with OpenAPI-unique names and a benchmark case, and generate its projections.

pages.title: I2402 — majordomus monitor follows the stream from a terminal and a script
pages.description: Add majordomus monitor with --follow, --for, --sources, --since, --count, --until and --format text|json|ndjson, rendering one line per signal with its source tag.

pages.title: I2403 — Pull requests, checks and deploys reach the stream when GitHub is reachable
pages.description: Add a GitHub source (pull requests opened, merged and closed, required check verdicts, deploy and release workflow outcomes) through the existing pull-request reader, cached and time-bounded.

pages.title: I2404 — The Cockpit shows the stream live
pages.description: Add /cockpit/monitor: the live feed polling the HTTP projection with its cursor, source filters, for-you pinned, the suppressed count, linked from the home and mesh pages.

pages.title: I2405 — Every session is told what happened since its last look
pages.description: Print a bounded monitor summary in the session-start briefing and majordomus context, and name majordomus monitor --follow in the provider bootstrap templates.

pages.title: I2406 — The stream is documented where a reader looks
pages.description: Write docs/MONITOR.md, a README section, cross-links from docs/MESH.md and docs/MCP.md, the site docs page through the generated copy, and a blog article written from what landed.

pages.title: I2407 — The monitor is released and deployed
pages.description: Bump the minor version on the branch, record the CHANGELOG entry, land through the lane, let the release pipeline cut it and verify majordomus.dev serves it.

pages.title: I2410 — A trusted machine on the tailnet is found through Tailscale, with no address written by hand
pages.description: Add a Tailscale discovery provider beside multicast, broadcast and rendezvous: it reads the local tailnet's peers and offers each one's tailnet address on the declared port as a candidate, which the link then admits or refuses under the trust list.

pages.title: I2411 — A server whose mesh is enabled is reachable on the tailnet and the LAN, and only by a trusted peer
pages.description: When the mesh is enabled, the shared server listens and advertises on the machine's tailnet and LAN addresses as well as loopback, so a trusted peer can dial it, while a request from a non-loopback address stays limited to what runtime-trust allows.

pages.title: I2412 — `majordomus init` declares the mesh and enrols this machine's key, so a fresh repository cooperates
pages.description: A fresh `majordomus init` writes a mesh declaration (multicast and Tailscale discovery on, deny_unknown trust) and an enrolment command adds this machine's node key to it, so a repository becomes a mesh by init and one enrolment per machine.

pages.title: I2413 — A linked worktree cooperates through its repository's running server, and a start that cannot ensure one says why
pages.description: Mesh commands in a linked worktree with no server of its own use a running server of the same repository (the primary's, or the first ready one), and the session-start hook reports, never silently skips, when it cannot ensure a server.

pages.title: I2414 — mesh.state and mesh.peers answer a filtered summary that fits one tool answer
pages.description: Give mesh.state and mesh.peers inputs that narrow and summarise: a kind (sessions, claims, handovers, reviews), open-only, mine-only, a scope or PR substring and a limit, with a counts-only summary by default.

pages.title: I2415 — A mesh review request carries a body, can be withdrawn, and expires
pages.description: Give review requests a body beside the 256-byte subject, a withdraw event its requester may write, an optional expiry, and a result note the requester may attach to its own request, so a request ends instead of staying open forever.

pages.title: I2416 — The ci verdict asks every selected gate for a receipt, and a gate whose step never ran is red
pages.description: Make scripts/ci/verdict green only when every gate the plan selected left a receipt from the step that ran it, every receipt `success`: a job's success is not a gate's, because a job carries many gates and a step its condition skipped does not fail the job. Cancelled, skipped, missing and absent never pass, and each has a fixture.

pages.title: I2417 — The landing page is a click-through story: an editorial hero and an evidence chain a visitor steps through
pages.description: Give the homepage the editorial typography and the click-through interactivity of the prismatic case reports: a serif display hero and section heads, and an interactive evidence chain in the proof section — what the repository declares, what the registry generates, the interfaces it reaches, the rules a machine decides, the guaranteed claims, the executable use cases and what a recorded run supports — in which every node is a button that opens its figure, its sentence and its source, and every edge is solid where a machine holds the link and dashed where it is declared and awaits evidence.

pages.title: I2460 — The overview asks its sources at once, so it costs its slowest source and not their sum
pages.description: dashboard.overview executes its distinct sources concurrently through the shared executor, so the Cockpit's first page and every screen built on the overview paint in the time of the slowest source rather than the sum of all seven.

pages.title: I2461 — majordomus ui is served at /ui as its own product, with screens composed from capabilities
pages.description: Serve the UI, the primary human surface the owner names `majordomus ui`, as its own native surface on the shared server: its own mount, shell, delivery-vocabulary navigation and assets, with a first Dashboard composed only from capabilities, each value citing the capability and pointer it was read from.

pages.title: I2462 — The UI has every screen, and its mesh is a graph whose nodes open an inspector
pages.description: Complete the navigation of majordomus ui against the owner's references with the Command, Capabilities, Deployments and Documentation screens. Make the Mesh screen interactive: a graph of machines, runtimes and sessions, each node selectable into an inspector whose selection is a URL.

pages.title: I2463 — A train of stacked pull requests is a typed object, served everywhere and drawn as a graph
pages.description: Derive the trains of open pull requests (chains and DAGs of declared and base-branch stacks) from the executor's own recorded observation as a typed read model, project it once as the capability integration.trains to the command line (majordomus prs trains), HTTP and MCP, and draw it in the Cockpit at /cockpit/trains as an interactive graph with a server-rendered table beside it.

pages.title: I2464 — A path that holds a space is one path to the scope doctrine
pages.description: Read the files a task touched as one path per line, with git's -z output, everywhere the shell layer lists them, so that a file name holding a space is judged as the one path it is.

pages.title: I2470 — The pull requests drain in the UI: a queue a reader narrows, inspects and follows to what each depends on
pages.description: Give majordomus ui a PR Drain screen (/ui/prs) that shows every open pull request as the integration lane assessed it, lets the reader narrow it by disposition, lane and text, inspect one pull request and the plan issue it names, and follow each dependency and overlap to the pull request it leads to; every control is a link or a GET form, so every view has an address and the screen is complete without JavaScript.

pages.title: I2471 — The roadmap opens a milestone: what it holds, what can start, its critical path, and what it waits for
pages.description: Let a reader of majordomus ui open any milestone of the plan (/ui/roadmap?milestone=M004) into an inspector that shows its issues and where each stands, the issues that can start now, the longest chain of open work through it, the intents its issues serve, and the milestones it waits for, is blocked by and unblocks, every one of them a link.

pages.title: I2472 — How long CI takes is measured, from when each run started to when it completed, and the CI/CD screen draws it
pages.description: Record when each check run on an open pull request's head started, beside when it completed, and answer how long CI takes from that record with a typed capability (integration.timings): per check its measured runs, failures, median, 90th percentile and longest duration; per open head its wall time and slowest check; and how many runs could not be measured. The CI/CD screen of majordomus ui draws it in place of the panel that said no capability records CI timings.

pages.title: I2473 — A pull request shows its trail: what the executor did to it, and the drain what the lane did lately
pages.description: Show, in the PR Drain's inspector, every event the integration executor recorded about the inspected pull request, newest first, and on the drain the lane's most recent events about pull requests, each leading to that pull request's inspector.

pages.title: I2474 — The drain draws its merge throughput: each day's merges over the fortnight its trail ends on
pages.description: Draw on the PR Drain how many pull requests the executor merged on each of the fourteen days that end on the day of its trail's newest event, as a chart whose counts are written in its label and in a table beside it.

pages.title: I2475 — The issues are browsed: every issue of the plan by status, milestone, priority or text, each a link onward
pages.description: Give majordomus ui an Issues screen (/ui/issues) that lists every issue of the plan, narrowed by the plan's own statuses as tabs and by milestone, priority and text in a GET form, each issue leading to its inspector, its milestone to the milestone's and what blocks it to that issue's.

pages.title: I2476 — An intent opens what serves it: its statement, its criteria and their evidence, and the milestones and issues that serve it
pages.description: Let a reader of majordomus ui open any intent (/ui/roadmap?intent=<id>) into an inspector that shows what it says, the invariants it holds the work to, each criterion of its satisfaction with its evidence, state and how to reproduce it, and the milestones and issues that serve it, each a link.

pages.title: I2477 — A claim opens its proof: what settles it, its last run, what changed since, how to see it again
pages.description: Let a reader of majordomus ui open any claim of the product (/ui/evidence?claim=<id>) into an inspector from evidence.claim: what it says and where, its state and what that means, the run behind it, what changed since it was proven, the command that reproduces it, the runs the ledger holds, and the claims its test also proves, each a link.

pages.title: I2478 — A rule opens its proof: what it states, the tests that prove it, what is missing, and the rules around it
pages.description: Let a reader of majordomus ui open any rule (/ui/governance?rule=<id>) into an inspector from rules.show: what it states, how it is enforced, every test that proves it with the state of its proof, the gates that run them, what is still missing to prove it, and the rules it depends on and that require it, each a link.

pages.title: I2481 — The UI links every entity it names, and says none where a source has no value
pages.description: Make every entity a screen of majordomus ui names lead somewhere: to the UI's own screen or inspector for it, to its technical view when the UI has no screen for it, or to the address its source gives when it lives elsewhere; say none where a source has no value; say how much a cut list leaves out; and count throughput over the window the queue states rather than one the screen chooses.

pages.title: I2482 — Every screen of the UI has a case, and no link on the UI is dead
pages.description: Prove every screen of majordomus ui through a real server, and prove that every link the UI draws inside the server answers.

pages.title: I2483 — The UI is published as a snapshot: read once at the published commit and carried by the site at /ui
pages.description: Let a person who has not cloned the repository open majordomus ui on the public site: the UI's own answers for every screen and panel, and for the inspectors they link to up to a bound, written as static files at the commit the site publishes, every page saying it is a snapshot and none of them leading to nothing.

pages.title: I2484 — majordomus ui ensures the shared server and opens the UI's dashboard
pages.description: Give the primary surface its command: `majordomus ui` ensures this checkout's shared server, the way `serve ensure` does, prints the address of /ui and opens it in a browser, so that a person reaches the UI in one step and never needs the lease, a port or the Cockpit to find it.

pages.title: I2485 — The bench measures the first request after the repository moved, and a budget bounds it
pages.description: Measure what a reader pays on the first request after the repository changed, as a benchmark target of its own, so that the budget of I2489 covers the case ADR 0142 was written for and not only the warm one.

pages.title: I2486 — No screen waits for a source: a page shows the latest reading with its age, read again behind the reader
pages.description: Take every handler, git call and file read off the path of a UI request: the executor keeps the latest reading of each source a page asked for, a screen is rendered from those readings at once, and a worker reads a source again behind the reader whenever the reading is not of the repository as it is now.

pages.title: I2487 — A screen is streamed, and one stream tells an open page which readings changed
pages.description: Send a screen as it becomes known and keep it current without polling: the shell and every panel whose reading is at hand are written at once, a panel whose first reading is pending follows on the same response, and after that one WebSocket subscription tells the page which readings changed.

pages.title: I2488 — The HTTP stack is chosen by measurement: the same routes and several hundred open streams on tiny_http and on axum
pages.description: Decide which HTTP stack the shared server keeps, from a measurement of the two candidates on the same routes, a streamed route and long-lived subscribers, and record the decision so that the repository has one stack and knows why.

pages.title: I2489 — A screen over its budget fails the build: the UI's latency budgets are benchmark policy, and bench --check holds them
pages.description: Make the owner's UI latency budget something CI enforces: the benchmark policy declares absolute bounds, bench --check holds them with or without a baseline and on every host, and the ui job runs that check on every change that can slow a screen.

pages.title: I2491 — A personal layer changes nothing shared: init --personal and install.sh --personal keep the layer one person's own, verify it, and --shared hands it to the team
pages.description: Let one person use the tool on real work in a repository other people share without changing anything shared: one flag on init and on the installer, every later writer covered by the same mechanism, the result verified at install and on every doctor, the executable reading an untracked layer without being told to, and one command that hands the layer to the team.

pages.title: I2495 — The Cockpit is published as a snapshot at /cockpit, and the UI's evidence links lead to it
pages.description: Publish the Cockpit on the public site as a snapshot read at the published commit, with the exporter that already reads the UI, so that /cockpit/ is a verified surface of the product and a capability the UI cites is a page a reader can open.

pages.title: I2521 — What a derive costs is measured per stage and per kind of change, and every file a stage reads is listed
pages.description: Measure the present derive on a named commit, stage by stage, for the kinds of change the incremental design is meant to make cheap, and establish which files each stage reads, so that every later issue of this milestone is judged against a recorded baseline and a known input set.

pages.title: I2522 — The derivation is a typed graph in the crate: every producer is a node with declared inputs and outputs, answered by one capability
pages.description: Declare the derivation graph as data in the Rust crate: one node per producer, with a stable identity, input selectors, exact outputs, an operation version and edges, ordered deterministically and refused when it is unsound, and answer it through one read capability and its generated schema.

pages.title: I2523 — A node's key is computed from the bytes its producer reads, the index membership it enumerates and the generation of the executable
pages.description: Give every node of the derivation graph a deterministic SHA-256 key over its identity, its operation version, its declared inputs as the producer actually reads them, the keys of the nodes it depends on and the generation of the executable, with a schema version of its own.

pages.title: I2524 — majordomus derive plan and derive explain say, without writing, which nodes would run and which input moved each one
pages.description: Add the read-only half of incremental derivation: a planner that marks every node reuse, regenerate, invalid or blocked with its reason, and the commands derive plan, derive status and derive explain over it, declared once as capabilities and projected everywhere.

pages.title: I2525 — An incremental derive runs only the nodes its plan marks, a no-op derive runs no generator, and the full derive stays as it is
pages.description: Execute the plan of I2524: run the producers of the nodes marked regenerate in graph order, leave the others untouched, record the keys of what succeeded, and keep the present full derive reachable and unchanged as the oracle. Opt-in; the default does not change here.

pages.title: I2526 — The site generator's sections are nodes with inputs of their own, and the use-case scenarios run only when what they exercise changed
pages.description: Split stage B into the nodes its real dependencies allow, starting with the execution of the use-case scenarios, so that an edit to one canonical file does not rerun every section of the site generator, and keep a coarser node wherever a finer one cannot be shown to be both correct and faster.

pages.title: I2527 — An incremental derive equals a full derive byte for byte, and an omitted dependency turns a gate red
pages.description: Hold the invariant that an incremental derive and a clean full derive of the same inputs leave the same tracked bytes, by a differential case over disposable repositories, by mutation tests that break the graph on purpose, and by a project rule with a check that runs.

pages.title: I2528 — The UI shows the derivation graph and its last plan, and one documentation page explains the model
pages.description: Show the derivation graph, the state of each node and the reason for it on one screen of majordomus ui, reading the capabilities of I2522 and I2524 and nothing else, and complete the documentation of the model in docs/DERIVE.md so that the published site carries it.

pages.title: I2529 — A node's outputs are kept under its key and restored only after every digest is verified
pages.description: Add a local content-addressed store of node outputs: a typed manifest and the output bytes per key, published atomically, verified on read, restored into the work tree only for paths the node owns, and never able to turn a damaged entry into a success.

pages.title: I2530 — The derivation store is bounded and measured: its size and hit rate are read by a capability, and only an explicit command removes entries
pages.description: Make the store a quantity the repository measures and reclaims like its other accumulating directories: report its size, entries, hits, misses and time saved or spent, and remove entries by age and quota only through one explicit mutating command that spares entries in use.

pages.title: I2531 — Two worktrees deriving the same key compute it once, and the machine lock covers the write into a tree, not the computation
pages.description: Let the worktrees of one machine share the store safely: one computation per key at a time, each worktree's files written only by its own run, and the machine-wide derive lock narrowed to what must not interleave, with the rule that states it amended in the same change.

pages.title: I2532 — CI reuses derivation entries keyed by the graph, and still fails on a stale committed file whether or not the cache was restored
pages.description: Restore and save the derivation store in the CI job that proves the derived data current, keyed from the graph and never from a second mapping of paths, while the job's verdict remains the byte comparison against the committed files.

pages.title: I2533 — The incremental derive becomes the default after a shadow period proves it equal, and one flag returns to the full derive
pages.description: Move scripts/derive to the incremental path by default in guarded steps: a shadow mode that runs both and compares, a recorded comparison on the real repository, the switch of the default, and a tested way back.

pages.title: I2601 — majordomus evidence reaches record, stamp and show
pages.description: Make the documented `majordomus evidence record|stamp|show` work from the launcher.

pages.title: I2652 — The UI shows what the knowledge base holds: the candidates awaiting review and whether the deriver still writes, read and never acted on
pages.description: Give the queue the work leaves behind a screen: what awaits a reviewer, what it is about, and whether a derivation still follows every closed episode, so that the result of a review is seen where every other state of the delivery is.

pages.title: I2653 — Every diagram on the site is one interactive, linkable viewer whose node links are inferred, and a derived table can be drawn as a chart
pages.description: Make every Mermaid diagram the site publishes zoomable, pannable, full-screen, downloadable and addressable by a fragment (#diagram-<name>, and #diagram-<name>:<node> for one node), with a node that names a rule, a decision, a command, a capability, an issue, a milestone or a document linked to that object's page by the build rather than by the diagram's author; and let a table the site already renders from derived data be drawn as an interactive Apache ECharts chart by declaring it, with no second copy of the numbers.

pages.title: I2654 — A chart is held to its table by a gate, and the tables that are measured series are drawn
pages.description: Give the chart component (site/charts.js, ADR 0152) the two checks it lacks, and declare the remaining tables whose content is a measured series as charts: the benchmark baselines, the economics pairs and segments, the claims by status.

pages.title: I2655 — The homepage decides whether it carries a derived figure, within its declared story and budget
pages.description: Decide, as a reviewed change to site/data/homepage.toml, whether one section of the homepage shows a derived diagram or chart through the shared viewer, and what that costs in the declared byte budget; if the answer is no, link the diagrams page from the section that argues for derivation.

pages.title: I2656 — The diagram viewer serves the Cockpit and majordomus ui, and a node that is a repository file links to its source
pages.description: Extend what I2653 built in two directions it left out: let the Cockpit and majordomus ui render a Mermaid diagram through the same viewer instead of a second implementation, and link a node whose label is a tracked file path to that file at the commit the site was built from.

pages.title: I2660 — The site is published as an artifact by the job that built it, so a ready site waits for no second workflow
pages.description: Remove the second queue from a publication: the job that built and checked the site hands it to GitHub Pages itself, and one publisher writes everything the site serves.

pages.title: I2661 — A publication that did not arrive is a finding the next reader meets, never a green step
pages.description: Make the gap between 'the workflow succeeded' and 'the site serves the commit' visible where a lander looks, the minute it exists.

pages.title: I2662 — Validation leaves the deployment a runner: a branch's checks never hold the pool a publication or a release record needs
pages.description: Bound what validation may occupy, so that the two things only the trunk can do, publish and record a release, start when they are ready.

pages.title: I2663 — The published UI is not read from nothing on every deployment
pages.description: Stop paying a quarter of an hour per deployment for a snapshot whose inputs did not change.

pages.title: I2664 — A run that has already failed is cancelled by itself, and a red on the trunk is fixed before anything else is prepared
pages.description: Make the time from a red to its fix the thing the pipeline is built for: a run stops spending runners the moment it cannot be green, and the trunk's red has one carrier at once.

pages.title: I2670 — A build-cache offer is a typed model and its selection is a pure, explained function
pages.description: Model an offer (protocol, provider, scope, non-secret endpoint, bucket, priority, capacity, health) and select among offers deterministically with the reason.

pages.title: I2671 — A provider offers its cache as a signed, expiring mesh record, and a stopped provider goes stale
pages.description: Let a node publish its offer through the mesh journal so peers discover it without a committed endpoint, and let the offer expire when the provider stops.

pages.title: I2672 — The offers and the selection are one read, projected to CLI, MCP, HTTP and OpenAPI
pages.description: Declare the read once with capability! so that every surface answers the same offers, the same choice and the same reason.

pages.title: I2673 — The sccache client configuration is derived from the selected offer, local disk first
pages.description: Emit the sccache environment for the chosen offer through majordomus env, local as level one and the offer as level two, with no hand-set variable.

pages.title: I2674 — A node is provisioned as an S3 cache provider, idempotently, with no secret in the repository
pages.description: Provision a MinIO service on a chosen node: native or declared service, persistent storage on a bounded path, a private bucket with expiry, a least-privilege client identity, and a bounded bind.

pages.title: I2675 — Build-cache health, headroom and hit statistics are visible where the mesh is
pages.description: Show which offers exist, which is selected and why, headroom and the statistics sccache supports, labelling estimates, on the existing health, monitor and UI surfaces.

pages.title: I2676 — The build cache is verified and validated: failure paths, security and a real second-node hit
pages.description: Prove the acceptance contract: stop the provider and build, restart and recover, bad credential, low space, put/get, remote hit across two nodes of one platform.

pages.title: I2677 — The build cache is documented, governed by a rule and described on the site and the Pages
pages.description: Say once, derived, what the cache is, how a node offers and uses it and how to see it, on the handbook, the site and the landing's account of how the cluster compiles.

pages.title: I2678 — The public Observatory replays events that were recorded, and says it is a replay
pages.description: Let the three scenes of the mesh move on the public site without inventing a single event: from a capture of real events, redacted, with its manifest, labelled as a recorded replay with its original times.

pages.title: I2679 — The Observatory follows a stream with a cursor instead of asking for its page again
pages.description: Make a change on the mesh reach the display when it happens, and make a gap in what was received something the display knows and says.

pages.title: I2680 — The Observatory's gates are closed with evidence: screenshots, measured frame rates, a soak, the recovery drills
pages.description: Close each acceptance gate of the owner's Observatory specification with a command, its result, its environment and a path to the evidence, or record it as not run.

pages.title: I2694 — A promoted note resolves in every checkout, not only where it was promoted
pages.description: Make `majordomus knowledge promote` produce a record that `knowledge check` accepts in a fresh clone and in CI, so that the evolve skill's procedure can be followed to its end.

pages.title: I2695 — The Observatory draws the proof, claim, surface, wave and release scenes from the capabilities that already answer them
pages.description: The kiosk shows thirteen scenes, five more of which read what the repository proves, and says why for any that has nothing to draw.

pages.title: I2696 — p5 is a built, optional asset of the UI and the page says where it is
pages.description: A p5 scene is drawn when the library is served and is an honest statement when it is not.

pages.title: I2697 — The public snapshot carries the p5 library, or says which scenes it cannot draw
pages.description: The kiosk on the public site draws the proof scenes with p5, from the one reading taken at the published commit.

pages.title: I2698 — The new scenes have screenshot evidence at 1080p and 4K on a named revision
pages.description: A manifest names the revision and holds a screenshot of each new scene at 1920x1080 and 3840x2160.

pages.title: I2700 — A lease probe asks a cheap liveness route, and a server holding another lease token is not taken for the leaseholder
pages.description: Point the lease probe at a liveness route that answers without resolving the index and carries the repository id, the leaseholder and a digest of the lease token, and judge a process whose digest differs from the lease's not the leaseholder.

pages.title: I2701 — The idle timeout is declared beside the other server timings, and serve --idle overrides the declaration
pages.description: Declare the server's idle timeout under policy.yaml server: beside the lease timings, validate it by the policy schema, and make every server that starts stop after the declared time unless serve --idle says otherwise.

pages.title: I2702 — A checkout keeps one address across restarts, because its server binds a port derived from the checkout
pages.description: Bind a port derived from the repository and worktree identity before falling back to a free one, so that a Streamable HTTP client configuration or a bookmarked UI names an address that survives a restart.

pages.title: I2703 — The mesh cooperation rule lists the hello checks in the order the code runs them, and a test names that order
pages.description: Bring rule project.mesh-cooperation-is-authenticated to the check order accept_hello runs, with the nonce cache last and the recipient check before it, as a new version of the blocking rule, and hold the code to it with a test.

pages.title: I2704 — A dialer reads no reply beyond the link bound and no more candidates than the bound, and a refusing peer is retried at a measured, jittered rate
pages.description: Bound the link and rendezvous replies a dialer reads at the link message bound and the candidate count it accepts at the registration bound, give the link backoff jitter, and measure the unknown_link retry rate in a test.

pages.title: I2705 — A node key can be rotated, peers follow the new key, and the old key is refused
pages.description: Offer a node key rotation that peers which trusted the old key can follow to the new one, after which the old key's hello is refused, and purge a withdrawn key's events from the running journal without waiting for a restart.

pages.title: I2706 — An own event whose append failed is never acknowledged as durable, and a journal reload is bounded in size
pages.description: Refuse to acknowledge an own mesh event as durable when its append failed, and bound how much a journal reload reads.

pages.title: I2707 — majordomus doctor reports a stale server, or says plainly that it checks governance only
pages.description: Make the top-level majordomus doctor either report the runtime of the checkout (server, lease, mesh) or say in its help, usage and reference that it checks governance alone.

pages.title: I2708 — A mesh event field nobody listed fails the mesh check, and no log field or review body carries a credential the redactor knows
pages.description: Make scripts/ci/mesh-check refuse an EventBody field absent from an allow-list, add a redaction layer for every tracing field, and pass review bodies through the redactor.

pages.title: I2709 — A red on the trunk has one named carrier, and nobody else may land until it is paid
pages.description: Make the trunk's red the first thing every lander knows about and the one thing that may land: a carrier is named on the board within the minute the red is read, and the landing claim is refused to anyone else until the fix is on master.

pages.title: I2710 — A release run never waits behind pull-request validates for a job slot
pages.description: Give the release path (the release workflow, the record pull request's verdict and the Pages deploy that publishes the release) priority over branch validates on the shared runner pool, so that a published release reaches majordomus.dev within its own run time.

pages.title: I2711 — The pages job judges production only after the deployment of its own commit has arrived
pages.description: Stop validate's `pages` job on master from reporting red because it read majordomus.dev before the deployment of the commit it judges had been served.

pages.title: I2712 — release-check treats a tag whose release run is still going as pending, not as a missing record
pages.description: Make scripts/ci/release-check tell a tag whose release workflow is still running (or whose record branch is about to be opened by it) from a published release that nobody recorded.

pages.title: I2713 — A build never lets idle incremental sessions fill the disk
pages.description: Make the repository's own build entry points keep a build directory's incremental cache bounded, so that concurrent sessions building on one machine cannot run the disk out.

pages.title: I2714 — One build directory never serves two worktrees' jobs at once
pages.description: Prevent a build directory set through CARGO_BUILD_BUILD_DIR from being used by jobs of two different worktrees at the same time, so that one job's build cannot replace the artifacts another job is testing.

pages.title: I2715 — New public Rust code meets rust-quality before the structure job does
pages.description: Put the rust-quality verdict (examples, behavioural tests and prose for every exported item) where an author meets it while writing — the fast local checks and the change's own proofs — instead of first in the 15-30 minute structure job.

pages.title: I2716 — A case derives its budgets and lists from what it tests, never pins them
pages.description: Keep a case from failing because its subject grew: a budget, a count or a list of names that a case states by hand is derived from the model or carries the margin and the reason it holds.

pages.title: I2717 — A release record pull request gets a verdict that can pass
pages.description: Give the record pull request the release workflow opens a ci verdict it can earn, so that it lands on that verdict and not on a lander's local judgement.

pages.title: I2718 — A linked worktree runs its own hooks, never the primary checkout's
pages.description: Make every linked worktree run, and doctor judge, the hooks of its own tree, so that a stale primary checkout cannot refuse or weaken the commits of every other worktree.

pages.title: I2720 — majordomus self update re-runs the published installer, and never reimplements it
pages.description: Give every installation one typed command that reports and applies an upgrade to the stable release by running the published install.sh with --version and the installation's own prefix, so the download, verification and swap exist once.

pages.title: I2721 — An enrolled mesh node follows the stable pointer by itself
pages.description: Make every node the mesh declaration enrolls keep its installation at the version releases/latest.json names, checking at server start, every 15 minutes with jitter and when the mesh announces a release, and applying through self update.

pages.title: I2722 — A hub activates a new version under its service manager, checks its health and rolls back by itself
pages.description: Make a hub that has installed a newer release restart onto it through its systemd user unit or launchd agent when no session is attached or after a bounded grace, pass a readiness and mesh verify check, and otherwise rename the launcher back, keep serving the previous version and put a rollout failed entry on the board.

pages.title: I2723 — The mesh shows each node's version and how far a release has rolled out
pages.description: Make every runtime publish its version and follow setting to the mesh, mesh peers print them, and mesh doctor name a node more than one release behind the stable pointer; a release is rolled out when every enrolled following node reports it.

pages.title: I2724 — A node without a route to the site takes the archive from a peer and still verifies it itself
pages.description: Let a following node that cannot reach github.com or majordomus.dev fetch the release archive from a linked peer over the authenticated mesh link, and install it only after checking its digest and size against release metadata it read itself or that was relayed and signed by the publishing node.

pages.title: I2731 — Every failure class in the published failure table names its test or its stated limitation
pages.description: Give the runtime's published failure table a proof column, in which every failure class names the tests that drive it or states the limitation that nothing does, and hold the column with a case that refuses a row with neither and a citation that does not resolve.

pages.title: I2733 — A resumed mesh.events walk returns every event exactly once, across partitions
pages.description: A reader that walks mesh.events page by page and resumes from the cursor each page answers receives every event the runtime accepts, exactly once, including an event from a writer that was partitioned from the mesh and stamped it at or below a position the walk already passed.

pages.title: I2734 — A session joins the mesh at its start and leaves it at its end
pages.description: The provider's start event opens the session on the mesh of the checkout's shared server as <provider>-<provider session>, with client, branch, head and the active task; the briefing names that id; a resume says it again; the end event closes it.

pages.title: I2735 — An edit no claim covers is refused
pages.description: With session.edits_require_claim on and the mesh enabled, a provider's pre-tool hook refuses a write (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit) no claim covers: the active task's scope or a live mesh claim of the writing session; judged by majordomus guard hook in the checkout the file belongs to, and by the capability guard.edit over MCP and HTTP.

pages.title: I2740 — An issue's delivery is inferred from branches, pull requests, merges, tags and the published site
pages.description: Add the capability plan.delivery (CLI majordomus plan delivery [--json] [<id>], HTTP and MCP from the one capability declaration) that answers, for every issue, the furthest stage of none, branch, pr_open, merged, released, deployed, each with the object that proved it and when it was observed, and expose it in the site data the plan pages read.

pages.title: I2741 — Merged work the plan has not recorded is drift, and on the trunk past a window it is red
pages.description: Add plan.drift over plan.delivery with the classes merged_not_recorded, active_without_work and done_without_trace (advisory), and a gate scripts/ci/plan-drift-check that refuses merged_not_recorded older than a window declared in .ai/repo/ci/plan.yaml on the trunk, naming majordomus plan verify|done <id>.

pages.title: I2742 — A milestone's version is inferred from the release that carried it, never typed
pages.description: Remove version from the milestone schema and the eight records that carry it, refuse a record that carries one, and derive released_in for a milestone as the first release record (the tracked statement of a tag) whose commit contains the merge of its last accepted issue (unreleased while open), in both the awk and the Rust engines' output; rewrite the vendored roadmap-integrity rule and its validator to match.

pages.title: I2743 — The public roadmap draws every milestone in the graph's order, each issue with its inferred delivery
pages.description: Rewrite site/templates/roadmap.html and site/content-src roadmap so /roadmap/ lists every milestone of the plan in the milestone graph's order (no filter on any hand field), shows released_in, each issue's declared status beside its inferred stage linked to the pull request, commit and tag that prove it, states the commit and time observed, and draws the milestone graph through the ADR 0152 viewer with nodes linked to milestone pages.

pages.title: I2744 — The UI roadmap reads delivery and the releases themselves, and its now is where work is
pages.description: Make /ui/roadmap (apps/majordomus-cli/src/ui/roadmap.rs) show each issue's inferred stage from plan.delivery beside its declared status, derive Now as the milestones with work in flight (open pull requests, mesh claims, ACTIVE) and Next from the graph, and read the latest release from the releases (tags and the published latest.json) at the moment it renders, so a snapshot never shows an older release than the executable that drew it.

pages.title: I2745 — The landing page states no present it does not read
pages.description: Replace every sentence in site/data/marketing.toml, manifesto.toml and homepage.toml that describes the current state of the product with a rendered datum from site/data/generated (release, plan figures, delivery, recent landings) or remove it, fix the link text that promises waves the roadmap does not show, and extend scripts/ci/homepage-check to refuse present-state vocabulary (today, not yet, nothing ... yet, no command ... today, is shipped) in those files.

pages.title: I2746 — Every published tree draws its diagrams, and every diagram is the interactive viewer
pages.description: Raise project.a-diagram-is-drawn-not-typed to version 2 covering .ai/repo/adrs, .ai/repo/rules, handbook and every markdown string majordomus ui renders, convert every box-art diagram those trees hold to Mermaid (Cytoscape where the graph is data) through the ADR 0152 viewer with inferred node links, and extend scripts/ci/diagram-check and case 272 to the new scope.

pages.title: I2747 — Every code block on every surface is highlighted by one engine with one palette
pages.description: Highlight every code block majordomus ui and the executable's reports render with syntect, the engine Zola already uses for the site, emitting the same class vocabulary; generate one stylesheet for both themes from the design tokens and use it on the site, the UI and the handbook; remove highlight.js and any CDN highlighter; add a gate that refuses a second highlighter.

pages.title: I2748 — The drift already on the trunk is settled before the gate is made blocking
pages.description: Run plan.drift on the trunk and, for every merged_not_recorded issue, either record it through plan verify|evidence|done with evidence actually run, or record why it is not done (a slice) by narrowing the issue or opening its remainder as a new issue; then make the drift gate blocking.

pages.title: I2749 — A commit that only plans an issue is not its delivery
pages.description: plan.delivery stops counting as a merge of an issue a commit or pull request that names it while changing only the plan's own records and what is derived from them, so that plan.drift's merged_not_recorded holds only work that was delivered.

pages.title: I2750 — The trunk's drift gate reads the forge before it judges
pages.description: The structure job that runs scripts/ci/plan-drift-check on the trunk records the forge first (open pull requests and merged pull request titles), and a finding the gate could not settle because the forge went unread is reported as unjudged rather than refused.

pages.title: I2760 — A scope entry is one path, and a path context would refuse is refused at start
pages.description: Refuse at `start` every scope entry that the task record cannot hold as one path or that `context` would refuse, and stop a recorded entry that `context` cannot resolve from breaking `context` and every commit hook.

pages.title: I2770 — majordomus ui and the Cockpit wear the site's navbar: one renderer, the same styles and scripts, and a browser comparison that refuses a difference
pages.description: Make majordomus.dev the reference for the product's look by giving every screen of majordomus ui and every page of the Cockpit the site's own navbar: the bar the site's partial renders over site/data/nav.toml, cut out of the built site and compiled into the executable, styled by the same Tailwind build over the same tokens, driven by the site's own scripts, and held to the site's bar by a browser comparison in both themes and at every declared width.

pages.title: I2780 — The UI has an intent workspace: an intent, its milestones, issues, waves and graph on one screen
pages.description: Add /ui/idd to the UI's screens: the intents as a choice with stage and verdict, the chosen one's criteria, its milestones in the roadmap's order with status, its issues with status, wave, priority and what blocks them, the waves those issues occupy, and the dependency graph between them with a table beneath it, every entity a link to its existing inspector and every ready issue a link to the move that starts it.

pages.title: I2781 — An issue is started, verified and finished from the intent workspace
pages.description: Render, for the issue picked in /ui/idd, the same plan.transition form the Cockpit's issue page offers — start, verify, done — started through executions.start and followed through executions.get, with the effect the capability declares confirmed before the move, the buttons disabled while it runs, and the refusal's own reason shown when the plan does not allow the move.

pages.title: I2783 — The intent workspace reads itself again when a move ends on its server
pages.description: Have /ui/idd hold one channel to /events through the Cockpit's socket.js, named by the page with the channel's path, and read the screen again when an execution ends there, at most once per burst; the line beside the read time says whether that channel is live, reconnecting or offline, from the socket's own state.

pages.title: I2786 — The published UI reads the evidence CI recorded, and a publication that would show tests as not run is refused
pages.description: Give the Pages workflow's UI snapshot job the ledger the validation of the published commit, or of its nearest validated ancestor, recorded (scripts/pages evidence --ledger-out), before the UI is read; then refuse to publish when evidence.report still counts more not-run claims than .ai/repo/evidence/published-not-run.txt declares (scripts/pages published-evidence); with the rule, a case and the documentation.

pages.title: I2787 — A build never lets the shared build directory's crate artifacts fill the disk
pages.description: Bound the shared build directory's debug/deps the way I2713 bounds debug/incremental: before a bounded build starts, remove the crate's own test binaries and libraries (majordomus_cli-*, libmajordomus_cli-*, and each tests/*.rs binary) of generations no live tree is building and older than a declared age, never a file a running process holds open, never another crate's dependency artifacts, and say on stderr what was reclaimed.

pages.title: I2789 — The intent workspace shows why an intent stands where it stands and every move made on its issues
pages.description: Add to /ui/idd, for the open intent: a panel asked on its own route (/ui/panels/standing?intent=<id>) from intent_realization.explain — the sentences its stage and verdict rest on, each unmet criterion with its evidence state, the command that reproduces it and the issues serving it, the work realising the intent with each link's provenance, and its drift; and a panel from executions.list of every plan.transition this server ran on the intent's issues, newest first, each leading to its execution.

pages.title: I2795 — The trunk's recorded run reaches the tracked evidence ledger, and the baseline is tightened to it
pages.description: Land the executions the newest green trunk run recorded (validate run 38844702397, artifact evidence, origin ci, 606 executions) in .ai/repo/evidence/ledger.json, as the recording pull request ADR 0080 proposes would, and tighten .ai/repo/evidence-baseline.txt to what that ledger supports with scripts/evidence-check --baseline.

pages.title: I2812 — The IDD loop is accepted end to end in a real browser on one commit
pages.description: Add case 3220: on a fixture repository and a real server, a real browser picks a test intent in /ui/idd, reads its issues and the dependency between them, starts an issue from its move form, sees the row change without the test reloading, writes and commits the work, runs the issue's own check as a real test and records its command and result as evidence, verifies the issue from a second tab while the first shows it without navigating, marks it done, and reads the standing panel's explanation and the issue page's evidence; the recorded command, run again, gives the recorded result. No feature is added.

pages.title: I2813 — A published page that answers 503, or does not answer, is asked again before it is called missing
pages.description: In scripts/pages verify-ui, ask again every page that answered 503 or did not answer at all (000: a connection refused or timed out), at most MJ_PAGES_RETRIES times (default 4) with a pause that starts at MJ_PAGES_RETRY_SECONDS (default 1) and doubles, and say each retry on stderr (\"retried /x: 503 ×2 then 200\", \"retried /x: 000 ×1 then 200\", or \"still 503 after N retries\"); any other status, and a 503 or 000 that persists, fails exactly as before. Case 3226 holds both halves of each and the 404 that is never retried, against a server of its own.

pages.title: I2825 — A claim released on one runtime is released on every runtime that holds it, and a link to a restarted peer recovers
pages.description: Find why a release event accepted on one runtime of this machine never reached the runtime whose stream holds the claim, fix it, and make the mesh say so when replicas stop converging: links to a peer's previous instance re-handshake instead of being refused indefinitely, and a rejection storm is reported rather than counted silently.

pages.title: I2826 — A GitHub release carries the tool's own changelog for its tag, never GitHub's generated notes
pages.description: Publish each GitHub release with the body `majordomus release changelog` composes for its tag (the release's decisions, including a release declaration such as ADR 0175, its conventional changes and its artifacts) instead of `gh release create --generate-notes`, and refuse a release whose published body is not that projection.

pages.title: I2827 — A tool written a moment ago is run once its writer lets go
pages.description: Give the crate one helper that starts a program and, while the program's file is still open for writing somewhere (ETXTBSY), waits briefly and asks again within a bound; use it at the spawn sites whose tests write a stand-in tool and run it at once.

pages.title: I2829 — An alpha is published as a pre-release end to end, and never becomes the latest release anywhere
pages.description: Let a pre-release tag (vX.Y.Z-alpha.N, -beta.N, -rc.N) go through the release pipeline: the publish job publishes its tag file and leaves latest.json alone, the release smoke waits on that file, installs it pinned and requires latest.json to name another release, release-check holds a published pre-release to its record and orders versions by semantic-version precedence, and the installer installs a pre-release only by name.

pages.title: I2840 — A cancelled MCP call stops, and the client is told it stopped
pages.description: Honour notifications/cancelled on every MCP transport: the call it names stops within a declared bound, is answered as cancelled rather than with a late result, and a writer's effect is reported as complete, absent or unknown.

pages.title: I2841 — The site's browser probe is split, so the site job runs well inside its timeout
pages.description: Split `probe the site in a browser` (scripts/site-probe over every route at 320, 390 and 1280 px) so the site job no longer runs at its timeout, and keep the full sweep: no route and no width is dropped.

pages.title: I2842 — The live site is verified on a schedule, and its last verification is evidence
pages.description: Between deploys, keep proving that majordomus.dev serves what the trunk says: every scheduled Pages run that finds nothing owed also reads the live homepage, UI and Cockpit snapshots against the trunk, latest.json against the newest release tag, and asks a rotating sample of the UI's pages through `scripts/pages verify-ui`; the result is recorded and shown, and a mismatch that outlives the deploy window turns the run red with the page named.

pages.title: I2849 — release next raises from the trunk the repository names, never from a branch name written in the tool
pages.description: When `majordomus release next` (capability release.next) is given no --base, it measures the landing against the remote-tracking ref of the trunk this repository names, through the one rule the delivery report already uses (delivery::revision::trunk_ref), and refuses by name when the trunk cannot be told.

pages.title: I2850 — the published PR Drain carries its pull requests, and counts pull requests rather than plan issues
pages.description: A UI page the snapshot writes carries every slow panel the screen defers to its script, already read, in the place the script would have put it: the published /ui/prs shows the drain, the Dashboard its pull requests and Deployments its delivery. The PR Drain's counts are the integration queue's own, one card per lane the queue counted, each a link to that lane.

pages.title: I2851 — the homepage's product view counts the delivery the history proves beside the statuses the records declare, each count a link
pages.description: The product view in the homepage's hero counts, first, how far each issue's work travelled as plan.delivery infers it from the history, stage by stage in the projection's order, naming the commit it was inferred at. Then it counts the statuses the issue records declare. Every count is a link into /roadmap/, where each issue carries its stage and the object that proves it, and homepage-check holds the counts to delivery.json and plan.json.

pages.title: I2852 — every class a UI screen gives an element is one the UI's stylesheet defines
pages.description: A unit test reads every literal `.class(...)` of the UI's screen sources and the UI's stylesheet source, and refuses a class that the stylesheet neither defines nor defines parts of. The classes it found undefined move to the kit's own: the search labels to mj-sr-only, the lists to mj-ui-prose-list, the mesh's counts to mj-ui-mono.

pages.title: I2853 — a Pages deploy on a fresh master is not refused for claims newer than the ledger it reads
pages.description: `scripts/pages published-evidence` reads a `not run` claim whose test exists at none of the commits the ledger was recorded against as not yet recorded: it is named in the output and is not held against the published-not-run baseline. A claim whose test existed when the ledger was recorded still counts, and every claim counts when no commit of the ledger is in the history.

pages.title: I2882 — A remote derive builds only inside its own run directory
pages.description: The derive offload's remote script pins cargo's build directory, not only its target directory, to the run directory `<shared>-<tag>` that its traps remove, so nothing a remote derive compiles outlives the derive on the host, whether it succeeds or fails.

pages.title: I2900 — Every issue id on the intent workspace is a link, the shared-scope pairs are one folded line, and no missing library is asked for
pages.description: On /ui/idd, the plan's next issue tile leads to that issue, and each shared-scope pair names both of its issues as links; the pairs fold into one line that gives their count and opens to them. The UI names the vendored graph library only when the distribution holds it, so a checkout without it serves the graph's table with no request, no 404 and no console error. Case 3220 asserts all three in a real browser. No new feature.

pages.title: I2901 — One grammar names an issue id, and every surface reads it
pages.description: Declare the issue id grammar once: a pattern in the issue schema (or generated from one Rust const) and one plan::is_issue_id, read by ui/prs.rs, ui/idd.rs, case 3220 and share/ui JS, so no surface spells it its own way.

pages.title: I2902 — A status names the moves it admits, and every surface reads that
pages.description: Give plan::Transition the rule of which status admits which move (READY start, ACTIVE verify, VERIFY done), used by plan::transition's refusal, ui/idd.rs and cockpit::plan::moves, with a test that they agree.

pages.title: I2903 — The workspace prefers stages by IntentStage, not by strings
pages.description: Make idd::PREFERRED_STAGES a list of IntentStage, printed through IntentStage::as_str, so a renamed stage cannot leave the workspace behind.

pages.title: I2904 — An intent whose criteria are met while its milestones hold open issues says so
pages.description: When an intent's criteria are all met but its milestones still hold issues that are not DONE, every surface (/ui, /cockpit/intents, the snapshot) says \"criteria met; N issue(s) still open\", derived from plan.roadmap.

pages.title: I2906 — Every id and chip on the workspace leads to its record
pages.description: Make every milestone chip, the roadmap's current milestone and the issues that serve a criterion links: a milestone to /ui/roadmap?milestone=<id>, an issue to its inspector; one href per kind in ui/view.rs that /ui/mesh can reuse.

pages.title: I2907 — The workspace's headline numbers are the chosen intent's
pages.description: Replace the hero's global counts with the chosen intent's: criteria met of all, its milestones done of all, its issues by status, each derived from intents.explain and the issues the screen already filters; the global counts stay on /ui/roadmap.

pages.title: I2908 — Stage and verdict wear the kit's one badge
pages.description: Draw an intent's stage and verdict through the same state badge every status uses, retiring the boxed uppercase variant on the workspace.

pages.title: I2909 — A panel with nothing to show is one sentence
pages.description: Draw a workspace panel that has nothing, or one trivial row (no dependency, one wave), as one sentence instead of a full panel.

pages.title: I2910 — A move on the published workspace reads \"live only\"
pages.description: On the snapshot, render each move control disabled and labelled \"live only\", with a link to the live route, instead of a control that looks actionable and is not.

pages.title: I2911 — The workspace is a list and its chosen intent side by side
pages.description: Lay the workspace out as master and detail at 1024 px and wider: the intent list on the left, the chosen intent on the right and sticky; stacked below that width.

pages.title: I2912 — A screen's sources are one disclosure, not a footer per panel
pages.description: Fold every panel's source line into one \"Sources\" disclosure per screen, keeping each capability, its time and its technical-view link.

pages.title: I2913 — Each intent in the list shows its progress
pages.description: Give each intent in the list a compact progress row: criteria met of all and issues done of all, derived.

pages.title: I2914 — No /ui page shows an issue id that leads nowhere
pages.description: Add a ui-audit rule links.bare-issue-id that fails any /ui page showing an issue id outside a link or a code block, at every width.

pages.title: I2915 — The workspace speaks in plain words
pages.description: Rename the workspace's labels to plain words (\"Next issue to start\", \"What is missing\", \"Work serving it\") and keep capability ids only in the source lines.

pages.title: I2916 — The workspace reads in the order a person asks
pages.description: Order the panels: what the intent is, what is missing, what to do next, the work (milestones, issues, waves, graph), then evidence and moves.

pages.title: I2917 — Each intent has one primary action
pages.description: Show one primary action per intent (\"Start I0702\", \"Verify …\"), derived from plan.next restricted to the intent's issues and the move that issue's status admits; every other move is secondary.

pages.title: I2918 — The issue list filters by status
pages.description: Let the issue list be filtered by status, the statuses read from the plan and the filter kept in the URL so the snapshot can carry it.

pages.title: I2919 — The graph and the intent list respond to a hand and a keyboard
pages.description: A dependency graph node opens its issue when the vendored library is present (the table stays the fallback), and the intent list is navigable with the arrow keys and Enter, with an axe-clean focus order.

pages.title: I2941 — A fresh init leaves doctor clean: a README that does not name AGENTS.md gains one paragraph that does
pages.description: Make the adopter's clean-install path (init, update, the two hook lines) doctor-clean: a shared init appends one paragraph naming AGENTS.md to an existing README.md that does not mention it, once, leaving the rest of the README byte for byte, and lists it with what it created; it creates no README and a personal layer leaves the project's README alone.

pages.title: I2942 — An installer dry run changes nothing, and the install guide says only what is true
