pages.description: Stop `install.sh --dry-run --init` from initialising the repository when the resolved version is already installed, and correct what the install and distribution documents state by hand that is not true: the clone directory of the build-from-source steps, provenance for releases before attestation existed, the one call to GitHub the installer can make, and the container image the release workflow already publishes.

pages.title: I2943 — A mesh this process is not on is said as not observed, never as zero or no
pages.description: When mesh.peers answers that cooperation does not run in this process, /ui/mesh and the dashboard's mesh tile and panel say the mesh was not observed, with the runtime's own reason, and draw no machine count, refused-link count, journal clock or 'Mesh active: no'; the kit gains one not-observed KPI and one not-observed panel body that every screen can use.

pages.title: I2962 — What the served surfaces change is said as the registry says it
pages.description: Correct every published sentence that calls the server read-only or counts its writers by hand, to what the capability registry says each capability changes and to who may call it, and hold that with a case that compares the interfaces feature's list of repository writers with the registry and refuses the retired sentences.

pages.title: I2963 — The README's exit codes are the commands' contract
pages.description: State in the README's command table the exit codes each command's model declares, and hold the table to share/commands.yaml (through its generated projection) with a case, so the sentence 'Exit codes are a contract' is true of the table above it.

pages.title: I2964 — Every step that reads a surface into the published snapshot can ask the forge
pages.description: Give every Pages workflow step that reads the UI or the Cockpit into a snapshot (`web report`) the workflow's token, so that a page which asks GitHub through gh while it is rendered publishes what the forge says instead of the failure to ask, and hold that with a case that reads the workflow.

pages.title: I2965 — The site says a test proves a guarantee only as far as recorded evidence supports it
pages.description: Qualify every site sentence that says a test proves a guarantee, or that work ends proven, to what the recorded evidence supports, and declare the proof words as homepage promises so the existing homepage check refuses them in the hand-written copy unless a supported claim permits them.

pages.title: I2966 — A forge setting that could not be read is unknown, never \"allows nothing\"
pages.description: Read the repository's merge settings as unknown when the forge's answer does not carry them, and say so in the integration policy, in each held pull request's reason and evidence and in the queue's diagnostics, instead of reporting that the repository allows no merge commit.

pages.title: I2967 — The site's own pages name the layout in force
pages.description: Correct the site pages that name the retired `.majordomus/` layout as current, and hold every top-level page, the site's hand-written data and its templates to the `.ai/` layout with a case, leaving the retired path to the migration and plan pages where it is history.

pages.title: I2987 — server.status and peers.list ask every checkout at once, a bounded number at a time
pages.description: Make the repository-wide readings of `server.status` and `peers.list` ask the checkouts git registers concurrently, at most `server::ASKED_AT_ONCE` (16) at a time, through one helper (`server::each_checkout`). The answers are folded in the order git lists the checkouts, so the output, its order and `complete` are what the one-at-a-time loop gave. Each probe stays bounded by the declared probe timeout, so the wait is a few timeouts however many checkouts there are.

pages.title: I2993 — doctor counts the work no remote holds in one walk, whatever the number of branches
pages.description: Make doctor's `clone unpushed` reading one walk of the clone: the commits some branch reaches and no remote does, with their parents (`git rev-list --parents --branches --not --remotes`), and every branch's tip (`git for-each-ref`). Each branch's count is the commits of that set its tip reaches, walked inside the set. The finding, its wording and its counts are what the per-branch `rev-list --count` gave.

pages.title: I2995 — doctor does no work whose answer cannot change a finding: the roadmap lookups and the board's wide status
pages.description: Remove the two readings that dominated doctor in the commit hook without changing a finding. (1) The roadmap doctrine reads the README's release list first, and when the section lists none it decides OK before looking up any milestone's release; a list is still compared with the release records both ways (ADR 0166, I2742: records, not tags). (2) The context builder's board asks `serve status --checkouts this` for the address it uses, and asks every checkout only when this one has no server, so its answer is the one the wide question gave.

pages.title: I3000 — The workspace's record texts are drawn as prose
pages.description: Draw every record text on the workspace (statement, why, criteria, standing sentences, drift) through ui::prose, so code spans, strong words and links render and an id is linked only when the plan holds it; ui/idd.rs's own id linking goes.

pages.title: I3001 — The intent is the page's title, and panels ask questions
pages.description: Make the chosen intent's title the page's h1 with \"Intent workspace\" as the eyebrow, and title the panels as plain questions.

pages.title: I3002 — A command to reproduce is a code block a reader can copy
pages.description: Render each reproduce command as a code block with a keyboard-reachable copy control, in the snapshot too.

pages.title: I3003 — The workspace's prose is set for reading
pages.description: Set the workspace's prose at about 70 characters a line with the kit's body size and contrast, keeping muted grey for secondary text only; the design contrast check passes.

pages.title: I3004 — No raw markdown reaches a /ui page
pages.description: Add a ui-audit rule text.raw-markdown that fails any /ui page whose rendered text carries ```, ** or a backticked span, and a case 3220 step reading a rendered criterion's code span.

pages.title: I3005 — Code on the UI has one highlighter
pages.description: Highlight code blocks on the UI with one shared highlighter, the same one the site uses or a vendored one, not a second.

pages.title: I3007 — A commit that a record or the site's data names is a commit the history holds
pages.description: `scripts/ci/link-check --sources` decides, before any site is built, every commit/<sha> link written in a tracked file under .ai/repo/project, site/data or site/content-src, and every commit a data file hands a template to link, the key names read from the commit links the templates build, by the rules the built-page check already uses: a commit outside the history being published is a finding, and a shallow clone defers. lib/common.sh gains mj_commit_in_history (0 in, 1 not, 2 undecidable), the one predicate for the producer side (I3050). Two issue records that cited rebased evidence commits name the commits that landed.

pages.title: I3008 — A homepage link with a fragment resolves to an element its page carries
pages.description: Hold the homepage navigation rule (site-check 13d) on a fixture: a hero or navigation link with a #fragment resolves when its page exists and carries that id, fails naming the element when the page lacks it, and a link to an absent page fails as unresolved. The rule becomes one function, run by the full site-check and alone through `site-check --nav PUBLIC_DIR CONFIG_TOML`.

pages.title: I3010 — The mesh manual says the edit guard is not wired, and how to wire it by hand
pages.description: docs/MESH.md stops saying the edit guard is wired in the provider's configuration. It says that `capture install` writes no PreToolUse entry, so `session.edits_require_claim` refuses nothing in Claude Code yet; that the hook script and guard.edit exist; how a person wires it by hand (the entry, which settings file, a new session); and that wiring it and refusing an unclaimed edit are the generated-plugin work after the alpha.

pages.title: I3020 — The Knowledge screen states nothing about the repository that its checkout could not observe
pages.description: Where knowledge_base.status read no line of the session ledger (no close, no derivation, no close without a derivation), /ui/knowledge shows the ledger-derived tiles (Closed, underived; Newest episode) as 'not recorded here' and its deriver panel says that no ledger is recorded in this checkout and where the judgement is made, instead of '0', 'unknown' and 'never, in this checkout'.

pages.title: I3021 — The Knowledge screen shows each review command as code with what it does as a sentence
pages.description: The Review panel of /ui/knowledge draws its six commands as an ordered prose list, each step a command in inline code followed by what it does as a sentence, instead of fact cards whose command is drawn as a bold headline value.

pages.title: I3022 — An empty knowledge queue is one sentence that says how a record arrives, not two empty tables
pages.description: When knowledge_base.candidates answers a total of zero and no candidate, /ui/knowledge draws one Awaiting review panel holding one sentence: nothing awaits review, and a record arrives when a session closes and the deriver writes it, or when majordomus knowledge observe records what was noticed.

pages.title: I3023 — The Knowledge screen reads in review order, in plain labels, and leads to the knowledge manual
pages.description: /ui/knowledge orders its panels as a reviewer works (Awaiting review, By subject, How to review, Is learning up to date?), labels its tiles and facts in plain words (From an unknown branch, Sessions not yet learned from, Newest session, Up to date, Last learned from, Last session closed) and links the review to the knowledge manual under /docs/knowledge/.

pages.title: I3024 — The Knowledge screen's manual link names a page the site has, on the server and on Pages
pages.description: The How to review panel of /ui/knowledge links to the knowledge manual as {DOCS_MOUNT}/docs/knowledge/, which a server serves from the site build mounted at /docs and which the published snapshot rebases to /docs/knowledge/ on majordomus.dev.

pages.title: I3025 — Every Knowledge tile reads whole at a phone's width
pages.description: The hero tiles of /ui/knowledge carry labels and written values that fit the kit's narrowest tile (9.5rem, about 152 px at 390 px): Unknown branch, Not learned from, and 'no ledger' where no session ledger is recorded, with a crate test that holds every tile label and the written value to the measured budget.

pages.title: I3060 — A provider hook declares its timeout, and the session end closes its episode inside the budget
pages.description: `capture install` writes a per-hook `timeout` for every hook it generates. The values come from one declared table per provider and event, read by both the configuration writer and the end handler. The SessionEnd handler keeps the episode close inside that budget: it skips the optional closing checkpoint and continuation, as typed failures, when running them would leave the close too little of the budget. A configuration that byte-for-byte matches the shape this tool wrote before timeouts existed is rewritten to the new shape. Any other configuration is left as it is, and install names the timeouts it lacks.

pages.title: I3090 — The UI audit warms every surface and gives an unreachable page a second load
pages.description: Before the first visit, the UI audit loads the first planned page of every top-level surface, not only the root. It records page.unreachable only after a second load fails, and never retries a refused connection, which still stops the run.

pages.title: I3100 — What the ChatGPT project decided is promoted into the layer, each record naming the conversation and message it came from
pages.description: Read every conversation of the declared workspace chatgpt-majordomus once, extract what the owner ordered, decided and learned, verify each candidate against master and the peer board, and promote what is not yet recorded as intents, milestones, issues, proposed ADRs and curated knowledge, each record citing its sources as chatgpt-majordomus:<conversation>#<message> so it drills back to its root; raw content stays in the git-ignored workspace store.

pages.title: I3110 — A blocking rule reads proven only when one of its cases shows its violation refused
pages.description: Extend the rule proof so that a blocking rule is satisfied only when one of its named cases declares the rule whose violation it refuses with a '# majordomus-refutes: <rule-id>' header and has a passing recorded run. '# majordomus-negative:' keeps its command vocabulary and is never read as rule proof. majordomus-cli rules report prints the blocking rules that lack such a case, and scripts/ci/rule-proof-check ratchets that list.

pages.title: I3111 — Every dispatched blocking validator is run against a declared violation, and one that accepts it fails the case
pages.description: Replace grep-only effect proof with execution. Each dispatched blocking rule (x-majordomus validator) declares a minimal violation fixture under test/fixtures/violations/<rule>. One case builds a disposable repository per fixture, runs the real entry point (check, finish or the pre-commit hook) and requires a non-zero exit that names the rule id.

pages.title: I3112 — rule-proof-check prints the blocking rules no recorded run proves, and that count only falls
pages.description: Deliver the milestone criterion that has no issue: majordomus-cli rules report and rule-proof-check print, per class, the rules whose state is not_run, gated, stale or unproven. The blocking not_run ratchet runs in the validate job after scripts/ci/evidence-collect, over that run's own executions for its own head. /ui/rule, /ui/governance, the published snapshot and site/content/rules render each rule's state and refusal_shown, so no not_run, stale or unknown rule is drawn as pass.

pages.title: I3113 — github-check refuses when master's protection no longer requires the verdict check gates.yaml names
pages.description: Teach scripts/ci/github-check to read the default branch's requirement from repos/{repo}/rules/branches/{base}, which the Actions token can read, and classic branch protection only where the credential allows, and to compare the required contexts with the verdict job .ai/repo/ci/gates.yaml declares. Drift is a refusal with the exact idempotent gh api command as remedy. A 403, a 404 'Branch not protected' and an absent requirement are distinct typed readings, none of them pass.

pages.title: I3114 — A merge past the required check is observed from the forge and matched to the owner's recorded authorisation
pages.description: From the forge's merged pull requests, list each merge whose head had no successful run of the verdict check that .ai/repo/ci/gates.yaml declared at the merge commit's parent tree. Match each to the decision record that carries the owner's order (rule an-expedited-landing-is-the-owners-word, point 1) and to the lander's landing claim. An unmatched merge is a finding of integration and of the evidence view.

pages.title: I3115 — A rule or guarantee that cites a proposed decision as its authority is listed, and the owner's acceptance queue is derived from it
pages.description: Derive the citation edges from active rules, docs/CLAIMS.yaml guarantees and features to ADRs. Report every blocking rule or guarantee whose cited ADR has status proposed, ordered by how many rules rest on it, as the owner's acceptance queue. This is advisory, not a refusal.

pages.title: I3116 — The debt every ratchet baseline holds is one derived table, with its rule and its trend
pages.description: Derive one table from every ratchet baseline file under .ai/repo: the top-level *-baseline.txt files and .ai/repo/ci/case-numbers-baseline.txt, .ai/repo/ci/github-drift-baseline.txt and .ai/repo/evidence/published-not-run.txt. Each row names the gate that writes it, the rule it serves, and its entry count now and at the previous release. Show the table in the evidence view and in doctor --json. A baseline with no owning gate is a finding.

pages.title: I3117 — The README and the launch page say only what master does about model invocation, doctrine dispatch and overrides
pages.description: Reconcile the model-invocation clause of README.md:20-21 ('never invokes a model') and docs/LAUNCH.md:44 and :61 with master, where scripts/advisor-consult carries questions to advisor CLIs, and state that an expedited landing is a recorded override. Qualify README.md:207-212 as the doctrine dispatch of lib/doctrine.sh and lib/check.sh, distinct from the CI ratchet baselines. Add each corrected sentence to docs/CLAIMS.yaml so claim-proof-check holds it to a test.

pages.title: I3118 — The edit guard's contract names every case it lets through, and each row has a test
pages.description: Write the guard's decision table into docs (server unanswered, policy off, path outside the checkout, local state, no-file tool, own claim, task scope, another session's claim). Make guard.rs tests table-driven over it. Public text calls the guard blocking only for the rows that block.

pages.title: I3119 — The delivery report computes required_tests_current, test_evidence_published and ui_linked instead of citing a merged pull request
pages.description: Fill the three phase-1 dimensions of apps/majordomus-cli/src/delivery/mod.rs: required_tests_current from the subject verdict of the feature at the trunk revision, test_evidence_published from the site's publication of that verdict, and ui_linked from the routes /ui and the site serve for the subject. Then remove EVIDENCE_PENDING.

pages.title: I3120 — A scheduled mutation run over the declared critical predicates records its survivors as evidence
pages.description: Declare the critical predicates once in .ai/repo/ci (mesh trust and protocol, guard judge, evidence freshness, finish vacuous-verify, release compatibility). Run cargo-mutants over those files on a schedule or an offload host. Record the run (killed, survived, timeout per mutant) through the existing ledger path, and list the survivors in docs/COVERAGE.md's evidence section.

pages.title: I3121 — The release compatibility analyzer's invariants hold under property tests
pages.description: Add proptest properties to apps/majordomus-cli/src/release/compat.rs: diff(a,a) is empty; reordering a surface gives no change; adding a distinct atom is at least minor; removing one is at least major from 1.0; normalisation is idempotent.

pages.title: I3122 — A coverage figure on every surface names its dimension, its commit and what it does not measure
pages.description: Make the coverage publication carry, per figure, its dimension (Rust crate lines, functions or regions; session domain), the commit and tree state it measured, and the list of unmeasured dimensions (shell cases, browser, MCP and WebSocket transports). The site and /ui render that, not one percentage.

pages.title: I3123 — finish refuses a verify command the profile does not admit for the change, and keeps its output
pages.description: Let a profile or policy declare the verify commands (or command prefixes) a completed outcome may cite per scope class. finish refuses a command outside that set, beyond the no-op and print refusal already in mj_verify_is_vacuous, and records the tail of its output with the exit code.

pages.title: I3124 — A JUnit XML report a repository already produces is imported into the evidence ledger, and nothing in that repository changes
pages.description: Add an importer (majordomus evidence import --junit <file>) that normalises test cases into ledger executions with suite, case, outcome, duration, commit and tree state. Malformed XML, duplicate imports, missing artifacts and a stale revision are typed refusals. For a foreign repository this is the default Observe mode: discover and import, never instrument.

pages.title: I3125 — Coverage from LCOV or Cobertura is linked line by line to the source at the measured revision
pages.description: Import LCOV and Cobertura into the coverage record (reusing the llvm-cov export shape) and render a covered or uncovered region as a link to the source at the measured commit.

pages.title: I3126 — check and finish count the refusals later overridden and the completions later reverted, per rule and per release
pages.description: From the ledger, derive two rates per rule and per release. Candidate false refusals: a refusal followed by an override, or a later finish of the same task with no relevant change. Candidate false acceptances: a completed finish whose commits are reverted, or whose issue reopens, within a window. Publish both with denominator, window and provenance.

pages.title: I3127 — A clean installation reaches its first refused finish in a foreign repository, and the time and the manual steps are recorded
pages.description: Give scripts/ci/install-check a first-run stage: with the installed release in a throwaway HOME, init a foreign fixture repository and run the steps of .ai/repo/use-cases/catch-an-agent-that-says-it-is-done.md against the installed binary (a worker edits outside scope and claims done, check and finish refuse, the fix lands, finish accepts), recording elapsed seconds per step, the platform, and every command typed that the published site does not document. Run the stage in the validate.yml install job and the release.yml smoke step against the published installer, and keep a pre-merge regression case on case 1024's fixture.

pages.title: I3128 — init ends with what it found in the repository it adopted, each finding naming its file
pages.description: After init writes the layer, print a read-only account of the adopting repository, each line naming the file it read: which instruction files share/providers.yaml declares exist and whether they agree by a rule docs/ADOPTION.md states, which hooks git would run (core.hooksPath and the hook files there) are wired to doctor or check, and whether the effective profile declares verification.verify_commands (I3123).

pages.title: I3129 — An outside developer's first run is recorded as it happened, and each friction it met becomes an issue with a failing case
pages.description: Write the outside-first-run protocol as a workflow (who may run it, the private consented invitation, the fixed form the tester answers, what is recorded and what never is), record five real outside runs as the testers' own answers committed as curated knowledge, give each friction an id, open one issue per friction in this milestone or in a-second-adopter-is-served, and add the case that checks the records and the friction coverage. The issue stays blocked on external until the five runs exist.

pages.title: I3130 — The ledger answers how many false dones finish caught, by doctrine, with the tasks it counted
pages.description: Declare one read capability in the gates family that aggregates task.refused and task.finished from this checkout's ledger: tasks accepted, tasks refused at least once before acceptance (false dones caught), refusals per doctrine, tasks refused and never accepted, and the time from first refusal to acceptance, each with the task ids behind it; project it to CLI, HTTP and MCP by majordomus generate.

pages.title: I3131 — A refusal answered by no change to the tree is not counted as a caught false done
pages.description: Record on task.refused and task.finished an answer digest over every input a refusing doctrine reads (the tree id from mj_worktree_tree_id, already written as verify.tree, the completion note's content, the verify command and the obligation evidence), and have the aggregate classify a refusal as unanswered only when none of the inputs its own doctrine reads changed before acceptance, and as downgraded when the accepted outcome is lower than the refused one.

pages.title: I3132 — /ui shows what finish caught beside what being caught cost, and says not observed where there is no ledger
pages.description: Add one card to the /ui dashboard that reads the gates aggregate: false dones caught, unanswered refusals, refusals by doctrine, median time from first refusal to acceptance, each linking to the tasks it counted, with the kit's not-observed rendering for an absent ledger and in the published snapshot.

pages.title: I3133 — The economics benchmark measures acceptance: how many sessions declared done while the task's hidden tests fail, with and without the finish contract
pages.description: Add an acceptance metric to the economics methodology over the existing pilot corpus: per arm, the fraction of sessions whose final state the agent called done while the hidden acceptance tests fail, and add a treatment variant that includes the finish contract and hooks the first treatment excludes; the generator publishes it only past the methodology's existing rule.

pages.title: I3134 — The product sentence is declared once, and the homepage, README, page titles, Open Graph and launch kit read it
pages.description: Make the owner's chosen product sentence a field of the declared site copy, have scripts/generate-site-data read it instead of grepping README.md for '**A lightweight', render README's bold line and lead from it (or fail homepage-check when they differ), and close docs/HARDCODING_LEDGER.yaml row product-sentence-has-two-wordings.

pages.title: I3135 — The launch kit is held by the same promise check as the homepage, and the tool publishes none of it
pages.description: Extend homepage-check's [promises] and product-sentence checks to docs/LAUNCH.md and site/content/docs/launch.md, derive the kit's one-sentence pitch from the declaration, and correct what the kit states that the model does not (it runs 'in portable shell').

pages.title: I3136 — The copy refuses hype words that no recorded comparison permits
pages.description: Add to site/data/homepage.toml [promises] the words the positioning work ruled out (revolutionary, revolutionize, 10x, next-generation, AI-powered orchestration, unlock, transform), each \"\" until a claim permits it, so homepage-check refuses them in the copy files it reads.

pages.title: I3137 — Lumen is a declared term of the vocabulary, defined by the capabilities it composes
pages.description: Once the owner accepts ADR 0209, add lumen to docs/CONCEPTS.md as a lowercase row naming the owner's mesh-wide view, listing the capabilities it reads (blackboard, peers, mesh, monitor) and the surfaces it appears on, in the same change as the first surface that says the word (docs/MAJORDOMUS_UI.md), so that case 28 reads the row and finds the term in use.

pages.title: I3138 — One page shows the whole mesh from the blackboard, peers and monitor with each figure's freshness, and recovers after a reconnect
pages.description: Make /ui/mesh the owner's one mesh page by adding to 5a's blackboard rendering only the delta: the source capability and age of every figure, the runtime's liveness words (expired, and the link state mesh.peers reports) and blockers with their source, read through the blackboard's shared read and followed over its live channel, so that after a gap the page says reconnecting and then shows the current state.

pages.title: I3139 — The mesh page offers one authorised action through an existing capability, and shows its result from the journal
pages.description: Offer one mesh action on the live /ui/mesh page, mesh.review.request, written only under the identity the router resolves and refused by the capability without one, once the ADR amending ADR 0126 that decides how a mesh event names its human author is accepted; render its outcome from the journal event it produced rather than from the click.

pages.title: I3140 — The mesh page's latency is measured against a recorded baseline before any target is claimed
pages.description: Record, under rule project.performance-evidence and through a measuring command under scripts/ui and scripts/lib, warm status on a named route, cold and warm first paint, local event to screen, and subscription recovery for the mesh page, with hardware and percentiles; only then declare targets, as budgets of benchmark policy.

pages.title: I3141 — majordomus session close writes its record through the typed domain's closer, and the shell closer is deleted
pages.description: ADR 0047 cutover step 1: route the shell's session close to session::store close, keeping the shell's arguments, human output and exit codes, and delete the shell writer and its lock path.

pages.title: I3142 — An episode opens through the typed domain and records the task and issue it began on
pages.description: ADR 0047 step 2 plus the missing attribution: session start delegates to the domain's opener, and session.started carries the task the episode began on as an Option<TaskId> taken from a ledger fact of its own provider session; the closer derives the bound issue from that task's own ledger events and folds both into tasks and issues.

pages.title: I3143 — Each provider lifecycle event leaves a typed receipt written by the domain before any guard can return early
pages.description: ADR 0047 step 3: the provider hook shims call the domain instead of capture session, and every start, compact, end and prompt event writes a received or failed receipt with its diagnostic.

pages.title: I3144 — Checkpoints and handovers are recorded against the episode, and the shell only parses and renders them
pages.description: ADR 0047 step 4: lib/checkpoint.sh and lib/handover.sh become argument parsing and rendering over the domain, which writes checkpoints and handovers against the episode.

pages.title: I3145 — Continuity is resolved and judged fresh by one function, and the shell's copies are deleted
pages.description: ADR 0047 steps 5 and 6: continuity.state, lifecycle.*, episodes.* and the Cockpit read the domain's aggregates; mj_resolve_latest and mj_freshness are deleted and their callers ask the executable, so nothing in lib/ holds domain state.

pages.title: I3146 — A closed session record says whether it is complete, and one that changed the tree without saying what it served is not
pages.description: Derive a completeness verdict for every closed record (complete, incomplete with named reasons, legacy-unverifiable) and for the calling provider session's open episode; report it on doctor, check and finish; keep episode_closed, task_completed, verified and accepted as four distinct facts.

pages.title: I3147 — The effective governance has one digest, computed by one function and shown by the preflight
pages.description: Compute a digest over the sources of the effective governance, declared once in policy.yaml (project and vendored rules at their versions, profiles, workflows, skills, prompts, scope.yaml, the declared share/schemas entries, the hook wiring in .claude/settings.json and a declared list of governing policy keys), as sha256 over a canonical manifest of (input id, content hash) from working-tree bytes, and show the digest and its manifest in the preflight's governance check and on every entry surface.

pages.title: I3148 — An episode records the governance digest and the briefing digest it was handed at start
pages.description: Write governance_digest and the governance manifest into session.started, and append a session.briefed event carrying briefing_digest once the start briefing has been derived; the preflight and the brief show the recorded values; an episode that edited files with no session.briefed receipt is flagged where the policy and the provider promise a briefing.

pages.title: I3149 — A governance change during a session is told at the session's next brief or check
pages.description: Compare the current governance manifest with the episode's recorded one whenever the session briefs itself (I2399), runs check or reaches the next lifecycle event its provider wires, and print the inputs that moved with the command that re-reads them.

pages.title: I3150 — A handover carries the governance digest it was written under, and resolving it says when governance moved
pages.description: Write the governance digest and manifest into a handover's front matter and have handover --resolve name the inputs that moved, beside the plan_revision drift I2003 reports.

pages.title: I3151 — Every entry surface reports the same governance digest for one checkout
pages.description: Write one new parity case that drives .envrc (majordomus-env enter), the Claude Code SessionStart shim, a Codex and a Gemini session entry, an MCP initialize, brief.session and the CLI preflight and compares their governance digests with each other and with the episode's session.started; a stale input fails it.

pages.title: I3152 — Every known route around the preflight and the edit guard is a case or a stated limit
pages.description: Enumerate the routes around entry and the edit guard (hooks disabled, a client without hooks, raw git, MAJORDOMUS_NO_BUILD, a missing executable, another machine) and give each a case that proves the refusal or a line in SECURITY.md's limits, held together by a structure check.

pages.title: I3153 — Task start says how far its base is behind the remote's master as last fetched, and stops only on a diverged local master, with the next step
pages.description: Have start report how far merge-base(HEAD, refs/remotes/origin/master) is behind, with the age of the last fetch from that ref's reflog, warn on a dirty tree, and refuse only when local master is both ahead of and behind refs/remotes/origin/master, naming the command that brings it current; start never fetches and never pushes.

pages.title: I3154 — Every just recipe is generated from the command graph or names the exemption that keeps it hand-written
pages.description: Count the untracked bridge that majordomus commands bridge generates (ADR 0027) as the generated recipes, refuse a hand-written recipe whose body is one call of a bridged command, and resolve every remaining hand-written recipe to its inventory record.

pages.title: I3155 — The shell check reports shell by disposition, and the count of domain-logic shell never rises against the merge base
pages.description: Add a ratchet to majordomus shell check comparing the class-A unit and line counts with the merge base and refusing an increase or an unexplained relabel, serve the per-class counts as a reading on CLI, MCP and HTTP, and draw that reading as the shell observatory on /ui.

pages.title: I3156 — Every command path is implemented by one executable, and the other only delegates
pages.description: Derive, from the command graph's existing join of share/commands.yaml and the Rust registry, the implementing executable of every command path (program plus its full word sequence); report a path both implement outside a declared delegation as a commands validate finding; serve the reading on CLI, MCP and /ui. Delegation stays read from docs/generated/cli.yaml at run time.

pages.title: I3157 — A scripted capability declared in an adopting repository's layer reaches its surfaces with no change to the tool, and says where it came from and what it may do
pages.description: Prove I1801's kind from outside the tool's tree: a fixture adopter declares a scripted capability, it is discovered and projected, and capabilities explain shows its origin file, declared effect, exposure ceiling and the projections it reaches; a call above the ceiling from MCP or HTTP is refused.

pages.title: I3159 — A shell unit is deleted only after a parity case shows its replacement gives the same verdict on the same fixture
pages.description: Generalise I1804's per-gate parity into a harness: the inventory record of a unit being migrated names its parity case, the case runs the legacy and the new path on one fixture and compares exit code and structured output, and the shell check refuses deleting a class A or B unit whose record names no passing parity case.

pages.title: I3160 — A behavioural case can be written as a Rust integration test over a disposable repository, and the continuity cases are the first ported
pages.description: Add a typed fixture builder (disposable git repository, remote, fake clock, two checkouts) under apps/majordomus-cli/tests and port the continuity cases 821-827, whose behaviour is already Rust, with the same assertions, deleting the shell originals.

pages.title: I3161 — The commit hook is one call of the executable that runs the commit subset of doctor, the worktree guard and pages current under a declared budget
pages.description: Replace .githooks/pre-commit's sequence of bin/majordomus doctor, worktree guard, scripts/pages current and providers-check with one hook command of the executable that composes them and reports its own time against benchmark.budget.

pages.title: I3162 — Which task.refused lines are friction is measured across every checkout, and then each repeated refused rule becomes one observation candidate
pages.description: Measure once, over every checkout's ledger, which refusals are friction rather than the tool working, and record the classification rule through majordomus reasoning; then have the deriver, reading only the closing checkout's ledger across its episodes, turn a refused rule id seen in at least a declared number of episodes into one observation candidate with about and route.

pages.title: I3163 — Each episode boundary derives whether evolve is due — skip, defer or run — and the next session is told why
pages.description: At episode close in lib/session.sh, derive once a readiness verdict from the candidate groups, their recurrence and routes, the last evolve.run, live mesh claims, and a cooldown and budget declared in policy; record it as a ledger event even when it is skip; name it in the SessionStart briefing, with a directive on run, and in brief.session, CLI, HTTP, MCP and /ui/knowledge; 'run' tells the session to run the evolve skill, never promotes.

pages.title: I3164 — A change an evolve run makes yields no candidate about itself, and a rejected subject is not proposed again without new evidence
pages.description: Have the deriver skip, as sources, the task.finished and decision.recorded lines of an episode that holds I3163's evolve.run, cite none of that episode's commits, and keep its observation.recorded lines; prove with a test that a rejected subject returns only beside a later observation.

pages.title: I3165 — What evolution changed is measured: recurrence of a subject after its lesson landed, per window, with its denominator
pages.description: Derive, from candidates, promotions and later observations, how often a subject recurs after its lesson landed, over declared windows, and show unavailable as unavailable.

pages.title: I3166 — A curated note whose cited file changed since its last review is reported for review, not served as current
pages.description: Have knowledge validate and the context compiler compare each cited provenance.derived_from file with the blob recorded at the note's last review and mark the note needs-review when it differs.

pages.title: I3167 — A campaign is a kind of the index: every pack under campaigns/ is an object with its manifest digest, served read-only
pages.description: Make campaign a kind of the index through a tracked YAML index outside campaigns/ (one member per pack: id, path, date, origin, revision digest) read by the existing members mechanism of share/kinds.yaml, so every pack rides the index onto CLI, MCP, HTTP and OpenAPI; the revision digest is defined from campaigns/MANIFEST.sha256; the site keeps not publishing pack bodies.

pages.title: I3168 — An intent, milestone or issue cites the campaign that drove it, and a campaign answers which records cite it
pages.description: Accept a campaign:<id>[/<path>] reference in the one provenance.derived_from of intent, milestone and issue records (ADR 0211), refuse a dangling one with the same finding in both plan engines, and derive the reverse relation on the campaign object.

pages.title: I3169 — A new pack enters campaigns/ through one command that checks the archive before writing a byte
pages.description: Add a campaign add command that reads a ZIP or directory with limits on member count, sizes, decompression ratio, nesting, path traversal and symlinks, writes the pack verbatim, appends campaigns/MANIFEST.sha256 and the campaign index member, and executes nothing it contains.

pages.title: I3170 — An execution of a record that cites a campaign pins the revision it ran, and a later revision changes nothing about it
pages.description: Record the campaign id and revision digest on an execution whose input names an issue, milestone or intent citing that campaign, resolved at start and never changed afterwards, with no change to StartInput or the executions.start contract.

pages.title: I3171 — The compiled context names source ranges with their reason and confidence, not only whole objects of the layer
pages.description: Extend devcontext so a request with scope paths yields source entries (path, line range, symbol where known, reason, confidence, cost) beside layer objects, and measure the tokens saved against whole-file reading on a large file.

pages.title: I3172 — The compiled context names the small set of capabilities the work needs
pages.description: Add a selector over the capability registry so a compiled context lists the capabilities relevant to the request's scope and kinds, each with its reason, within the budget.

pages.title: I3173 — A synced workspace conversation proposes candidate records that cite their conversation and message, and nothing becomes canonical without an act
pages.description: Map synced workspace content (.ai/local/workspaces) into knowledge candidates and intent proposals through the existing candidate pipeline and intent.propose, each citing the typed workspace reference of ADR 0211 pinned to the upstream message identity (never a positional message index); promotion stays an act.

pages.title: I3174 — An exclusive claim carries a fencing epoch, and a holder returning under an old epoch is refused
pages.description: Give every exclusive mesh claim a monotonically increasing epoch issued by the runtime that admits it, carry it on every write the holder makes under the claim, and refuse a write or a completion whose epoch is lower than the current one, so a worker that reappears after its claim expired and was retaken cannot finish under its old right.

pages.title: I3175 — Two hosts presenting one node key are named as a duplicate, never folded into one flapping node
pages.description: Detect two live instances advertising the same node id from different addresses within one expiry window, report them as a duplicate identity in mesh peers and as a failed check in mesh doctor, and keep the registry from counting their alternation as restarts.

pages.title: I3176 — The committed mesh declaration names its hubs by node, and no private address is tracked or published
pages.description: Let the declaration name a hub by its node id and resolve its endpoint from signed, expiring mesh records (tailnet or Bonjour discovery, the hub's own advertisement), then remove the LAN and tailnet addresses from .ai/repo/mesh/majordomus.yaml and the fleet table of docs/MESH.md.

pages.title: I3177 — Two nodes one release apart keep linking, and what the older cannot answer is shown unavailable
pages.description: Prove in the mesh lab that a node upgraded one release ahead keeps its node identity, takes a new instance id, still links to the older node through the negotiated protocol, and that a capability only the newer offers is listed unavailable on the older's surfaces rather than hidden.

pages.title: I3178 — A self update killed at any stage leaves a usable installation
pages.description: Drive the installer that self update runs through an interrupted download, a kill at each stage (download, verify, stage, swap, health check), a failed post-update readiness and two concurrent updates, and hold that each ends with the previous or the new version runnable and saying which.

pages.title: I3179 — The runtime reports one typed state, with how it got there, and every surface shows it
pages.description: Extend ServerStanding into one runtime state per checkout (keeping absent, starting, ready, outdated and stale, adding building, mesh attaching, operational, degraded, stopping, stopped and failed) derived from the lease, the readiness report and the mesh doctor, with the time and reason of the last transition, and serve it through server status, the briefing and /ui.

pages.title: I3180 — Entering a checkout whose executable is missing or stale starts one background build and says building
pages.description: When the entry hook finds no executable or a stale one, start one deduplicated, detached build under the shared build lock, report 'building' in the banner and the runtime state, and let the next entry or client start the server once it finishes; never compile synchronously in the shell.

pages.title: I3181 — A change made on another node reaches every open page by push, and a gap is refetched
pages.description: Carry mesh journal events that arrive from a linked runtime (sessions, claims, handovers and reviews) into the events channel the local executions use, so /ui/mesh and /ui/peers update without a reload, a page that detects a cursor gap asks for a snapshot, and a client that ends and returns resumes from a snapshot and cursor with nothing lost.

pages.title: I3182 — One read says which work is progressing, waiting, stalled, failed or orphaned, and on what evidence
pages.description: Add a read-only capability that folds health, mesh presence, session episodes, executions, claims and integration waits into one classification per item (progressing, legitimately waiting, suspected stall, unbounded, confirmed failure, orphaned, unknown outcome, repeated recovery failure) and per resource (leaked, not draining), each with the evidence and the age that decided it; project it to CLI, MCP and /ui.

pages.title: I3183 — A safe repair runs once per cause through ensure, recovery, leases and the reaper, and a repeated failure escalates
pages.description: Act on supervision findings of the idempotent classes only (reconnect a valid mesh link, ensure a required server, resubscribe events, refresh a derived projection, free a resource whose owner is provably gone), each with reason, owner, one verification and a circuit breaker that stops after repeated failure and puts the finding on the board.

pages.title: I3184 — One command lists every Majordomus runtime of this user on this host, with no checkout open
pages.description: Add a host-scoped read that enumerates the servers of every repository this user runs (from their leases, found through a disposable per-user cache of checkout roots beside node.json and, for runtimes that predate it, the process table), with version, repository identity, checkout, port and node, and serve it from the CLI without a server and from any running server's API.

pages.title: I3185 — A request on a host with two Majordomus versions reaches the one whose protocol satisfies it, or is refused with a reason
pages.description: From the host inventory and each runtime's negotiated protocol range and capability set, answer which runtime a client should attach to for a given repository and request, deterministically, and refuse an incompatible pair with a typed reason.

pages.title: I3187 — A link names the endpoint candidates it tried, the one it chose and why
pages.description: Record, per link, the endpoint candidates each discovery provider produced (source, observed_at, expires_at), the dial attempts with their outcome and latency, the path chosen and the rule that chose it, with hysteresis against flapping; serve it in mesh peers and /ui/mesh.

pages.title: I3188 — A cold node finds the mesh from a signed manifest on Pages, and refuses a stale, rolled-back or unsigned one
pages.description: Publish, through the existing Pages pipeline, a manifest of hub node ids and their public reachability hints, signed by a key the trust root names, with canonical serialisation, a monotonic sequence and an expiry; a node with no live peer reads it, keeps the last valid copy, and stops needing it once linked.

pages.title: I3189 — Two nodes with no direct path cooperate through a trusted hub that relays their authenticated frames
pages.description: Let a hub both nodes trust carry link frames between them when neither can dial the other, with the frames still signed end to end by the existing link keys, a byte and rate bound per relayed link, and a direct upgrade attempted in the background and taken when it succeeds.

pages.title: I3190 — The mesh lab proves links behind NAT, with the relay, a hub outage and an address change
pages.description: Add NAT topologies to test/mesh-lab (two private networks behind masquerading routers, one blocked UDP) and scenarios for relayed link, direct upgrade, hub down, address change and compromised bootstrap, each with measured connect time, required by scripts/ci/mesh-lab-evidence.

pages.title: I3191 — The UI reads any linked runtime the mesh names, and says which runtime every reading came from
pages.description: Offer on /ui a target choice derived from mesh nodes (local, each trusted linked runtime), read the chosen runtime over HTTP from the endpoint on its signed RuntimeCard, through its declared ingress where one exists, stamp every panel with the runtime, the transport, that the read is unsigned and the observation time, and render an unreachable target as a state.

pages.title: I3192 — An operation started from /ui/mesh is authorised, executed, audited and its result streamed back
pages.description: First propose the ADR amending ADR 0126 that decides which credential admits a remote write and how a mesh event names its human author; then take the one mesh action I3139 offers on /ui/mesh through executions.start, authorise it by the caller's identity and the capability's declared effect, record its audit as the signed mesh journal event the write produces (author, operation, policy, result, evidence), stream the result to the page, and refuse it from an unauthenticated remote caller.

pages.title: I3195 — The lundra hub is a declared deployment target served over its tailnet name, and a second device reaches it
pages.description: Declare the hub as a deployment target whose listeners are declared separately (the mesh rendezvous port answering only the signed link and register routes; the UI/API/MCP origin on loopback behind a tailnet HTTPS ingress set up through the installed Tailscale CLI), run it as the user-scoped unit I2722 writes, prove reachability from a second authorised device with served observe extended to a named deployment target plus an off-tailnet negative probe, and commit each run as the target's evidence.

pages.title: I3196 — A deployment's external URL, trusted hosts and forwarded headers are one typed fact read by every surface
pages.description: Extend deployment/v1 with the target's external URL, visibility and auth mode, make the server derive its canonical and trusted hosts from it, honour forwarded scheme and host only from a declared proxy, and project the ingress state through deploy, health, the UI and the docs.

pages.title: I3198 — A peer is offered an assignment by capability under a fenced lease, and accepts or refuses it with a reason
pages.description: Add assignment offer, accept, refuse and return as mesh events and capabilities: the offer names the issue, the required capabilities and the lease; a peer whose declared capabilities do not satisfy it refuses with the missing one; a lease lost mid-run returns the work and says so; nothing executes yet.

pages.title: I3199 — An assignment names the execution profile it needs, and a peer whose envelope does not satisfy it is refused
pages.description: Carry the effective profile limits (write, deploy, tests required) on an assignment, compare them with each candidate peer's declared envelope, refuse an unsatisfying peer by the missing limit, and refuse an implementer as its own verifier.

pages.title: I3200 — The trunk's protection is compared with the CI model, and a drift is a finding that names the change
pages.description: Declare the aggregate verdict check once in .ai/repo/ci/gates.yaml, then compare the required checks the last forge observation read for master with it, and report a missing, extra or unread requirement as a finding with the idempotent gh command that would fix it, from the recorded observation and without reaching the network; scripts/ci/release-verdict reads the same declaration.

pages.title: I3201 — A publication never replaces the site with a build of an older commit than the one gh-pages serves
pages.description: Make scripts/site-deploy refuse to push a build whose source commit is a strict ancestor of the commit gh-pages:build.json records (the served build, the source pages.yml already reads), the way it already refuses an older release, so a delayed run or a manual deploy from a stale checkout cannot overwrite a newer site; --release-metadata stays exempt because it leaves build.json unchanged.

pages.title: I3202 — CI timings measure the wait before a run starts beside the run, and count what cancelled runs spent
pages.description: Read the Actions workflow-runs and jobs API over a declared window in prs refresh, so integration.timings gives each run its queue time (created to started) beside its execution time (started to completed) and tallies the runner minutes of cancelled and superseded runs, and the one-at-a-time pool's wait is measured instead of inferred.

pages.title: I3203 — Delivery lead time is measured per phase, from a pull request's opening to its verified publication
pages.description: Time the phases of the delivery stages plan.delivery derives per issue (I2740: pr_open, merged, released, deployed, each with the object that proved it) and report p50/p95, sample size and observation time per phase, taking a merged pull request's opened and merged times from the forge's pull request record so merges made outside the drain are counted, and writing no join of its own.

pages.title: I3204 — The backlog's bound is declared once in policy, and every session brief says when the landable backlog is past it
pages.description: Move the landable-backlog threshold from the MJ_BACKLOG_MAX default in scripts/ci/backlog-check into .ai/repo/policy.yaml, read it in both backlog-check and the session brief, and have the brief's integration section say 'past the bound' from the last recorded observation, without a network call and without refusing anything.

pages.title: I3205 — A pull request's change is split into canonical, derived and incidental paths, and the drain shows each
pages.description: Classify every path a pull request changes as a canonical input, a derived projection (what .gitattributes merge=derived and the generators declare) or incidental, carry the counts on the queue's assessment, and report change amplification: how many derived files one canonical change rewrote.

pages.title: I3206 — The delivery phases have budgets in benchmark policy, and a phase over its budget is a finding with its trend
pages.description: Once I3202 and I3203 measure the phases, declare each phase's budget beside the UI budgets bench --check already holds, report a phase over budget as a finding with its last window's trend, and keep wall time a report rather than a correctness gate where the runner is not ours.

pages.title: I3207 — A finished task names the pull request that carries its branch and that pull request's disposition
pages.description: Make majordomus finish report, from the last recorded queue observation, the pull request whose head is the task's branch, its disposition and next action, or that no pull request carries the branch yet, so the work a worker hands to the landing seat is named at the moment it is handed.

pages.title: I3208 — Whether a commit may be released is one read that names each condition and the evidence that settles it
pages.description: Add release.readiness to the release capability: for a commit and a candidate version, decide what release.yml's plan and verdict phases, the version gate and the base branch's ci verdict decide, and answer ready, not ready with the failing condition, or unknown with what could not be read, including the surface fingerprint the record will publish; release.yml's plan and verdict phases then call it, so one implementation decides both. The install job is the after-tag half and is named as not readable before a tag.

pages.title: I3212 — Two open pull requests that realise the same issue are reported as duplicates, with the survivor named
pages.description: Use the pull request to issue edge the work graph already derives to report open pull requests that realise the same issue, name the survivor by evidence (green head, landed member of a top, newer head) and leave the closing to the landing seat; never close automatically on title or path similarity.

pages.title: I3213 — One case walks a fresh clone from init to published evidence on the release candidate
pages.description: Compose the paths existing cases already prove separately (install into a foreign repository, init, a session joining, an issue started and finished, its test run, its evidence recorded and published) into one case that runs on the release candidate and names the stage that fails.

pages.title: I3214 — The narrow-screen menu of /ui and /cockpit closes on Escape, on a choice and on its backdrop, and returns focus to its toggle
pages.description: Give /ui and /cockpit one narrow-screen drawer shell (toggle, panel, backdrop) that each surface fills with its own entries: Escape, the backdrop and choosing an entry close it, focus returns to the toggle, the page behind does not scroll while it is open, it opens with scripts off, and only one menu toggle shows at a narrow width; the Cockpit gains the narrow navigation it lacks, and cockpit-probe holds the behaviour at every declared width.

pages.title: I3215 — The ui audit refuses a control a thumb cannot hit at the floor width
pages.description: Declare the minimum touch target once in share/design/tokens.yaml and feed it to axe's target-size check, which the ui audit already runs through the wcag22aa tag, so one measurement judges every control of every discovered page at the floor width; report its violations as component.target-size, and admit today's findings through a committed baseline that only shrinks.

pages.title: I3216 — The IDD loop is accepted at a phone's width as it is at a desktop's
pages.description: Run case 3220's walk (pick an intent, start an issue, verify it from a second tab, mark it done, read its evidence) a second time at the floor width the design declares, with no feature added.

pages.title: I3217 — A wide table on a UI screen is a stacked list below the narrow width, from the same rows
pages.description: Give the kit's table one narrow projection (each row a card with its labelled cells, the first column its heading) applied by CSS below the declared narrow width, and use it on the Issues, PR Drain and workspace issue tables; a graph's table fallback is shown first at that width.

pages.title: I3218 — The execution ledger is a source of the monitor, so a run started anywhere is followed everywhere
pages.description: Add executions to the monitor's sources with a cursor part of their own: a store-wide publish counter in the execution store paired with the server's epoch, so majordomus monitor and monitor.read carry execution starts, ends and refusals and an expired cursor is answered as the other sources answer one; the event vocabulary is the execution model's, not a new one.

pages.title: I3219 — The Observatory is told what happened over the live channel, and asks only when it cannot be told
pages.description: Let /ui/observatory and /ui/kiosk be told what the journal appended: the journal tells its subscribers every append, /events serves it as a topic carrying the client's logical clock, and PR #1178's observatory-stream.js applies each frame to the scene model the page already builds; the page falls back to its cursor read of /api/v1/observatory/events only when the socket is refused, saying so; the published replay is untouched.

pages.title: I3220 — An intent proposed or an issue moved by any client reaches an open intent workspace without a reload
pages.description: Advance the change generation (crate::change, from I2981) on every repository_mutation capability of the plan and intents (intent propose, plan transition, evidence attach), and have /ui/idd read itself again on that frame, whichever client made the change: the CLI, MCP from a Claude Code session, or another tab.

pages.title: I3221 — Every live surface says in ADR 0158's words whether it is live, reconnecting, stale, polling, a snapshot or a replay
pages.description: Give every live surface one browser-side mapping from its transport state to ADR 0158's words, shared by the scripts of /ui screens, /ui/peers, /cockpit/monitor and the Observatory: LIVE, RECONNECTING, STALE and POLLING on a server, SNAPSHOT and REPLAY on the published site; view::liveness and the Cockpit kit render only the first-paint word.

pages.title: I3222 — A follower whose frames are lost, delayed or reordered, or whose peer is partitioned, ends equal to a fresh snapshot
pages.description: Add a fault-injection case over the live channel: a test-only frame-level WebSocket proxy drops, delays and reorders frames and partitions a mesh peer, then each follower's state is compared with a snapshot read afresh; no feature is added and the protocol is unchanged.

pages.title: I3223 — The homepage hero lets a visitor switch between recorded scenarios, each ending in the refusal it proves
pages.description: Offer in the hero's left column, under the reassure line, a short list of links: the challenge as the default, described as refused and then accepted, and every use case that site/data/generated/terminal.json names among its refusals, each linking to its /use-cases/<id>/ page with at most its one derived verdict line, naming the homepage problem it answers, with the build's commit; homepage-check and case 333 hold it.

pages.title: I3224 — Every problem and every step on the homepage leads to the feature and evidence behind it, with the maturity the product model derives
pages.description: Make the recognise section's problems and the how section's steps nodes that name the features answering them, derived and never declared (a problem's features are its domain's; a step's are the product.json features whose commands contain its lifecycle command), with those features' evidence and each feature's declared status and claims' evidence verdict; a step that no feature names is labelled as such.

pages.title: I3225 — A capability is run from /ui through the form its input schema generates, confirmed when its effect writes, and followed as an execution
pages.description: Move the Cockpit's schema-generated capability form and its execution start path (share/cockpit/executions.js installStartButton, data-mj-start, data-mj-confirm, followed through share/cockpit/socket.js) into the module both surfaces import (ADR 0135), and offer it on /ui/capabilities?id=: the run is an execution of the shared executor; confirmation is asked exactly when ExecutionPolicy::needs_confirmation is true; a refusal is the executor's, verbatim; the run's events follow on the page through the execution's links.events and links.websocket, its full page at links.cockpit. The direct-route runner (runner.js's Run) is not offered on /ui.

pages.title: I3226 — Every UI and Cockpit response says where its time went
pages.description: Write a Server-Timing header on every /ui, /cockpit and /api response from a request-scoped recorder installed in Router::handle and fed by ui/source.rs's capability reads (with cache hit or miss) and by the executor, named in the perf::Phase vocabulary plus the route, render and bytes stages this issue adds, and let the bench record it per route so a budget miss names its stage.

pages.title: I3227 — A UI link a reader is about to follow is fetched ahead when the route is cheap and the connection allows it
pages.description: First record from I3226's Server-Timing the document-fetch cost a prefetch would remove on a /ui navigation (documents are sent Cache-Control: no-cache, panels load as fragments) and the cockpit::csp directives a prefetch must satisfy; only if that cost is measured, prefetch on hover or focus the /ui links whose navigation carries it, skipping Save-Data and slow connections, with the prefetch list derived from the rendered links and the measurement, not kept. With no measured cost the issue closes as not needed and the criterion is withdrawn.

pages.title: I3228 — The UI's search finds any entity the registry addresses and offers the moves its status admits
pages.description: Give /ui a search of its own (Ctrl/Cmd+K), answered on /ui from objects.search over every addressable kind, each result naming why it matched from SearchHit's new additive `matched` field and, for an issue, the moves its status admits (imported from I2902's status-to-move table), leading to the entity's page or the move's form.

pages.title: I3229 — Every version badge says whose version it is and how it stands to the latest release
pages.description: Label the navbar's version badge on the site (the release it published), on /ui and /cockpit (the executable serving the page) and on the snapshots (the commit read), and when the executable differs from the latest published (offered) release say 'ahead of' or 'behind' it, from distribution.releases and the compiled version, never release.version, through new slots of the shared navbar.

pages.title: I3230 — The Dashboard opens on what needs the owner: what runs, what is blocked and why, what was verified, and the next safe move
pages.description: Add a first panel to /ui (the Dashboard), served as a /ui/panels fragment (ADR 0142), that answers in plain words: the intent being served, the issues active and who works on them (from the blackboard source I3138 composes), what is blocked and on what (plan.status), evidence.report's verdict at the presented revision, and plan.next's one next move, the same derivation /ui/idd renders; each sentence a link to its record; mechanism figures stay below.

pages.title: I3231 — The Observatory shows its own stream health: lag, dropped frames, resyncs and frame rate
pages.description: Add a diagnostics overlay to the Observatory (toggled like its legend) that derives from the stream it follows: frames received, last frame age, resyncs, gaps detected, and the measured frame rate of the renderer.

pages.title: I3232 — A kiosk left running for days shifts its marks against burn-in and recovers from a lost drawing context
pages.description: Give /ui/kiosk a slow positional drift of static marks and labels, a brightness ceiling, and recovery when the canvas context is lost, each bound declared in .ai/repo/benchmarks/observatory/manifest.json and read by the kiosk, and each covered by a drill in the Observatory's gates.

pages.title: I3233 — Stage C renders only the targets that read the index, and the manifest no longer renders every code-only artifact a second time
pages.description: Make the second `majordomus generate` of scripts/derive render only the targets that depend on the index stage B rewrote (the site registry dataset, the benchmark matrix, the manifest). Build the manifest from the plan without rendering every code-only artifact again, and keep the result byte-identical to today's derive.

pages.title: I3234 — A derive whose executable is current and whose inputs did not move answers before it waits for the machine's lock
pages.description: Before scripts/derive takes the derive lock, choose the executable through I2525's generation guard and compare the node keys I2525 records for this tree, the site-data node included, without spawning a generator: no `majordomus generate`, no `generate --check`, no scripts/generate-site-data. If no key moved and no derive of this same worktree holds the lock, exit 0 and say so; otherwise take the lock and derive as today. The pre-lock answer runs a pinned copy of the executable, or one verified by content hash immediately before exec. scripts/site-deploy uses the same answer and stops running `cargo run ... generate --check`.

pages.title: I3235 — The site generator reads the use-case catalogue once per run
pages.description: Parse the use-case catalogue once in scripts/generate-site-data and hand the parsed form to every section that needs it, with output byte-identical.

pages.title: I3236 — Independent derive nodes run in bounded parallel against one snapshot, and the bytes do not depend on the order
pages.description: Run the graph's independent nodes concurrently up to a declared bound, honouring input, output and publication edges and exclusive resources (staging, local evidence). A clean full derive is the oracle.

pages.title: I3237 — A derive publishes its whole output set at once after validating it, and a killed derive leaves the previous set
pages.description: Compute every node into staging, validate the affected set as a whole, then publish. Detect inputs that changed during the run and refuse or retry. A run that dies mid-way leaves the tree as it was.

pages.title: I3238 — A pull request runs the cases its change can affect, chosen from what each case declares it reads, and a change of unknown impact runs them all
pages.description: Extend the existing `# majordomus-covers:` header with the paths a case reads (or derive them from the commands it covers and the feature-to-module map), and make scripts/ci-plan select suite cases from the changed paths' closure. A case that declares nothing runs on every pull request. The full suite runs on the combined top, on release and on demand.

pages.title: I3239 — One job builds a run's executable and every other job of that run uses it
pages.description: Build the debug executable once per validate run, upload it, and have suite-shard, evidence, ui, mesh-lab and the site jobs download it as MAJORDOMUS_BIN instead of running cargo build each. macOS keeps its own build.

pages.title: I3240 — A pull request's browser audit visits the pages its change can reach, and a shared-layout change sweeps them all
pages.description: Map each route to the templates, styles and scripts it renders from, and audit on a pull request only the routes whose inputs changed plus one representative per route class. Any change to the shared layout, CSS or JS escalates to the full sweep, which also runs on the combined top.

pages.title: I3241 — Only a job that reads history fetches all of it
pages.description: Declare in gates.yaml which gates read history, and give fetch-depth 0 only to the jobs that run one of them.

pages.title: I3242 — The pull-request critical path has a committed GitHub baseline and a budget per required job, and a run's summary names its critical path and every cache state
pages.description: First commit a GitHub baseline window of validate runs through scripts/ci-baseline, warm, partial and cold apart, and derive from it a budget per required pull-request job that sums to 300 s on the critical path, naming every job over its share. Extend integration.timings to p50, p90 and p95 over a declared window of past runs with queue wait reported apart, and have the /ui CI/CD timings panel draw the same values. Extend scripts/ci/summary with sccache statistics, the docker-image job's cache state and the run's critical path across jobs, each value read from the run and none typed in.

pages.title: I3244 — The generated Dockerfile copies every path crate cargo metadata names, so a new workspace crate needs no edit of the image
pages.description: Have render.rs read the local path dependencies of the package from `cargo metadata` and emit their manifests in the recipe and dependency stages and their sources in the build stage.

pages.title: I3245 — The image build's cold and warm durations and its context size are read from docker-image runs, and the deployment records say what is built today
pages.description: Record cold, warm and one-line-edit image build times and the build-context size from docker-image runs as evidence, and rewrite the stale current_state of I0911 and I0921.

pages.title: I3246 — The evidence half of a gap is drafted from the ledger, and a second draft at one commit is the same
pages.description: Revive I2217 from origin/chore/the-owner-packs-are-planned (ec37317fe7c, 2026-10-10, never landed): a read-only intents.draft_gap (`intent draft gap <intent>`) prints a majordomus.gap/v1 record whose criterion states are derived from the evidence at the presented commit, each observation citing the ledger execution or claim it read. Port the record byte-identical first, then update its current_state to master.

pages.title: I3247 — Work is drafted for each criterion nothing serves, under a key derived from the intent, the criterion and the gap, so a second draft drafts the same work
pages.description: Revive I2218 from origin/chore/the-owner-packs-are-planned (ec37317fe7c, 2026-10-10, never landed): intents.draft_plan prints one issue draft per criterion no live issue serves and the gap did not observe satisfied, plus one per gap work item naming no issue, each with serves, scope from the criterion's reference, acceptance naming the criterion's evidence and a draft key derived from (intent id, criterion id, gap kind).

pages.title: I3248 — A draft that drops or weakens a criterion of its intent is refused unless a recorded decision names the change
pages.description: Compare a draft against the intent revision it was drafted under; a draft whose criteria set or evidence kinds are narrower is refused naming the criterion, unless a decision record (majordomus decision) cites it.

pages.title: I3249 — A replan is bounded: past a declared budget of drafts without measurable progress it ends in a named state a person resolves
pages.description: Declare in .ai/repo/policy.yaml a replan budget (drafts per intent revision without a newly satisfied criterion); intents.draft_plan reports `human_needed` with the criteria that did not move once the budget is spent, and drafts nothing further.

pages.title: I3250 — Before drafting work the planner says whether a criterion is met, met but unproven, or unmet, and drafts proof-only work where only proof is missing
pages.description: Classify each criterion before drafting: met (current evidence), unproven (implementation reachable from its ref, evidence not_run or stale), unmet; an unproven criterion drafts one issue whose only scope is the evidence it lacks.

pages.title: I3251 — A desired outcome is briefed with what the repository already holds about it
pages.description: Revive I2206 from origin/chore/the-owner-packs-are-planned (ec37317fe7c, 2026-10-10, never landed): `intent draft brief <statement>` returns, read-only, the intents, criteria, milestones, issues, capabilities and rules whose records match the outcome, each with the reason it matched, before anything is proposed.

pages.title: I3252 — A draft plan is judged as if it were written, and only a checked draft is written, through one capability
pages.description: Revive I2205 and I2207 from origin/chore/the-owner-packs-are-planned (ec37317fe7c, 2026-10-10, never landed): intents.draft_check runs the plan and intent validators over a draft (intent, criteria, milestones, issues) in memory; intents.draft_write writes it as records only when the check passes, as one execution with a declared repository_mutation effect.

pages.title: I3253 — A proposal lists the values it left unresolved, and a draft that carries an invented threshold is refused
pages.description: Add an `unresolved` list (value, why it matters, who decides) to the intent proposal and draft; the draft check refuses a numeric threshold in a criterion that cites no measurement or decision.

pages.title: I3254 — A proposal names the existing intents and issues it duplicates or overlaps, and is merged into one rather than added beside it
pages.description: intents.propose and draft_check compare a new statement and its drafted issues with existing intents and issues (the brief of I3251) and return each likely duplicate with the shared terms; the proposal is refused as a duplicate unless the caller names the existing intent to amend or confirms novelty.

pages.title: I3255 — A command criterion is met only by a recorded passing run of exactly that command at the presented revision
pages.description: Revive I2222 and I2223 from origin/chore/the-owner-packs-are-planned (ec37317fe7c, 2026-10-10, never landed): a criterion with evidence command reads current from a ledger execution receipt of exactly its ref, passing, whose inputs did not change since; stale, failing or not_run otherwise; never current on an unexecuted, deleted, forged or wrong-target receipt.

pages.title: I3256 — A deployment criterion is met only by a recorded observation of that deployment serving a build that contains the criterion's newest change
pages.description: Revive I2221 (origin/chore/the-owner-packs-are-planned (ec37317fe7c, 2026-10-10, never landed)) and I2506 (origin/chore/seven-owner-packs-are-tracked-and-planned (689021d6ce2, 2026-10-15, never landed)): a deployment criterion reads current when a recorded observation of that deployment served a build containing the newest commit that changed the criterion's serving scope; unreachable, malformed or undecided observations never read current.

pages.title: I3257 — intent explain follows each served issue past its merge to the release and the observed deployment that carry it
pages.description: Revive I2507 from origin/chore/seven-owner-packs-are-tracked-and-planned (689021d6ce2, 2026-10-15, never landed): intent explain and the realization join continue from each served issue's merge to the release record and the deployment observation that carry it, with a gap named where one is missing.

pages.title: I3258 — Evidence for and against one criterion is kept and named, and the criterion reads unknown until it is settled
pages.description: When two current pieces of evidence for one criterion disagree (a passing test and a failing claim, two observations), the criterion keeps both with their sources and reads unknown with reason `conflicting`; nothing averages or drops one.

pages.title: I3259 — Where the policy says completed means complete, finish refuses completed while a criterion the task serves is unmet, and writes no intent state
pages.description: Revive milestone finish-reads-what-its-work-serves as a-finish-reads-the-criteria-its-work-serves from origin/rescue/d1/feature/a-finish-reads-what-its-work-serves (dabafa5740a, 2026-10-09): finish asks intents.binding and the verdict for the criteria the task serves and, where policy requires, refuses outcome completed while one is unmet; partial is always available and the refusal says so.

pages.title: I3260 — One intent is carried in a disposable repository from a sentence through a failing criterion to a satisfied verdict, across two providers and a handover
