pages.description: Revive I2545 (origin/chore/seven-owner-packs-are-tracked-and-planned (689021d6ce2, 2026-10-15, never landed)) and extend it: a case creates a fixture repository, proposes an intent from a sentence, drafts and writes its plan (I3252), runs part of the work in one provider session, hands over to a second, sees one criterion fail and the intent stay unsatisfied, drafts the remaining work (I3247), fixes it, and sees the verdict satisfied with the lineage explained, through capabilities only.

pages.title: I3261 — Every bypass of the intent loop is tried by a test and is refused or exempted by policy, never passed
pages.description: Revive I2224 and I2215 from origin/chore/the-owner-packs-are-planned (ec37317fe7c, 2026-10-10, never landed): a matrix test tries each named bypass — start with no binding, execution before critique, completion on green tests alone, satisfied from a closed issue, a GitHub edit changing intent state — and asserts refusal or a typed exemption.

pages.title: I3267 — One read-only evaluator says what accepting an issue would unblock, from plan.next's own readiness rules
pages.description: Add plan.impact: for hypothetical accepted issues, return direct and transitive dependents, immediate unlocks (issues that become READY), remaining blockers, milestone state changes and wave changes, with the graph fingerprint and source commit, computed by applying the readiness function of plan.rs to a copy of the plan.

pages.title: I3268 — The published plan has an impact page whose graph and sortable table agree and name the commit they were read at
pages.description: Generate /plan/impact/ on the site from plan.impact over every issue: a sortable, filterable table (id, milestone, wave, status, immediate unlocks, transitive reach, remaining blockers) and the graph via site/graph.js; row and node select each other; a no-JS table is the fallback.

pages.title: I3269 — Accepting several issues at once is previewed on the original graph, with shared unlocks counted once
pages.description: plan.impact accepts a set; the result reports unique new unlocks, overlap and remaining blockers, labelled hypothetical.

pages.title: I3270 — A blocked issue says which kind of block holds it: a dependency, contention, or a stale record
pages.description: plan.issues and plan.status classify each blocked issue: open dependency (named), environment or CI contention (a recorded refusal), or a stale planning record (a dependency done in fact but not recorded, from delivery inference).

pages.title: I3271 — plan.drift reports a source it could not observe as unknown, never as a drift finding
pages.description: Each drift finding names whether its evidence was observed (merged PR read, branch read) and a finding whose source was not read is classed unknown, counted separately.

pages.title: I3272 — A received brief is a campaign revision pinned by its manifest digest, and the same bytes again are the same revision
pages.description: Reconcile proposed ADR 0194 onto proposed ADR 0180's noun (campaign): 0194 cites 0180 and keeps only the reconciliation decision, or is withdrawn. A revision is a campaign under campaigns/ with its MANIFEST.sha256 digest, made a kind by I3167 and written by I3169's campaign add; prove through that command that the same bytes added twice change no byte, and rebind the criteria of a-brief-is-reconciled-into-the-plan to their tests. Gated on the owner accepting ADR 0180.

pages.title: I3273 — Each requirement of a campaign revision has a content-derived identity and is reconciled into the existing intents and issues
pages.description: Split a campaign revision into segments whose identity is the digest of their normalised text (document, heading path and position are only their location) and classify each against the existing intents and issues: existing from I3254's duplicates, satisfied or partial from the derived verdict, superseded from the matched record's stage or superseded_by, conflicting where it negates a matched invariant or non_goal (reported with both texts for a person), new otherwise. A conversation enters only as workspace references read from the local store. Output is a draft for I3252's check, never records.

pages.title: I3274 — A new campaign revision reports only the criteria whose source requirement changed
pages.description: Diff two revisions by segment digest (added, removed, modified as a removed digest paired with an added one at the same location) and report the criteria citing a removed or replaced digest; a rename or reorder moves no digest and reports nothing. The report changes no stored or derived state.

pages.title: I3275 — An intent's inspector shows the campaign segments it was derived from
pages.description: /ui/intent, /ui/idd, /cockpit's intents panel and intent explain show, for an intent and each issue, the campaign revision and segment references that produced it, drawn through I3283's provenance link as one more reference form of the shared Provenance definition (proposed ADR 0211); the published snapshot shows the references only.

pages.title: I3276 — The time from an intent's proposal to its verified satisfaction is derived from the records, with the interventions on the way
pages.description: Derive per intent: proposed_at (the author time of the commit that first added the intent record), the first commit at which every criterion reads current (from evidence-ledger receipts), elapsed time, replans (commits that change the intent's criteria or milestones or the issues serving them), interventions (each kind read from the record that holds it, or not_recorded), governance time and rework as docs/ECONOMICS.md defines them, and the windowed aggregate; thin data says thin (I0403).

pages.title: I3278 — The 2026-10-18 import is the workspace store's first sync, not a scratchpad
pages.description: Move the conversations captured on 2026-10-18 into .ai/local/workspaces/chatgpt-majordomus/ in the layout I1303 declares, as workspace-record/v1 records with transport, acquisition and support stated, and write the checkpoint a later sync resumes from.

pages.title: I3279 — The vendor's own data export is a transport, and it carries the message identities an in-page read did not keep
pages.description: Accept the ChatGPT account export archive as a second transport (acquisition: export) that the mapper of I1307 reads offline, keeping each message's upstream id, parent and position on the current branch.

pages.title: I3280 — An intent, a milestone and an issue carry provenance the way an ADR and a knowledge record do
pages.description: Give the intent, milestone and issue schemas an optional provenance header (origin, derived_from) like the ADR and knowledge schemas carry, with one reference grammar declared once and inlined by majordomus generate into each schema, each kind admitting its own declared subset, read by the plan model, so a promoted plan record can name where it came from.

pages.title: I3281 — A workspace message is a typed provenance reference that validates in every checkout without the store
pages.description: Add workspace:<workspace-id>/<conversation-id>#<message> to the shared Provenance reference grammar; validate it structurally against the tracked workspace declaration everywhere, accept a digits-only <message> as a positional reference flagged for pinning, and never consult .ai/local/ to decide validity.

pages.title: I3282 — A workspace reference resolves to its message where the store holds it, and says 'not held here' where it does not
pages.description: Resolve a workspace: reference through the one continuity-shaped workspaces capability (I1308) to the stored message, returning resolved, not-held-here or gone-upstream (tombstone), never failing a check because the store is absent.

pages.title: I3283 — The UI opens the message a record cites, and the published snapshot shows only the reference
pages.description: Draw every workspace: reference in a record's provenance as a link in /ui (through ui::prose) to a served, local-only message view, list on a conversation's view the records promoted from it, and render the reference as plain text in the published snapshot.

pages.title: I3284 — Every reference the 2026-10-18 import wrote is pinned to the upstream message it meant
pages.description: Rewrite each positional workspace reference in tracked records to the upstream message id, matching position in the 2026-10-18 flattening together with the message's time and a hash of its text, and refuse to pin any reference that matches zero or more than one message.

pages.title: I3285 — A vendor workspace reads the plan through the authenticated remote MCP surface, and a tunnel never makes it look local
pages.description: Let a ChatGPT custom connector call the read capabilities (plan, intents, evidence) over the existing MCP-over-HTTP projection, through a listener of its own whose callers authenticate by the mechanism an ADR amending ADR 0126 defines (ADR 0126 admits reads beyond loopback without authentication), and refuse any deployment where a tunnel terminating on loopback would make vendor requests pass as local.

pages.title: I3286 — A proposal from a workspace arrives as intent.propose carrying the workspace reference it came from
pages.description: Once the owner decides remote mutation (open question), accept intent.propose from an authenticated vendor caller with a minimal structured delta (statement, criteria, workspace reference), never a transcript, under an autonomy-per-work-class policy declared as data.

pages.title: I3287 — A provider declares how it reports usage, with the evidence, beside its lifecycle
pages.description: Extend share/providers.yaml `offers` with `usage` (otel | app-server | stream-json | none) and `usage_evidence`, so discovery, normalisation, tests and surfaces read one declaration instead of a ClaudeTelemetry/CodexTelemetry/GeminiTelemetry subsystem.

pages.title: I3288 — The shared server receives Claude Code's OpenTelemetry usage events over loopback and records them as reported
pages.description: Accept OTLP over HTTP with JSON encoding (no protobuf, no new dependency) on the shared server's loopback listener, and map claude_code.api_request events into a new economics usage record (an optional value per token category plus an absence reason, distinct from execution::Execution) through a lossless adapter over the existing economics::usage normalisers, keeping input, output, cache-read and cache-write tokens separate and storing numbers and names only.

pages.title: I3289 — Turning usage collection on is a dry-run plan the person consents to, never a committed repository setting
pages.description: Generate the minimal client configuration that points a client's telemetry at the shared server (for Claude Code the CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY and OTEL_* environment), print it on --dry-run, and apply it only with consent: launcher-scoped by default with OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES naming the repository and checkout, keeping existing user settings; a persistent user-level endpoint waits until a stable receiver is declared.

pages.title: I3290 — Codex usage is read from app-server increments, and a cumulative total is never summed
pages.description: Map Codex app-server thread/tokenUsage/updated notifications into the same record, adding last-increment values only, cross-checking against total_token_usage, and recording a session as incomplete when turn completion arrives without a final total.

pages.title: I3291 — Gemini CLI usage events map onto the same record, thought tokens included
pages.description: Map gemini_cli.api_response (input, output, cached-content, thought tokens) through the receiver of I3288 with no Gemini-specific path beyond the mapping table.

pages.title: I3292 — Reported tokens, a price-list estimate and a billed amount are three fields, and the billing mode says which account paid
pages.description: Give the usage record of I3288 reported_tokens, estimated_cost (class estimated) and billed_cost (absent unless reconciled), plus billing_mode (subscription, api_key, api_credits, unknown) declared by the person, so that on a subscription an API-equivalent price is never shown as spend.

pages.title: I3293 — Usage is attributed to the session, task and issue it was spent on, from records the repository already keeps
pages.description: Join a usage record's provider session id to the session record (ADR 0164), its active task and the task's issue and intent at read time, storing no join, and report unattributed usage as such.

pages.title: I3294 — /ui shows usage by provider, model, session, task and issue, and every figure opens its reported events
pages.description: Extend the observatory's Token Spectrum scene on /ui, read only from the economics capabilities, to group usage by provider, model, session, task and issue, each figure naming its class and age and linking to the events it sums.

pages.title: I3295 — A task declared over its token budget is told so, and refused only where policy says refuse
pages.description: Declare per-profile token and cost budgets as data in policy, have finish and the brief compare a task's attributed usage with them, and say which figure (reported or estimated) the judgement read.

pages.title: I3296 — Each compaction is measured: the context before and after, from the provider's report
pages.description: Record pre- and post-compaction token counts from the provider's own events (PreCompact/PostCompact and the compaction telemetry) against the episode, and derive the ratio and the time to the next compaction.

pages.title: I3297 — A waste finding names its evidence and confidence and is never presented as a saving
pages.description: Derive findings (low cache-read share, oversized tool results, repeated tool calls, an expensive model on routine work, subagent cost without an accepted outcome) from attributed usage, each with the events behind it, a confidence and an estimated effect labelled counterfactual.

pages.title: I3298 — The benchmark declares one arm per mechanism and per agent topology, and a short-task hypothesis beside the long-work one
pages.description: Extend .ai/repo/benchmarks/economics/methodology.yaml with treatment arms that isolate context compilation, handover, skills and single-agent versus architect-plus-workers, and record the hypothesis that a short isolated task gains little or loses, so a later total can be explained by parts.

pages.title: I3299 — Majordomus's own overhead in an adopting repository is measured per operation against declared budgets
pages.description: Declare budgets for CLI start, warm discovery, idle server CPU and resident memory, incremental derive, and the bootstrap tokens a session pays, measure them in an adopting fixture repository with the existing bench, and fail when one is exceeded.

pages.title: I3300 — Majordomus installs into Claude Code as one generated plugin carrying its skills, hooks, mods and MCP server
pages.description: Generate one plugin bundle from the registry (the skills editors/claude.rs projects, the capture and edit-guard hooks, the two mods under share/mods/claude-code, the MCP server entry), stamped with its source digest and the Claude Code version it was verified against, replacing hand-assembled pieces.

pages.title: I3301 — A Claude Code session that stops with an active task is told what the task still owes
pages.description: Wire the provider's Stop event to a generated shim that reads the active task's owed obligations from the running shared server's obligations capability and reports them, never blocking a stop.

pages.title: I3302 — An installed plugin or mod that differs from what the repository generated is a doctor finding
pages.description: Extend the existing installed-versus-source comparisons with each generated extension's digest, version and declared permissions, and report an unknown or drifted active extension in doctor and /ui.

pages.title: I3303 — Codex's hooks draw its episodes and refuse an edit no claim covers, as Claude Code's do
pages.description: Write the Codex adapter share/providers.yaml calls `unadapted`: session events to capture session and, where Codex offers a pre-tool event, that event to guard hook --provider codex, generated like the Claude shims, with its offers evidence verified against the installed Codex.

pages.title: I3304 — A prompt reaches the model within a declared capture budget, and no captured record is lost
pages.description: Declare a latency budget for the UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart hooks in benchmark policy, meet it by handing the capture to the running shared server (or a durable outbox) instead of a cold executable start, and prove no record is lost.

pages.title: I3305 — A scripted capability installed from outside the repository registers like one inside it
pages.description: Discover scripted-capability packages from a declared install location outside the tree and hand them to the registration I3157 proves, so they reach CLI, MCP and HTTP with their origin and no second registration.

pages.title: I3306 — An external scripted capability runs under default-deny grants, bounded, and leaves an audit record
pages.description: Give external packages explicit grants for file, environment, network and process access on top of I1800's sandbox and time bound, quarantine a package after repeated severe failures, and record each privileged action.

pages.title: I3307 — The default MCP tools/list stays within a declared byte budget, and a full schema is fetched per tool
pages.description: Declare a byte budget for the default tools/list, carry compact descriptions and no output schemas in it, serve the full schema per tool on demand, and fail a gate when the listing exceeds the budget.

pages.title: I3308 — Zed validates and completes .ai files against the repository's own schemas
pages.description: Project YAML and JSON schema associations from share/schemas onto .zed/settings.json through the existing Zed adapter, so .ai records get validation and hover in the editor.

pages.title: I3309 — A fix finishes completed only with a named regression case that fails on the task's base and passes on its head
pages.description: For a task started under the debugging profile, finish --outcome completed runs the regression case the task names twice: at the task's base commit (in a disposable worktree, with only the case file applied) where it must fail, and at the head where it must pass. The completed note of such a task carries a Root Cause section naming the observed failure, the mechanism and the violated invariant. The check is a typed Rust capability the finish validator calls, so no domain-logic shell is added.

pages.title: I3310 — majordomus start refuses a task, owner or reason that the task record cannot hold, and writes nothing
pages.description: Refuse at entry, with a usage exit and no write, any task description, --owner or --because value that is multi-line, carries a control character, or would not round-trip through the layer's YAML reader; adr propose, decision add, knowledge observe and question add/resolve already refuse multi-line text through mj_is_multiline.

pages.title: I3311 — Generated sequences of episode events never move an episode in a way its transition table forbids
pages.description: Add proptest harnesses over session::state and session::store: random sequences of open, checkpoint, handover, close, duplicate close, reconnect and recovery keep every invariant of EpisodeState::may_move_to, a closed episode is never active again without an explicit resume, and a record round-trips through its serialisation.

pages.title: I3312 — An ADR may name the paths it governs, and the compiled context for those paths includes it
pages.description: Let an ADR header carry tracks: the pathspecs it decides about, with the same meaning a context document's tracks has (docs/CONTEXT.md); devcontext selects an accepted or proposed ADR whose tracks match the request's path, and says that tracks is why it is in.

pages.title: I3313 — A failing verification in a closed session record says whether the ledger already held it failing at the task's base
pages.description: When finish or close records a failing verification, look the failing subject up in the evidence ledger at the task's base commit and mark it pre-existing (failing there), introduced (passing there) or unknown (not recorded there); the resume context lists pre-existing failures so the next worker does not diagnose them again.

pages.title: I3314 — An object's read names the commit that last changed its file, and its page lists the commits that changed it
pages.description: Add a read-only history projection to an object of the layer: the last commit, its date and the commits that touched the object's file (git log --follow, bounded), served on the entity read and its detail page, and computed from git rather than stored.

pages.title: I3315 — The image smoke completes an MCP initialize on /mcp and a WebSocket upgrade on /events, not only a ready probe
pages.description: Extend the one image smoke definition so that the container it judges answers a protocol-level MCP initialize on /mcp and upgrades a WebSocket on /events, completes a minimal exchange and closes cleanly, in docker-image.yml and release.yml alike.

pages.title: I3316 — The rescue command a stranded worktree is offered is proved by a drill that restores its work byte-identical
pages.description: Add a drill that builds a fixture worktree with staged, unstaged, untracked, stashed and detached-HEAD work, runs the rescue command worktree uncommitted suggests, removes the worktree, restores from the rescue ref and compares the result, and fix the command where the drill shows it loses or moves work.

pages.title: I3317 — An execution records the commit it started at, and a writing execution the paths it changed
pages.description: Stamp every execution with the commit HEAD named and whether the tree was clean when it started; for a capability whose declared effect writes the repository, also record the commit at its end and the tracked paths that changed between the two, so a person can see what a run changed and rerun it against the revision it ran on.

pages.title: I3318 — Every decision and curated note is read on /ui, with the records it names and the records that name it
pages.description: Give /ui one screen for decisions (adr kind) and one for curated knowledge, each list and inspector projected from the index the objects API already serves, with an inspector showing the record's related/relations as links and the reverse edges (which issues, milestones, intents and notes name it) derived from the same index.

pages.title: I3319 — No record names a repository a design was studied in
pages.description: Remove from adr-0017 and its site projection the names of the two repositories its design was studied in, keeping the decision's content, and make a check refuse, in any tracked file, every token of a declared forbidden list: the name of the studied repository that no tracked file needs. The owner's own adopter repository, the other one adr-0017 names, is not on the list, because tracked files name it as the adopter (the independence check, cases 569 and 3017, the import pack, I3129 and the curated note an-adopters-work-never-waits-for-majordomus), not as the source of a design; adr-0017 is the only file that names it as a design source, and that is what this issue removes.

pages.title: I3320 — A lifecycle command run against an absent or stale executable fails loudly and never falls back to a shell writer
pages.description: Give the lifecycle commands (session open and close, the provider event shims, checkpoint and handover) one resolution of the Rust executable with a declared lifecycle contract version: with no resolvable executable, or one older than the tree's contract, the command writes a typed provider.event.failed naming the cause, leaves the episode open, exits non-zero (the hook shims stay fail-open for the provider), and nothing falls back to a shell writer.

pages.title: I3321 — In a foreign repository, the wired pre-push hook of the claude-code projection refuses what finish would refuse, through the installed release
pages.description: Add to install-check's first-run stage a step in which the refusal is reached through the pre-push hook (finish --check) that the claude-code projection wires in the foreign fixture repository, so the refusal is shown to arrive on the path an agent's session takes, not only through commands the stage calls itself.

pages.title: I3322 — capture install wires the edit guard into Claude Code's PreToolUse, first in an advisory mode, and doctor reports it unwired
pages.description: Have capture install write the Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit PreToolUse entry for .claude/hooks/majordomus-edit-guard into .claude/settings.json, extend the lifecycle wiring check to it, declare an advisory mode in policy that reports an unclaimed edit without refusing it, and correct docs/MESH.md.

pages.title: I3323 — An unclaimed edit is refused in Claude Code once no live peer edits without a claim
pages.description: Switch the edit guard from advisory to refusing through .ai/repo/policy.yaml once the claim-coverage report of I3322 shows no live peer editing without a claim, and prove an unclaimed edit is refused through the generated Claude Code configuration.

pages.title: I3324 — After every deploy the published homepage's hero choices are probed and found reachable
pages.description: Extend scripts/pages verify --smoke so that, after a deploy, it reads the hero choices the published homepage offers and requests each one, failing when a choice's page is absent, with no route list kept by hand; no site feature is added.

pages.title: I3350 — The homepage copy may not use a word of delivered value until a claim permits it
pages.description: Add the value words the proof tests would settle to the [promises] table of site/data/homepage.toml, each mapped to the empty claim id, so scripts/ci/homepage-check refuses each in site/data/marketing.toml and site/data/manifesto.toml until a claim permits it: faster, cheaper, fewer interventions, less human effort, less effort, fewer reruns, saves time, more reliable, speeds up, speed-up, recovers without loss, pays for itself. Extend the table's comment to say the words wait for the proof scorecard's tests.

pages.title: I3351 — A proof plan is a validated record in which each protocol is frozen by its own digest, so registering one test never stales another's records
pages.description: Add apps/majordomus-cli/src/economics/proof.rs, declared from mod.rs, which loads and validates .ai/repo/benchmarks/proof-plan.yaml (schema proof-plan/v1): tests with id, title, question, settles (docs/CLAIMS.yaml ids), dimension (accepted_results, wall_time, human_interventions, ci_reruns, spend, recovery, onboarding), value_words, instrument (built, or planned with the issue ids that build it) and an optional protocol. A protocol has version, registered_at, changes and a decision of one of three kinds: paired (names an economics suite and the digest of that suite's registration block), trials (record fields with their classes, min_trials, min_successes, all_must_pass) or window (period, admitted work, a bound per field on its not-observed share). Each protocol carries registered_digest over its own canonical form, computed by one public digest function the suite registration also uses. The validator refuses a digest mismatch, an unknown dimension or decision kind, a duplicate id, a claim CLAIMS.yaml lacks, a paired protocol whose suite or registration digest does not resolve, and a version without a changes entry. Expose counts_toward(record, test): a record counts only when it carries its test's protocol digest and postdates registered_at. The plan file is a freshness input of no suite.

pages.title: I3353 — A trial is a typed record that carries its protocol's digest, refuses what the protocol does not declare, and redacts what its publication basis does not permit

When the basis is none, the loader refuses a repository name, a raw commit id (a salted digest is required), a path (only declared path classes) and any free-text field. The loader also refuses a missing declared field, an estimated or counterfactual number and an unknown test. Records whose digest or time does not count are kept and listed with their reason.

pages.description: Write .ai/repo/workflows/first-intent-trial.md (who counts as a newcomer: a developer who has not contributed to Majordomus; invitation and consent; the observer's rule of no help; the fields) and register the T6 trials protocol in the proof plan: fields reached_satisfied_verdict, seconds, commands_beyond_page, documents_beyond_page, observer_interventions, tool version, platform, agent; min_trials and min_successes from an owner decision; success requires zero interventions; redaction under I3353's rules. Link the workflow from .ai/repo/workflows/README.md.

pages.title: I3399 — Newcomer trials are run as the protocol declares, recorded as they happened, and the T6 verdict is published with every trial
pages.description: With each newcomer's consent, observe the registered number of trials without helping, record each as the newcomer reports and the observer measures under .ai/repo/benchmarks/trials/t6-first-intent/, cite each friction in an issue or a cancellation as I3365 does for T1, regenerate the economics projections and let the T6 row compute its status.

pages.title: I3400 — The decompose-a-brief skill exists, is invoked by the plan workflow, and is named by both skill tests, so skills verify holds it as a capability
pages.description: Add .ai/repo/skills/decompose-a-brief/SKILL.md (skill/v1) with the procedure given in this program: open the run and claim identities, keep the paste in one canonical byte form as a campaign (or as a reference, or ask, for a conversation or an AI assistant's answer), classify every item, map each requirement to the existing plan before drafting, draft only what is new, have the draft critiqued by a reviewer that did not write it, resolve the findings, derive and validate, deliver, and offer the first wave on the mesh without claiming its scope. Invoke it from .ai/repo/workflows/plan.md, add its id to the majordomus-skill marker lines of apps/majordomus-cli/tests/skills.rs and test/cases/391_skills_are_proven_capabilities.sh, and regenerate its projections.

pages.title: I3401 — intents.propose writes no record for a multi-paragraph, Markdown or over-length statement and answers invalid_input, naming the canonical digest and the skill that decomposes it
pages.description: Add a pure function in apps/majordomus-cli/src/intent.rs that says whether a trimmed statement is a brief: it holds a blank line between two non-blank lines, a line that opens a Markdown block (heading, list item, table row, code fence, block quote), or its canonical text exceeds a named constant bound. The canonical text is the statement with leading and trailing whitespace removed followed by exactly one line feed. The bound is the smallest power of two above the longest statement of a tracked intent on the issue's base (the longest statement line on 9904000d2df measures 846 bytes, so 1024 unless the base measures otherwise), stated in ADR 0144 with the command that measured it. propose() returns ProposeError::Invalid before any file is touched, with a message naming majordomus://skill/decompose-a-brief, the canonical text's byte length and sha256:<hex> of its UTF-8 bytes. Extend the Invalid variant's doc to cover a brief. Update the capability description, the intents README and the cli.rs example text, amend ADR 0144, and regenerate the projections.

pages.title: I3402 — The /intent alias follows the skill an unsuccessful answer names instead of stopping at it or retrying with altered text
pages.description: Change the generated command-alias text in apps/majordomus-cli/src/editors/claude.rs for a capability that changes something. When an unsuccessful answer names majordomus://skill/<id>, the alias reads that skill with majordomus skills show <id> or the MCP resource majordomus://skill/<id> and follows it with the same text. Any other refusal, or an unknown outcome, is reported as it is, keeping the pinned phrase 'do not try again by another way'. The alias never calls the capability again with shortened or rewritten text. Regenerate .claude/skills/intent/SKILL.md and document the rule in docs/EDITORS.md.

pages.title: I3403 — The Cockpit runner, the execution form and the intent workspace show an answer that names a skill as one link to that skill, proven in the existing browser case
pages.description: In share/cockpit/runner.js (show) and share/cockpit/executions.js (report), when an unsuccessful answer's message names majordomus://skill/<id>, append after the text a link to /ui/skills#skill-<id>; the message stays textContent and the link is built with createElement, never innerHTML. Change the no-intent hint at apps/majordomus-cli/src/ui/idd.rs:292 to say that a one-paragraph statement is proposed and a longer paste is decomposed by the skill, with a link to the same anchor. Extend the existing browser case test/cases/3220_the_idd_loop_is_walked_in_a_browser.sh with a step that submits a two-paragraph statement to /cockpit/capabilities/intents.propose and checks the link.

pages.title: I3404 — A decomposition of a synthetic brief in the skill's output shape is held valid by a test, its digest agrees with the refusal, and an unserved criterion in it is caught
pages.description: Run decompose-a-brief once, in a disposable checkout, over a synthetic English Markdown brief with three headings, one requirement that an existing fixture criterion already carries, two new requirements and one opinion. Commit what it wrote inline in apps/majordomus-cli/tests/intent_plan.rs, labelled with the skill version that produced it: the campaign file in canonical byte form with its manifest line and README row, one intent with two criteria, one milestone and two issues. Mark the file with majordomus-skill: decompose-a-brief. The test writes them into a Fixture repository and asserts: intents.propose refuses the brief with a digest and byte length equal to the campaign file's; plan validate and intent validate report zero failures; scripts/ci/campaigns-check is clean; intent coverage shows both new criteria served; plan waves lists at least one first-wave issue; every new record names the campaign; the reused requirement adds no criterion; deleting the serving issue makes intent coverage report the criterion unserved.

pages.title: I3405 — Every generated model-invocable domain skill follows the skill an unsuccessful answer names, so the MCP path does not end at a refused paste
pages.description: Put the rule I3402 gives the alias into the generic domain-skill text at apps/majordomus-cli/src/editors/claude.rs:179: an unsuccessful answer of a capability that changes something, when it names majordomus://skill/<id>, is followed by reading that skill (majordomus skills show <id> or majordomus://skill/<id>) with the same text; the capability is never called again with altered text; any other refusal is reported as it is. Reuse the sentence I3402 introduced rather than writing it twice, regenerate the 58 .claude/skills/mj-*/SKILL.md projections and extend docs/EDITORS.md.

pages.title: I3406 — A prompt delivered again, concurrently, on the next day or after a resumed session is still one record, and capture status counts every identity that more than one record holds
pages.description: Key prompt-capture idempotence on provider plus provider prompt id. Take the existing mj_lock_take (lib/common.sh:1406) around the check-then-write, under a lock path derived from that key, so that concurrent deliveries converge. Check the record's UTC day and the day before, so the hook scans at most two day-globs. Write a payload whose key is known but whose text differs, and count it as a key collision. Make capture status report, over the whole archive and off the hook path, the identities more than one record holds and the key collisions. Delete no record.

pages.title: I3407 — What a set of paths affects in the plan is derived from the index: the issues whose scope covers them, what those issues serve and their incoming edges, each with its relation, and nothing is rescanned
pages.description: Add a read-only capability, entity.affected, to the existing entity module. Given repository paths, it answers the entities they touch, each with a reason: the issues whose scope covers a path (reusing intent_binding's covers), the milestones and intents those issues serve, and the incoming entity edges of each reached object. Depth (default 2) and count (default 500) are declared inputs, so a test can drive both past their bounds. The order is canonical, and a path that nothing names is answered as unaffected rather than omitted.

pages.title: I3408 — A captured prompt is answered, on this machine only, with the existing intents and issues it matches or with no match, and the answer carries identities and never the prompt's text
pages.description: Add a read-only capability, intents.matched, that declares the checkout-private field I3434 adds. Given a captured prompt's identity (provider and prompt id) or an episode, it reads the record from .ai/local/prompts and runs the I3251 brief over its text through a new matcher in apps/majordomus-cli/src/devcontext/intent_match.rs. It answers each existing intent and issue above the floor with the shared title terms and a confidence. The verdict is matched (one candidate), ambiguous (several, all kept as candidates) or unmatched. It never proposes an intent, never calls a model and never acts on the text.

pages.title: I3409 — An episode answers, for each prompt it captured, the intent it matched, the task that recorded it, that task's outcome and the evidence of the criterion it serves, with the same identities on every surface and after any replay
pages.description: Extend intents.matched with an episode mode that derives the vertical slice on read. For each prompt the episode captured, it answers six things. First, the prompt identity and the match verdict. Second, the task whose task.started names that prompt (I3411), labelled recorded; for a line without the key it answers the next task the episode started, labelled inferred. Third, that task's bound issue and intent from task.started and intents.binding. Fourth, its task.finished outcome and verify command, from the recorded contract. Fifth, the evidence state of the criterion the issue serves, from intent_realization. Sixth, an agreement verdict: agrees, differs or no task. The live intent inspector lists the open episodes' prompts that matched the intent, by identity only. It re-reads on the frame I3431 emits, and to a viewer beyond loopback it says the list is answered on this machine only.

pages.title: I3410 — A Codex prompt is captured through Codex's own UserPromptSubmit hook, and capture status stops calling Codex prompts unadapted
pages.description: Add a codex line to MJ_CAPTURE_ADAPTERS that reads Codex's prompt field, with the shim and config entry capture install writes, in the way it writes the Claude one. Before building, re-verify the dated vendor evidence in share/providers.yaml against the installed Codex.

pages.title: I3411 — A task records the captured prompt it followed, so the join from prompt to task is a recorded fact rather than a time adjacency
pages.description: When majordomus start writes task.started (lib/start.sh:158), add an optional prompt key. It holds the provider and provider prompt id of the newest capture record that the starting episode captured before the start. The record is found through a helper in lib/capture.sh over the same two day-globs I3406 bounds. Write no key when the episode captured nothing, and never any prompt text. Document the optional key in share/events.yaml's note for task.started, and leave requires unchanged.

pages.title: I3412 — entity.affected also answers the rules, claims and knowledge records whose declared references name an affected path or issue, and takes a revision range
pages.description: Extend entity.affected with two relations: the rules, claims and knowledge records whose declared references (file:, issue:) name an input path or a reached issue, read from the references the index already holds; and a revision range, whose changed paths come from git and give the same answer as those paths passed directly. This is the reader I3414 and I3430 use, so no second derivation of the same backlinks is written.

pages.title: I3413 — A decision, resolved question or verified task fact already curated or pending from another episode of this checkout is not proposed again, and derive names the record it matched
pages.description: In mj_knowledge_derive_cmd, before writing a decision, question or task row, compare its evidence digest (the twelve hex characters after the episode in the record id) with the file names under curated/, candidates/ and this checkout's outbox. This is a directory listing; no record is read. A match under another id skips the row and reports it, in text and JSON, as a duplicate of the matched record's id. Observation rows are never skipped this way, because their recurrence is the signal that case 981 and I3165 count. Rejected subjects stay with I3164. knowledge check reports two records that share a digest as a WARN.

pages.title: I3414 — Every candidate group names the curated notes and the rule that already speak about its subject, read from entity.affected, so a possible duplicate or contradiction is in front of the reviewer with both sources
pages.description: Add a related list to each candidate group in the Rust knowledge_base.candidates reader and on /ui/knowledge. It is computed on read and never written into a candidate. It lists the curated notes that entity.affected (I3412) reaches from the group's subject path and, for a subject that is a rule, the rule's path. The shell reader is unchanged, and case 981's parity normalisation leaves related out. Step 2 of the evolve skill tells the reviewer to read related, and to reject with --by naming the curated note when a candidate duplicates it.

pages.title: I3415 — knowledge promote refuses evidence that names no reference existing in this checkout, and knowledge.promoted records the references it stood on
pages.description: Require the promote evidence on stdin to contain at least one typed reference (file:, test:, commit:, issue:, claim:, knowledge:, rule: or adr:) that resolves through the existing resolver (mj_knowledge_resolve_refs, lib/knowledge.sh:1832). Otherwise refuse with exit 10 and write nothing. Add the resolved references to the knowledge.promoted ledger line as an evidence array declared in share/events.yaml. Update the documented examples and the fixtures that promote with prose. A reference that resolves exists; it is not proof, and the promoted record reads as decided.

pages.title: I3416 — The episode boundary is proven to give one candidate for an observation recorded twice, none for a partial task, and one file per episode when two episodes close at once
pages.description: Extend the idempotency case so that it proves three behaviours the deriver has by construction and no case asserts. An identical observation recorded twice in one episode derives one file. A task finished partial yields no candidate, while knowledge.derived is still written. Two episodes of one checkout closing concurrently each write their own candidate once, knowledge check passes, and no staging file is left.

pages.title: I3417 — An observation can cite the mesh review that found what it records, and the reference stays in the candidate's body, never in its provenance
pages.description: Accept a review: reference carrying a mesh review request key among the evidence references of knowledge observe. The compose step keeps it in the candidate's Evidence body and never in provenance.derived_from, because a mesh review key does not resolve in every checkout. Document it in step 1 of the evolve skill.

pages.title: I3418 — Every advisor consultation records the model that answered, the source it came through and the session that asked
pages.description: Add to the consultation record the model the transport actually used, or its absence with a reason, and the adapter and vendor or peer runtime it came through. Add to the reasoning record envelope the session id of the writer. Every inference a decision rests on is then attributable.

pages.title: I3419 — A conclusion's independent review count counts distinct sources, defined as adapter plus recorded model, so two answers from one source are one review
pages.description: Define a source as the adapter plus the recorded model. A mesh-review consultation that reported no model counts as the adapter plus the answering peer runtime, and any other consultation without a model counts as the adapter alone. Compute independent_review_count and the task totals' independent reviewers from distinct sources instead of distinct advisor ids, and list the sources a conclusion was reviewed by.

pages.title: I3420 — A mesh peer asked for critique receives the question and its evidence, and its answer is recorded with the session that gave it
pages.description: Have the mesh-review adapter send the bounded, scrubbed question the driver built as the review request body, within the mesh's body bound. The question holds the hypothesis and prior opinions marked as opinions, the evidence references and the request for a falsifier. Return the answering session as the consultation's source.

pages.title: I3421 — A reasoning plan over the task's declared token or time budget consults nobody and says that the budget decided
pages.description: Make reasoning.plan read the per-profile token budget that I3295 declares in policy, and a wall-time cap for consultation. Count the task's reported consultation tokens against the budget. When it is spent, plan the structured local review with reason budget_exhausted, naming the budget, the figure and its class.

pages.title: I3422 — Advisor consultations are economics usage with their measurement class, and a consultation over its plan's budget is a finding
pages.description: Read each consultation's reported usage, model, latency and outcome into the economics usage record as reported tokens, with no invented cost and absent where the transport reported nothing. Report a consultation whose reported tokens exceed its plan's budget as an economics check finding.

pages.title: I3423 — docs/REASONING.md maps the pack's routing levels onto the existing plan outcomes and modes, and a test fails when an outcome is missing from that mapping
pages.description: Document the pack's four routing levels (deterministic, cheap local, reasoning peer, multi-peer critique) in docs/REASONING.md as a mapping onto the existing PlanOutcome values and modes, and name the level that has no producer today. Add a unit test in policy.rs that fails when a PlanOutcome variant is absent from the mapping table. Add no field, no setting and no noun.

pages.title: I3424 — No inference transport is reachable from the shell closure of any declared hook command, and reasoning check refuses one that is
pages.description: Add a hooks check to reasoning check that derives the hook closure. It starts from each hook command share/providers.yaml declares and the shims under .claude/hooks, takes the majordomus subcommand each shim runs, and follows the lib/ shell units that subcommand sources. It refuses a closure that names scripts/advisor-consult, scripts/lib/advisors or scripts/lib/inference. The check lists any Rust capability a hook subcommand reaches as outside its closure, so the limit is stated rather than hidden. A person-invoked consultation outside the closure is not refused.

pages.title: I3425 — A standing conclusion is reused only while the files it cites are unchanged since it was recorded
pages.description: Before reusing a prior conclusion on the same subject, compare each file evidence reference it cites, at the conclusion's recorded head, with the current tree, and check an optional declared age window. When a cited file has changed or the window has passed, plan review again and name the evidence that moved.

pages.title: I3426 — An advisor answer carrying instructions or record-shaped fields is kept as bounded text and changes no record
pages.description: Add two negative fixtures. The first is an answer that tells the executor to ignore governance or promote candidates. The second is an answer that carries status, verified, reviewed_by or independent_review_count fields. Both are normalised to the declared consultation fields only and bounded, and the writer refuses any extra field a caller forwards.

pages.title: I3427 — Every entity read names how its record says it is known, and never answers verified itself: proof stays the pointer it is
pages.description: Add an epistemic field holding class and basis to EntityView. One pure function in apps/majordomus-cli/src/entity.rs reads it from the record's own fields. A candidate or proposed status gives proposed. A superseded status or superseded_by gives superseded. Knowledge epistemics inferred gives inferred, and a generated projection gives derived. Anything else is observed. The function never computes verified: an object with a proof keeps the existing ProofRef pointer (entity.rs:181-185), and a surface shows verified only from that capability's answer. docs/SURFACES.md states the vocabulary once, with each older vocabulary's mapping, as the proposed ADR decides.

pages.title: I3428 — An entity read carries the observation envelope repository.info already answers, plus the blob of its file, and a change to that file moves both
pages.description: Add to EntityView the observed envelope that repository.info already carries: observed.index with observed_at and stale_after, from the index observation crate::live takes. Add the blob of the object's file from the git index, beside the last-changing commit I3314 adds. A member of a collection file names the file it is read from. Introduce no new freshness type.

pages.title: I3429 — One entity reads the same on the command line, REST, MCP and the Cockpit: identity, kind, class, evidence, observation envelope and edge order
pages.description: Extend the Cockpit integration test with one test that reads four surfaces for one entity of every kind the index holds: majordomus entity show as JSON, GET /api/v1/entity, majordomus_entity over MCP and the Cockpit entity page model. It compares uri, id, kind, epistemic class, evidence state, the observed envelope and the order of relations.

pages.title: I3430 — The IDD standing panel and the Cockpit intent page show, under each criterion, the knowledge that bears on it, each with how it is known
pages.description: Extend the standing panel I2789 landed on /ui/idd (apps/majordomus-cli/src/ui/idd.rs) instead of adding a screen. Under each criterion it already lists with its evidence state and serving issues, list the knowledge records that entity.affected reaches from those issues' scope paths and from the issues themselves (I3407, I3412), each with the epistemic class entity.show answers (I3427). Render the same rows on the Cockpit intent page (cockpit/intents.rs), each linked to its object route. The panel re-reads on the frame I3431 emits. No new route, navigation area or dashboard.

pages.title: I3431 — A record a process outside the server writes (a knowledge record reaching the index, a ledger line or a captured prompt) reaches an open view within one heartbeat, without a reload
pages.description: On the 20 s heartbeat the live channel already runs (http/events.rs:70), take crate::live's repository stamp and the stamps of the ledger file and of today's capture directory: three stats per heartbeat, never one per object. When a stamp has moved, emit the frame I3220 defines, carrying the kinds that changed and no content. A knowledge record that the session-end hook wrote, once a commit or git add has brought it into the index, a task.started line, and a captured prompt then all reach open views. Wake followers through crate::change::Generation from feature/the-blackboard-is-pushed once that branch lands, rather than through a second wake mechanism. A woken reader writes nothing, so no frame can cause another.

pages.title: I3432 — The UI and Cockpit snapshots pass both privacy gates after they are placed and before anything is published, on CI and from a terminal
pages.description: In .github/workflows/pages.yml, after the steps that place every snapshot at its mount and before the publish step, run scripts/ci/local-never-published --no-probe and scripts/ci/prompt-privacy over the composed site/public tree. Run the same two gates in scripts/site-deploy before it pushes, including under --skip-build. Extend case 181 to assert the order.

pages.title: I3433 — A UI snapshot page renders only the readings its subject declares publishable, and a page that reads any other reading, or a capability that refuses remote callers, is withheld with a link to the live page
pages.description: Give the UI snapshot subject a declared list of the capability readings it may publish, checked where pages take their readings (ui/source.rs, ui/view.rs through capability/readings.rs). A page that reads a capability outside the list, or one that declares I3434's checkout-private field, is withheld exactly as /cockpit/continuity is today.

pages.title: I3434 — A capability declared as reading checkout-private records answers only this machine: a caller beyond loopback is refused on HTTP and MCP, and the refusal logs no input value
pages.description: Add one declared field to the existing ExecutionPolicy (apps/majordomus-cli/src/capability/model.rs, beside signed_input at :597) saying that the capability reads checkout-private records. admits_remote (model.rs:708) answers false for it, so two existing paths refuse it with the existing remote error: the router's refusal (http/router.rs:1028) and MCP's remote flag (mcp/protocol.rs:131, :297). Prove it with a fixture capability in tests/remote_callers.rs.

pages.title: I3435 — A Cockpit snapshot withholds every page that reads a capability refusing remote callers, not only the continuity page it names
pages.description: Replace the Cockpit subject's single-route list (snapshot.rs:111-114) with the same check I3433 gives the UI subject. The check takes the readings each Cockpit page declares in cockpit/pages.rs and withholds a page that reads an unlisted capability or one that declares I3434's checkout-private field. /cockpit/continuity stays withheld by that rule rather than by name.

pages.title: I3436 — Every article reads in every language the site declares, and its counterparts are reciprocal
pages.description: scripts/site-check refuses, naming the file, an article whose counterpart is not a page under site/content-src, is in the article's own language or in another language than alternate_lang names, or does not name the article back, and an article site/data/nav.toml lists with no counterpart in a language the site declares; the languages are config.toml's default_language and the lang values the pages declare, and the check runs alone as --articles over a fixture.

pages.title: I3437 — An article names every language version in one translations table, and every member names the same group
pages.description: An article's front matter may name every counterpart in [extra.translations] (lang = \"route/\") for any number of languages; site/templates/base.html emits one rel=alternate hreflang link per entry plus its own through get_url, the two-language alternate and alternate_lang pair stays readable, and site-check refuses a group that is not the same set from every member, a language listed twice and an article listing its own language.

pages.title: I3438 — A translation records the digest of its source, and site-check refuses one its source has moved past
pages.description: A translation names its source and the digest of the source it was made from, [extra] translated_from = \"route/\" and source_digest = the SHA-256 of the source's bytes after its closing front-matter fence; site-check recomputes the digest and refuses a stale or missing one, printing the file, its source and the digest to record once re-synced, and refuses a digest on an original and a source outside the group. The check never rewrites a digest.

pages.title: idd-reads-at-a-glance — The intent workspace reads at a glance and leads everywhere it names
pages.description: The workspace reads in the order a person asks (what the intent is, what is missing, what to do next, the work, the evidence), every id on it is a link, its numbers are the intent's, its texts render through the UI's one prose renderer, it offers one primary action, and audit rules keep bare ids and raw markdown off every /ui page from now on.

pages.title: idd-workspace — The UI is where the owner directs the work, from an intent to its next move
pages.description: One screen of the UI, /ui/idd, starts from an intent and shows its milestones, their issues with status and blockers, the waves the dependencies allow and the dependency graph, each entity a link to its inspector, and every ready issue one click from the move that starts it; delivery and the live channel follow as the capabilities beneath them land.

pages.title: intent-bound-work — A task is bound to the intent it serves
pages.description: `start` names an issue, an intent or a declared exemption, asks the binding capability what the task serves, and refuses a refused binding where the policy requires binding. The task record carries what was named and the revision it resolved at. `context` briefs the worker from the binding, `handover` pins the revision, and `handover --resolve` reports drift.

pages.title: intent-intake — A received brief is a campaign revision whose requirements are reconciled into the one plan
pages.description: A campaign revision's requirements get content-derived identities, are classified against the existing intents and issues into a draft, a later revision reports only the criteria whose source changed, and every intent shows the segments it was derived from.

pages.title: intent-lifecycle — Work is traceable to the intent it serves, and an intent is satisfied only by evidence
pages.description: An intent is a typed record above the milestones that realise it: a statement, its invariants, and satisfaction criteria each naming the evidence that settles it. Its stage is derived from the plan's milestone status and its satisfaction from the evidence ledger, never stored. A gate refuses an intent that names no milestone or evidence that resolves to nothing, a session's preflight names the intent its work serves or refuses, the Cockpit shows intents with measured and enforced coverage of its scripts, and a milestone closes on GitHub only when the intents it serves are satisfied.

pages.title: intent-planning — The plan of an intent is held to it before execution
pages.description: An issue names the intent criteria it serves; coverage of every criterion is derived from the plan and refused when a criterion has no work or work has no purpose. The gap a worker observed and the critique of the plan are typed records validated against the intent and the plan, and work does not start on an intent whose plan was never critiqued or has an open blocking finding.

pages.title: knowledge-acts-on-what-it-learns — The repository decides when to evolve its layer, and a session carries it out
pages.description: Friction is measured and then derived; each boundary records an evolve readiness verdict the next session is told; evolve output does not feed itself; outcomes are measured; a curated note whose source moved is flagged.

pages.title: knowledge-is-reconciled-before-it-is-reviewed — What a session proposes as knowledge is reconciled with what the repository already knows before a person reviews it, and a promotion stands on evidence that resolves
pages.description: A known fact gets one candidate. Each candidate group names what already speaks about its subject, read from the entity layer rather than from a second derivation. A promotion needs a resolvable reference and records it. An observation can cite the review that found it.

pages.title: M000 — Milestone and DAG driven development
pages.description: Every non-trivial change in this repository belongs to a milestone specification and to one dependency-linked issue execution contract, validated as a DAG, with status derived rather than asserted, and projected to GitHub and to the website from that one canonical model.

pages.title: M001 — A blocking question survives a handover
pages.description: An unresolved question keeps refusing a completed finish after the work moves to a new task, or the alternative is chosen deliberately and the reason is recorded where the next worker will read it.

pages.title: M002 — A durable record names the worker that wrote it
pages.description: A durable record either names the worker that produced it or is refused, and a record written from one session can never arrive attributed to another session's task.

pages.title: M003 — A session is a durable envelope, and knowledge is compiled from what is already canonical
pages.description: A worker with no conversation history can answer what happened, why, what was decided, which evidence supports it, where the canonical source lives, and what to do next — from records and a derived index, with git still the authority over both.

pages.title: M004 — Performance is executable evidence, and the hot path does no canonical work twice
pages.description: Every public command can be benchmarked from the command registry with cold and warm distributions, the phases and work counters of any run can be printed, the caches and batch reads that remove repeated work preserve every observable result, an accepted baseline lives in the repository and a check refuses a regression by policy, and the pre-commit hook is fast enough that nobody routes around it.

pages.title: mcp-transports-are-reliable — Every MCP transport delivers each request at most once, bounds what it carries, and honours cancellation
pages.description: A client gets each answer once or is told the outcome is unknown, can cancel what it started, cannot exhaust the server with one message, and finds its launch configuration generated from the provider declaration and diagnosed by parsing it.

pages.title: mesh-connectivity — Trusted nodes connect across NAT through proven transports, and every surface says which path
pages.description: A connectivity decision record, a relayed path through a trusted hub, a signed bootstrap manifest on Pages, and a NAT matrix in the mesh lab.

pages.title: mesh-journal-converges — The cooperation journal is durable, converges under any delivery order, and never lets a stale claim win
pages.description: An event the runtime accepted survives a crash or is reported lost; replicas with the same authenticated event set produce the same digest after any delivery order; a claim that expired never returns to beat a claim admitted while it was gone, and every claim conflict is announced; every page of the journal returns every event once.

pages.title: mesh-peers-execute-assigned-work — Work is offered to a peer by capability under a fenced lease, and runs there as an execution
pages.description: An assignment is offered, accepted or refused by a peer whose declared capabilities and execution profile satisfy it, and an accepted one runs through the execution plane under the same authorisation as a local call.

pages.title: operation-convergence — After the alpha, the time from an intent to its verified satisfaction is measured from the records
pages.description: Intent-to-verified-done, interventions, replans, governance time and rework are derived per intent from git history and the evidence ledger, and the with/without comparison is read from matched benchmark runs behind ADR 0082's rule.

pages.title: prismatic-lumen — Prismatic Lumen: the owner oversees and moves the whole mesh from one page, which owns nothing
pages.description: Lumen is a declared term naming one composed view over the runtime: a page that reads blackboard, peers, mesh and monitor with freshness and reconnect recovery, offers one authorised action whose result comes from the journal, and has measured latency before any is claimed.

pages.title: public-proof — A visitor sees the product prove itself, and can check every claim it makes
pages.description: One recorded scenario tells the whole story — a worker strays, claims it is done, hands over, and is refused until the repository's own test passes — and it drives the homepage hero, its own route, the README's first transcript and the live smoke check, each held to the recorded run by a gate rather than by care.

pages.title: recovery-from-injected-faults-is-proven — A killed worker, a cut connection and a conflict are injected on purpose, and recovery is proven without lost work or duplicate completion
pages.description: A conservation reading counts completions per issue, unreachable commits, stranded claims and multiply-consumed handovers; the T5 protocol registers three fault kinds; mesh lab scenarios and live single-host trials inject them; the T5 row publishes every trial.

pages.title: repository-automation-is-typed — Repository automation is typed capabilities that Rhai orchestrates, and domain-logic shell only shrinks
pages.description: A person, CI and an agent run the same repository automation through one executable with an embedded Rhai engine and typed Rust capabilities; just recipes are derived from the command graph and the commit hook is one call of the executable; shell remains only at declared OS, bootstrap and provider boundaries, and the domain logic left in shell only shrinks; and every migrated unit proved it behaves as its predecessor before the predecessor was deleted.

pages.title: routing-recommendations — Routing recommendations derived from measured cost
pages.description: The profile a task should run under is recommended from measured cost per accepted outcome, and the recommendation names the data it came from.

pages.title: runtime-adapters — Profiles become runtime constraints rather than advice
pages.description: A profile's axes become opt-in runtime clamps a provider actually applies — read size, output condensation, subagent budget — with the limit derived from the profile rather than configured twice.

pages.title: runtime-lifecycle — One usable server per checkout starts, attaches, stops and reports its state without races or hidden kills
pages.description: Entering a checkout, opening the Cockpit, or starting any number of MCP clients converges on one server for that checkout, which is taken over only when it is dead, stops in order when asked, removes only its own lease, reports a typed state every surface reads, and stays up while any surface uses it.

pages.title: runtime-trust — A runtime is safe to reach from another machine, and joining the mesh trusts nobody by accident
pages.description: Discovery is not trust, trust is not authorization, and a caller is admitted to change anything only by a key the trust policy names. A host that can reach a runtime reads it and changes nothing it cannot authenticate; every event in the journal was checked against the trust policy that holds now, whether it arrived over a link or from disk; and the limits the documents state are the limits the code enforces.

pages.title: safe-self-update — Every mesh node follows the published release by itself, versions meet safely, and a release's provenance can be checked
pages.description: An enrolled mesh node follows the stable release by itself through the one installer, forward only, activating in order and rolling back a failed activation (ADR 0161); a newer client replaces an older server in an ordered hand-off and an older client is told it is older; a change to any wire or on-disk schema needs a version bump; a released archive carries a provenance attestation the installer checks.

pages.title: shared-policy — Shared policy across repositories and workers
pages.description: A policy can be shared across repositories and workers, with local override remaining explicit and drift from the shared source detectable in one command.

pages.title: surfaces-never-disagree — Every surface projects the same state, says when it was observed, and keeps no list of its own
pages.description: A reader on any surface sees the same value, the time it was observed and whether it is stale; a capability added to or removed from the registry appears or disappears everywhere with no consumer edit; a page served beside the write routes runs only script it shipped.

pages.title: test-evidence — Every verifiable claim and widget resolves to revision-bound test evidence, on every surface
pages.description: Evidence is indexed by subject and judged at the presented revision, as ADR 0087 records. Every claim, rule, feature, command, capability, MCP tool and use case is a subject of one derived index, and every widget that states behaviour names one. Every surface reads its verdict from the tracked ledger alone, through one freshness function and one aggregation, at the revision it presents: the CLI and HTTP and MCP at the working tree or the checked-out commit, the site at the commit it was built from. A trunk run reaches the ledger through a reviewed recording pull request, and a supplementary record (a run record, coverage, a local row) can only weaken a verdict, naming itself when it does. Verified is rendered only for the one proven row of the freshness table, on every surface.

pages.title: the-corpus-is-registered-before-it-runs — A corpus of 20 tasks, stratified by a difficulty proxy measured and registered before the new tasks are written, is registered with its analysis, run order, stopping rule and a pinned release
pages.description: suites/corpus.yaml is a registration committed before the first run: 20 tasks in three strata whose cut-offs on a measured proxy were registered before the new tasks existed, each task proven failable and passable and reviewed by someone other than its author, a seeded interleaved run order, a stopping rule, and a treatment pinned to one released version.

pages.title: the-host-knows-its-runtimes — A host knows every Majordomus runtime it runs, with no project open
pages.description: A read-only host inventory first, derived from the leases every checkout already writes; a routing answer second. A hub's service is the declared deployment target of the-hub-is-reached-from-any-device, and no host-level resident is built.

pages.title: the-hub-is-reached-from-any-device — The hub is reached privately from any of the owner's devices, and a public ingress is configuration
pages.description: The hub is a declared deployment target with a tailnet ingress, and the external URL is one typed fact.

pages.title: the-intent-loop-is-proved-end-to-end — The intent loop is proved end to end, and the plan and the documents say what it does
pages.description: One fixture asserts the same intent id, verdict, criterion states, binding standing, disposition and remains on the command line, HTTP, MCP and the Cockpit page. A test tries every bypass the owner packs name and each is refused or exempted by policy, never passed. One case carries a desired outcome through draft, check, opposition, bound start, recorded evidence, a refused and then accepted finish, the GitHub body, a moved revision that stales the evidence and fresh evidence that restores it. The documents and the claims say what the loop does and nothing more.

pages.title: the-mesh-is-measured-against-one-agent — Coordinated workers on the mesh are compared with a single agent on the same batch tasks, at quality held by a registered non-inferiority guard
pages.description: The runner runs a coordinated-workers arm; batch tasks compose existing corpus tasks; a registered suite compares it with a single agent; the verdict on wall time is allowed only under a non-inferiority guard on accepted share, and is published on the T4 row.

pages.title: the-mesh-is-operated-from-any-device — The owner understands and operates the whole mesh from one page, on any device
pages.description: From a phone, a desktop or a Claude Code session the owner sees which nodes, sessions and tasks are live, what is blocked and why, and performs an authorised action whose result and evidence come back live; the page is a client of the persistent runtime, so closing it or ending a session loses nothing and changes nothing.

pages.title: the-mesh-is-operated-from-one-page — The owner operates the mesh from one page: every runtime readable, one action authorised end to end
pages.description: /ui reads any linked runtime and says which runtime every reading came from, and one mutating operation is authorised, audited and streamed back.

pages.title: the-mesh-works-out-of-the-box — The mesh works out of the box: trusted machines find each other by every means and their sessions cooperate from the first turn
pages.description: A trusted machine that starts any Majordomus surface in a repository with the mesh declared is linked to every other trusted machine on the LAN or tailnet without a hand-written address, every worktree takes part, and what the mesh holds can be read in one tool answer.

pages.title: the-plan-says-what-a-fix-unblocks — The plan says what finishing an issue unblocks, and why each blocked issue is blocked
pages.description: One counterfactual evaluator (plan.impact), a published impact page, set preview and blocked classes, all from plan.rs's readiness rules.

pages.title: the-product-shows-what-it-caught — What finish caught is counted from the ledger and compared on the benchmark, never asserted
pages.description: One read over the ledger answers what finish caught and what it cost, a refusal nobody answered is separated from a caught one, /ui shows it, and the benchmark gains an acceptance metric beside its token metric.

pages.title: the-proof-scorecard-is-published — One derived scorecard publishes every proof test's computed status, losses included, on every surface, and no value claim stands without a passed test
pages.description: economics.proof computes six rows from committed records and is served by CLI, HTTP, MCP, /ui/evidence and the site economics page; a guaranteed claim and a homepage value word stand only while the settling test reads passed.

pages.title: the-proof-tests-are-registered-before-they-run — The six proof tests are registered as validated protocols, each frozen by its own digest, and every trial is a typed record that publishes only what its basis permits
pages.description: A validated proof plan names the six tests. Each protocol is frozen by its own digest; a paired protocol references its suite's registration block by digest. One typed trial record serves T1, T3, T5 and T6, refuses what its protocol does not declare and redacts what its publication basis does not permit.

pages.title: the-runtime-supervises-itself — The runtime says what is progressing, waiting or stalled, and repairs only what is safe
pages.description: One read capability classifies the runtime's work; a bounded repair loop acts only through ensure, recovery, leases and the reaper.

pages.title: the-session-domain-is-written-once — The session lifecycle is written by the typed domain, and the shell only parses and renders
pages.description: Each lifecycle transition has one implementation in the typed domain; the shell commands keep their arguments, output and exit codes and delegate; a closed record states whether it is complete.

pages.title: the-ui-runs-and-explains — The UI runs any capability and explains what needs the owner, whose version it shows and where its time went
pages.description: I3225, I3226, I3227, I3228, I3229 and I3230 close these gaps on the existing screens.

pages.title: the-ui-works-on-a-phone — Every first-party surface works on a phone, and the primary flow is accepted there
pages.description: The narrow-screen menu behaves as one tested component on /ui and /cockpit, the audit refuses a control a thumb cannot hit, the dense screens have a phone projection, and the IDD loop is accepted at the floor width.

pages.title: truthful-plan-surfaces — The plan's surfaces are inferred from delivery, and nothing they show is typed beside the repository
pages.description: Every plan surface draws every milestone in the graph's order, each issue with its declared status beside the delivery stage inferred from branches, pull requests, merges, tags and the published site; a merged but unrecorded issue turns the trunk red past a window; no milestone carries a typed version; every relationship is a drawn, clickable diagram; every code block is highlighted by one engine with one token-derived palette.

pages.title: two-folder-integration — A repository that adopts Majordomus gains two directories and two lines, and can give them back
pages.description: Adoption is a reconciliation, not a template copy. One typed repository model is discovered once and every consumer reads it. A desired integration is computed from that model, diffed against what the repository actually holds, and applied as the smallest mutation that closes the gap — with everything Majordomus owns living under `.ai/` and `.majordomus/`, and anything outside those two namespaces reduced to a small managed bridge whose ownership is recorded. Running the reconciliation twice changes nothing the second time, and uninstalling gives back exactly what was taken and nothing a person authored.

pages.title: web-sign-in — The deployed surfaces know who is asking, and the identity providers are data
pages.description: One canonical identity-provider kind under .ai/repo/identity/providers/ describes each provider as data: its issuer, its endpoints or its discovery document, the scopes requested, the claim that carries a stable subject and the environment variable names its credentials arrive in. A single OpenID-Connect-shaped flow in the executable serves every provider in that directory; Google and Facebook are two objects, not two code paths. Sessions are cookie-borne, signed, short and revocable; identity is attached to a request once, in the router, and every surface — HTTP, Cockpit, OpenAPI, MCP — reads it from the same place. The capability registry's effect classification, not a per-route list, decides what an anonymous reader may do, and the OpenAPI document and the Cockpit both state that decision because both project it from the registry. Striking a provider is deleting one file and regenerating.

pages.title: what-a-workspace-decides-reaches-the-repository-with-its-source — What the owner decides in a vendor workspace reaches the repository, and every promoted record opens the message it came from
pages.description: The owner thinks aloud in the ChatGPT project. What the owner decides there is read into this checkout's own store, promoted by a person into intents, ADRs, milestones, issues and knowledge, and every promoted record names the conversation and message it came from, so that from the UI one click opens that message for the operator who holds the store, while the public repository and site carry only the reference.
