pages.title: majordomus_cli::intent_plan - Rust
pages.description: Intent coverage: which work makes which intent criterion true, derived from the plan.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::intent_realization - Rust
pages.description: Intent realization: which work realises which intent, through which sessions and providers, how each link is known, and what the intent still lacks.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::intent_review - Rust
pages.description: The two planning records an intent is held to before execution: the gap and the critique.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::lease - Rust
pages.description: One shared server per checkout: the lease that decides who it is. The first `majordomus mcp` (or `serve`) to create `state/mcp/server.json` under the checkout’s local half owns the server and publishes its URL there; every later process reads the file, checks that the server answers for this root, and attaches to it. A lease whose server does not answer is stale, and the next process takes it over; so is a file that is not a lease document, an empty one, or one whose owner never published a URL. A server that is slow to answer while its process is alive is busy, not stale: the election waits for it for `BUSY_GRACE` before it takes anything over. The file lives under `.ai/local/` (never tracked, by the layer’s contract), and it is removed when the server stops — including when `SIGTERM`, `SIGINT` or `SIGHUP` asks it to — but only by the process that still holds it: every removal and every rewrite re-reads the file under the lock beside it (`server.lock`) and acts only on a lease that carries the actor’s own token (`take_over_with` says why it is a lock).

pages.title: majordomus_cli::ledger - Rust
pages.description: The ledger: the append-only record of what happened to this checkout, and the one writer of it in this executable.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::live - Rust
pages.description: The repository as a long-lived process must see it: current, not as it was when the process started.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::logging - Rust
pages.description: Where diagnostics go, and where they must never go.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mcp - Rust
pages.description: The MCP capability: a projection of the index into resources and tools (`surface`), the JSON-RPC and MCP method handling over it (`protocol`), the one local transport (`stdio`), and the bridge that forwards a stdio session to the shared server of another process (`bridge`). Only `protocol` knows the wire shapes; only `stdio` knows about file descriptors; `surface` knows neither.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mcp::bridge - Rust
pages.description: The bridge: a `majordomus mcp` process that found the repository’s shared server already running forwards its client’s stdio frames to that server’s `/mcp` endpoint and writes the answers back, one HTTP request per message, and pings on the side so that the server keeps the session. It carries no index and no registry of its own, which is why it starts in milliseconds. The HTTP client below is the few lines a loopback request needs (the server always answers with `Content-Length`, never chunked); no HTTP library is pulled in for it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mcp::stdio - Rust
pages.description: The stdio transport: one JSON message per line in, one per line out. Nothing but protocol messages is ever written to the output; diagnostics go through `tracing`, which the executable points at stderr. EOF on input ends the session cleanly, and so does a closed output, because both mean the client has gone.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mcp::surface - Rust
pages.description: The surface: the registry as resources and tools, independent of any protocol encoding. Every resource is a capability with an MCP resource exposure; every tool is a capability with an MCP tool exposure; every call goes through the registry to the one handler the capability has. Nothing is declared here.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh - Rust
pages.description: The mesh: how one running Majordomus learns that others exist, and proves which one it is. ADR 0050 is the decision; this module is the whole implementation, and its boundaries are the point:

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::address - Rust
pages.description: Where this runtime can be reached: the `host:port` authorities it advertises and dials back. A server bound to a specific address advertises that address. A server bound to every interface (`0.0.0.0`) is reachable at each interface’s address and at none called `0.0.0.0`, so it advertises its up, non-loopback IPv4 interface addresses — physical ones before container bridges, at most `super::protocol::MAX_ENDPOINTS`. A server bound to loopback advertises loopback, which only this machine can dial; the mesh doctor says so.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::broadcast - Rust
pages.description: The UDP broadcast provider: the controlled fallback for segments where multicast is filtered. Same protocol, same port, no second serialization — only the destination differs: the limited broadcast address in `auto` mode, or the directed broadcast addresses the declaration lists in `explicit` mode. Never `auto` by default, and it does not spray interfaces: one socket, the destinations named above, nothing more.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::config - Rust
pages.description: The mesh declaration: whether this repository’s servers participate in discovery, and how. One typed object of the `.ai/` layer (kind `mesh`, schema `mesh/v1`), parsed here and nowhere else. No declaration, or `enabled: false`, means the mesh is off and not one socket opens — the repository’s default posture (“nothing leaves the machine”) holds until a person commits the object that says otherwise.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::cooperation - Rust
pages.description: Cooperation: the runtime that turns discovered, trusted runtimes of one repository into linked peers and keeps their journal converged. It owns the one peer-link table, the one journal of this runtime, the link handlers the HTTP surface answers, the dialers, the heartbeat and the expiry — and the operations (sessions, claims, handovers, reviews) every surface performs through it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::doctor - Rust
pages.description: The mesh self-check: every prerequisite proved on this machine alone, no second node required. Deterministic checks in a fixed order, each with its own verdict, so “why is the mesh not working” has an answer that names the broken link instead of a shrug — and, when a check fails or limits cooperation, what that means and what to do. Read-only toward the repository; the sockets it probes are ephemeral and closed before it answers.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::firewall - Rust
pages.description: The host firewall, as the mesh needs it: what inbound traffic the declaration implies this machine must admit, which firewall this host runs, the commands that admit it, what the firewall says now, and what the kernel logged it dropping.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::handover - Rust
pages.description: Handovers across the mesh. A handover is written on one machine by `majordomus handover` into that checkout’s `.ai/local/state/handovers/`; this module is the bridge between that record and the journal, in both directions:

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::identity - Rust
pages.description: Node identity: who this machine’s Majordomus is, independently of any repository, process, address or port. The identity is an Ed25519 keypair created once per user and machine and kept under the user’s state directory; the node id is a digest of the public key, so claiming an id means holding the key, and a hostname, an IP address or a PID is never identity — those are runtime attributes that change.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::journal - Rust
pages.description: The cooperation journal: the one replicated record of what the runtimes of a repository said to each other. Discovery (`super::registry`) answers “which runtimes exist”; the journal answers “what are they doing” — sessions, claims, handovers, reviews — as signed events that every linked runtime stores, relays and folds into the same state (`super::state`).

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::link - Rust
pages.description: The link protocol: what two runtimes say to become linked, and what they exchange once they are. Discovery (`super::protocol`) proves that a key exists somewhere; a link proves that the key is answering now, serves the same repository, speaks a compatible protocol, and is trusted — and only then does anything cooperative travel.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::manager - Rust
pages.description: The discovery manager: provider lifecycle, the one verification path, and the one registry. Providers hand raw bytes here; this thread parses, checks bounds and staleness, verifies the signature, evaluates trust, and only then touches the registry — in that order, for every transport alike. A provider cannot skip a step because no provider ever parses.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::multicast - Rust
pages.description: The UDP multicast provider: the preferred LAN mechanism. One socket, bound to the configured port and joined to the group; a listener thread hands every datagram to the manager, an announcer thread transmits the beacon on the interval with jitter. IPv4 only, TTL from the declaration (1 by default: the local segment and no further).

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::page - Rust
pages.description: What one answer about the mesh carries: a summary a worker can read whole, or the folded state narrowed to what was asked.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::protocol - Rust
pages.description: The discovery wire protocol: one envelope, every transport. A multicast datagram, a broadcast datagram and a rendezvous candidate all carry the same signed advertisement, so there is one serializer, one parser and one verification path — a second protocol per transport is exactly the five-truths defect ADR 0050 refuses.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::provider - Rust
pages.description: The provider contract: a discovery mechanism is a source of observations and nothing more. A provider watches one transport (a multicast group, a broadcast port, a rendezvous endpoint set), hands every datagram it hears to the manager as raw bytes, and answers for its own health. It parses nothing, verifies nothing, trusts nothing and holds no peers — the manager owns the one verification path and the one registry, which is what makes adding a provider a registration rather than a rewrite.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::registry - Rust
pages.description: The one registry of discovered nodes. Every provider’s observation converges here, deduplicated by node id (a digest of the key — never by address), so a node seen over multicast and handed back by a rendezvous is one record with two sources, not two rows with one truth each. Every surface — CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP, Cockpit — is a projection of this map; nothing else may hold peers.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::rendezvous - Rust
pages.description: The rendezvous provider: discovery across segments multicast cannot cross. Every Majordomus server is a rendezvous — the `mesh.register` capability accepts a signed envelope and answers with the envelopes it holds — so a “mothership” is any node the declaration points at, not a different program and not a canonical database. The local registry stays the only truth; a rendezvous is one more source of observations, its failure stretches the retry and stops nothing else, and its answers are signed end-to-end: a poisoned rendezvous can withhold nodes, it cannot invent one.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::repository - Rust
pages.description: Which repository and which runtime a mesh participant is — independently of any path.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::root - Rust
pages.description: The trust root: which copy of the mesh declaration a runtime obeys (ADR 0050 rule 6, I2135).

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::state - Rust
pages.description: The cooperation state: what the journal’s events mean, folded. Pure: the same set of events and the same liveness verdicts yield the same state on every runtime, whatever order the events arrived in and however often — events are applied in `(lamport, stream, seq)` order, and a set has no duplicates. That is the whole convergence argument, and a property test holds it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::mesh::trust - Rust
pages.description: Trust: what a verified advertisement is allowed to mean. Verification (the signature proves the key) happens in the protocol; trust (this key is one of ours) is decided here, by policy — and by default the policy is that an unknown key is observed, recorded, visible in every listing, and trusted for nothing.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::metadata - Rust
pages.description: Metadata: the kind schema (`kinds.yaml`) and one JSON Schema per kind, both read at run time from the tool distribution’s share directory and, when a repository adds its own, from `.ai/repo/knowledge/`; and the YAML helpers shared by every reader. The contract is documented in `docs/CAPABILITIES.md` and in `share/kinds.yaml` itself.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::metadata::frontmatter - Rust
pages.description: Front matter: the metadata block at the top of a document of the layer.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::metadata::yaml - Rust
pages.description: The layer’s YAML subset, as `docs/SCHEMAS.md` and the shell tool’s `mj_yaml_flatten` define it: `key: value`, nested maps by two-space indent, block lists (`- item`), lists of maps (`- key: value` plus indented keys), inline lists `[a, b]`, single or double quotes, comments. Tabs, odd indentation, anchors, multi-line scalars and flow maps are refused with the line named (the shell parser reads an anchor or alias as text; this one refuses it, which is the stricter reading of the same contract). A scalar is a string unless it is an unquoted integer or `true`/`false`; nothing else is interpreted.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::model - Rust
pages.description: The domain model: what an object is, where it came from, and what was wrong with what could not become one.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::models - Rust
pages.description: The model catalogue: which AI models exist for this tool’s world, what each can do, and which one a stated need selects — as declared data, never as a live client. ADR 0044 is the decision; ADR 0032’s boundary stands untouched: this crate calls no model, holds no SDK, and reads no credential’s value. The catalogue is `share/models.yaml` — one declaration, exactly like `share/providers.yaml` — and `models.list` / `models.route` project it to the CLI, HTTP, OpenAPI, MCP and the Cockpit, so no consumer keeps a model name of its own.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::order - Rust
pages.description: Canonical presentation order.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::pack - Rust
pages.description: The source pack: the tracked tree as a few text files a language model’s file search can index, with nothing in it that is not source.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::peers - Rust
pages.description: Peers: the clients attached to one shared server. Every MCP session, the owner’s stdio one and every one that arrived over HTTP, is a peer from the moment it attaches; `initialize` gives it a name (the client’s own `clientInfo`), and `peers.announce` lets it say what it is working on. The board lives in the server’s memory and nowhere else: it ends with the process, and nothing here touches the repository.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::perf - Rust
pages.description: Performance truth: process-wide counters of the work that must happen once (a repository scan, an index build, a registry build, a schema generation, a projection build) and of the work that happens per call (executions, handler invocations, cache hits and misses), plus phase timings on a monotonic clock. They are what the structural tests read after hundreds of requests to prove that no request rebuilt canonical state, what `perf.counters` answers over every transport, and what the benchmark evidence carries beside its latencies. Atomics only: reading them costs nothing worth measuring, and nothing here allocates on a hot path.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::plan - Rust
pages.description: The plan: milestones, issues, the two graphs between them, and everything derived from them — execution waves, issue status, milestone status, the roadmap order, the active milestone, the next executable issue and every validation finding.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::policy - Rust
pages.description: The canonical policy, typed: `.ai/repo/policy.yaml` and the profiles beside it. The policy is the one canonical input of the provider projections; the shell tool reads the same file with the same subset reader, so the two agree byte for byte on what a projection is and which hash it carries.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::product - Rust
pages.description: The product model: what this repository’s product does for a person, as the features under the layer’s features section declare it, with every fact a surface may say about a feature derived from the registries that own those facts.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::proto - Rust
pages.description: The reader for the layer’s Markdown document schemas.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::proto::project - Rust
pages.description: The projections of a `.proto` document schema.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::providers - Rust
pages.description: The provider projections: `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` and whatever else the policy’s `projections[]` declares, rendered from the provider templates and the canonical policy. They are one-way: the policy and the templates are the sources, the targets are caches that `generate --check` compares and `generate` rewrites.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::quality - Rust
pages.description: What this executable’s own public surface is held to, measured by the executable.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::quality::parity - Rust
pages.description: Transport parity: the canonical registry against every projection of it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::quality::policy - Rust
pages.description: What the repository demands of an exported item, and what counts as having met it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::quality::report - Rust
pages.description: Assembling one measurement: the inventory and the registry in, a `QualityReport` out.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::quality::source - Rust
pages.description: The crate read as a syntax tree: which items this crate actually exports, where each one is declared, what its documentation says, and which of its doc examples run.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::reasoning - Rust
pages.description: Reasoning: how a session turns material engineering uncertainty into a recorded, evidence-backed conclusion — with independent advisors when some are present, and without them when none are. ADR 0098 is the decision; `docs/REASONING.md` the manual.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::reasoning::availability - Rust
pages.description: Which advisors can be asked right now, and why each one that cannot, cannot.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::reasoning::catalogue - Rust
pages.description: The advisor catalogue: `share/advisors.yaml`, one declaration of every advisory role a session may consult, in the grain of `share/providers.yaml` and `share/models.yaml`.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::reasoning::check - Rust
pages.description: `reasoning.check`: the executable half of the rules `project.advisors-are-optional` and `project.review-is-recorded-not-claimed`. Each check reads files and says what it found; none of them asks an advisor anything.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::reasoning::policy - Rust
pages.description: The consultation policy: given what is uncertain and how much it matters, whether independent review is worth having, how much, and from which available advisors.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::reasoning::record - Rust
pages.description: The records a session writes while it reasons: typed engineering artefacts, never a transcript and never hidden reasoning. What is kept is what a later session needs to avoid rediscovering a decision — facts, evidence references, assumptions, questions, positions, conclusions, validation — and nothing an advisor said verbatim beyond the summary its adapter normalised.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::reasoning::state - Rust
pages.description: The reasoning state of a session, derived from its records and nothing else: what is uncertain, what was asked and what came back, where advice disagreed and what settled it, what was concluded and whether it was proven — plus the timeline, the degradation that happened along the way, and the report a handover or a final summary carries.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::reasoning::store - Rust
pages.description: The one writer of reasoning records, and the rules a record must satisfy before it becomes durable.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::redaction - Rust
pages.description: The one rule set that makes text a run printed fit to publish.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::release - Rust
pages.description: The release: what this project has shipped, what it would ship next, and the changelog that is a projection of both rather than a file somebody remembered to update.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::release::changelog - Rust
pages.description: Composing the changelog out of what the repository already states.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::release::commits - Rust
pages.description: Conventional commits, read from git and parsed.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::release::compat - Rust
pages.description: The compatibility engine: how much the public contract moved, and therefore what the smallest honest version is.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::release::landing - Rust
pages.description: The version a landing allocates (ADR 0134): what the integration executor raises the trunk’s version to when it lands a pull request, decided from three things and nothing else — the version the trunk declares, how far the pull request moves the public contract (ADR 0051’s measurement), and the repository’s typed `release:` policy.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::release::model - Rust
pages.description: The typed value every release surface answers with.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::release::surface - Rust
pages.description: The public surface: everything a caller can hold, read from the one declaration that states it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::release::version - Rust
pages.description: The version: the one place it is authored, what is derived from that place, what the contract requires next and what the commits imply as evidence, and the one writer that raises it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::repository - Rust
pages.description: Repository discovery: the nearest ancestor of the start directory that carries `.ai/manifest.yaml` is the root, and the manifest is the only thing read to find it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::rules - Rust
pages.description: The rules module: a rule, and everything the repository can show that proves it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::scope - Rust
pages.description: The repository scope: what a worker reads of the repository, and what it never reads.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::served - Rust
pages.description: What a deployment actually serves, observed from outside and judged against the commit that was meant to be there.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::session - Rust
pages.description: The session domain: one typed account of what an episode is, what identifies it, how it moves, and how it is closed exactly once.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::session::episode - Rust
pages.description: The aggregate: what an episode is, and what it is not.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::session::identity - Rust
pages.description: The identities of the session domain: six things that the stores spell as three words.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::session::ledger - Rust
pages.description: The typed event substrate: the existing append-only ledger, read and written with types.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::session::state - Rust
pages.description: Where an episode is in its life, and the transitions that move it there.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::session::store - Rust
pages.description: Persistence: the open-episode store, the closed-record store, and closing exactly once.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::share - Rust
pages.description: The tool distribution’s data directory: `share/kinds.yaml` and `share/schemas/<kind>.schema.json`, read at run time. Nothing about kinds or keys is compiled into the executable; the directory is located per invocation, explicitly or by convention, and named in every error when it is not.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::site - Rust
pages.description: The site’s registry dataset: what GitHub Pages renders about the executable, derived from the registry, the index, the command line, the benchmark projection and the accepted baselines, and nothing else. The site has no content model of its own for any of it; its templates read `site/data/registry/registry.json` and lay it out, and the shell site generator reads `docs/generated/registry.json` for the ids it turns into routes.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::skill - Rust
pages.description: Skills as proven capabilities: what the repository can show about each skill, derived.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::synthetic - Rust
pages.description: A synthetic repository: the layer `majordomus init` writes, with as many rules and documents as a test or a benchmark asks for, in a fresh temporary directory that is removed on drop. One generator for the property tests, the scaling benchmarks and the registry benchmarks, so that they measure and test the same shape of repository. Not a git repository: discovery goes through the filesystem, which is what a benchmark wants to measure and a property test wants to control.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::ui - Rust
pages.description: `majordomus ui`: the primary surface, a product of its own, server-rendered (ADR 0135).

pages.title: majordomus_cli::web - Rust
pages.description: The repository’s web surfaces: one model, discovered once, read by everything that serves, publishes, validates or describes them.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::web::discover - Rust
pages.description: Discovery: how the repository’s web surfaces are found without anybody listing them.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::web::files - Rust
pages.description: Serving a static surface: a generated directory answered under its mount.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::web::html - Rust
pages.description: The one page style every generated report uses.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::web::model - Rust
pages.description: The typed model of a web surface: what it is, where it is mounted, what produced it, and where every value came from.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::web::report - Rust
pages.description: The reports this repository generates as web surfaces: the test run, the benchmark run, the UI conformance audit that is a section of the first, and the UI itself read once at a pinned commit, which a publication carries at the UI’s mount (`snapshot`, ADR 0141).

pages.title: majordomus_cli::web::report::tests - Rust
pages.description: The test report: the suite’s own results, rendered.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::web::report::ui - Rust
pages.description: The UI conformance report: what a browser found on every page of the built site.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::web::serve - Rust
pages.description: Serving the static surfaces of a resolved topology.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::web::validate - Rust
pages.description: Validation: the invariants a topology must satisfy before anything serves or publishes it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::why - Rust
pages.description: The Why catalogue: the operational moments this tool is a response to, the audiences that recognise them and the areas they fall under, read from the index and answered as one immutable typed model.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::worktree - Rust
pages.description: The branch-to-worktree topology: where every linked worktree of a repository belongs, derived from git and from nothing else, and everything that follows from it.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::worktree::fingerprint - Rust
pages.description: The proof that a move lost nothing.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::worktree::state - Rust
pages.description: What git says about the state of a work tree and of every branch: uncommitted work from `status --porcelain`, and every local branch with its upstream, its distance from it and the work tree holding it from one `for-each-ref`. Nothing here fetches.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::worktree::trunk - Rust
pages.description: How far a checkout is from the remote trunk: the one measurement behind `project.a-checkout-serves-the-current-trunk`.

pages.title: majordomus_cli::worktree::uncommitted - Rust
pages.description: Uncommitted work in the linked work trees, and whether anything still holds it (I1995).

pages.description: Every closed execution episode this repository holds: what it started from, what it produced, and how it ended. Written by the tool from git and the ledger, never from a conversation.

pages.title: Skills
pages.description: Provider-neutral procedures for one bounded kind of work each, read from the repository's skills section. Every page is the skill's own file; every listing is derived from it.

pages.title: Assess before deleting
pages.description: Remove a file, branch, worktree, record or process only after each candidate has been classified by what depends on it and what would be lost, and the reversible step has been taken first.

pages.title: Deploy the site by hand
pages.description: Publish the website to GitHub Pages from a terminal, through the one script the Pages workflow runs, when waiting for the Actions queue is not acceptable.

pages.title: Evolve the repository's know-how
pages.description: Turn what sessions observed into reviewed knowledge and into the rule, skill, document or test each lesson belongs in, then deliver the change and tell every peer what moved.

pages.title: Implement a change
pages.description: Carry a requested change through the repository evidence-first, from the invariant it must keep to a verified, reconciled, documented and committed tree, without widening its scope.

pages.title: Pack the sources for a ChatGPT project
pages.description: Turn a committed tree into token-bounded Markdown shards that a ChatGPT project's file search indexes, verified to carry no binary, worktree, link, build output, projection or leaked value, and hand them over with the commit they were cut from.

pages.title: Pack the repository for an outside reviewer
pages.description: Prepare a bounded, reproducible snapshot of the tracked tree for a reviewer who cannot read the repository directly, with the local half and anything secret left out and the questions the review must answer written down.

pages.title: Repository review
pages.description: An evidence-driven review of the actual state of the repository, or of one change to it, before meaningful engineering work is recommended or done.

pages.title: Report by verification state
pages.description: Write the outcome of a piece of work as claims each marked VERIFIED, PARTIAL or BLOCKED by the evidence actually observed, so a reader can tell what was proved from what was only done or intended.

pages.title: What Majordomus supervises
pages.description: 11 responsibilities, one layer. Each is a file under .ai/ and a subcommand that reads it.

pages.title: Doctor
pages.description: proves the installation is real: policy parses, every declared enforcement is actually invoked by the hook it names without a swallowed exit code, every projection matches its own stamp, the always-loaded file is under budget

pages.title: Finish
pages.description: a typed outcome and a contract evaluated line by line; nothing written when any line fails

pages.title: Handover
pages.description: append-only records with computed front matter and required sections, created atomically, never staged; --resolve finds the right one for this worktree and branch and labels how far git has moved since

pages.title: Layer
pages.description: one portable .ai/ directory, readable without the tool: .ai/repo/ is tracked and canonical, .ai/local/ is this checkout's own and ignored; doctor proves the manifest resolves, every section it names exists, and nothing under local/ is tracked

pages.title: Plan
pages.description: milestones are outcome specifications and issues are execution contracts; status, execution waves and the next ready issue are derived from the dependency graph, never stored

pages.title: Policy
pages.description: one provider-neutral policy.yaml; unknown keys are errors

pages.title: Profiles
pages.description: one bundle per task class, each setting capability class, reasoning effort, verbosity, presentation, context toggles, verification, and checkpoint interval independently

pages.title: Projection
pages.description: update generates CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, or any target you name, deterministically, and stamps each with the policy hash and the hash of its own content; a hand edit is detected and never silently overwritten

pages.title: Scope
pages.description: start takes the paths a task may touch; check and finish fail on files outside them; other worktrees' overlapping claims are reported

pages.title: State
pages.description: one active task per checkout in current.yaml, with branch, head, and working_tree computed from git, never authored

pages.title: Watch
pages.description: reports drift between policy, projections, state, scope, and git, each finding with the command that reproduces it

pages.title: Sázka na vrstvu, ne na model
pages.description: Proč Majordomus není další AI agent: modely se stanou zaměnitelnými, koordinaci si jejich výrobci vezmou sami a co zbývá, je nestranný doklad, že práce je hotová.
pages.section: Sázka na vrstvu, ne na model

pages.title: The bet on a layer, not a model
pages.description: Why Majordomus is not another AI agent: models will become interchangeable, their makers will take coordination for themselves, and what is left is impartial proof that the work is done.
pages.section: The bet on a layer, not a model

pages.title: Use cases
pages.description: What people do with it: a task, the commands that answer it, and what you are left holding, each one proved against the tool. Every step is a real invocation, every rule and promise a real object, and every example below was executed to make this page.

pages.title: Decide whether finished work is actually finished
pages.description: Evaluate a contract line by line instead of accepting a sentence that says the work is done.

pages.title: Add a use case and let the tool prove it
pages.description: Scaffold a draft for an uncovered command, validate it, run its scenario against the real tool, and see the coverage move.

pages.title: Adopt a repository that already has its own rules
pages.description: Install the supervisory layer into a repository with a hand-written CLAUDE.md, without the tool taking ownership of a file somebody else wrote.

pages.title: Getting started and adoption
pages.description: Bringing Majordomus into a repository, new or old, without losing what people already wrote.

pages.title: Block acceptance on a question nobody has answered
pages.description: Open a question against the task, watch finish refuse completion while it is unresolved, resolve it with the answer, and only then complete.

pages.title: Keep the prompts that started the work, below the model rather than around it
pages.description: Wire the provider hook, prove it by running a payload through it, and see that a prompt the tool could not parse is reported rather than silently dropped.

pages.title: Hand work over with a question still open, and keep it blocking
pages.description: Close a task into a handover while a question is unresolved, start the follow-up task, and see the same question still refuse acceptance there.

pages.title: Catch an agent that says it is done when it is not
pages.description: One task, start to finish: a worker strays outside its scope, claims it is finished, hands over, and is accepted only once the repository's own verification passes.

pages.title: Checkpoint long work so a stop costs minutes, not the day
pages.description: Record compact progress inside the active task at the profile interval, so a session that ends without warning leaves the next one a place to start.

pages.title: Decide what belongs in the AI context, as data
pages.description: Read the repository’s declared scope policy, see which paths are in and out of the index, and let doctor and the knowledge index apply it rather than a hardcoded list.

pages.title: Complete an issue only when its evidence exists
pages.description: See an issue refuse completion while a required piece of evidence is missing, read the roadmap the milestone state derives, and keep the GitHub projection a projection.

pages.title: Completion and quality gates
pages.description: Deciding whether work is finished, with a contract every line of which passes or fails.

pages.title: Sessions and handover
pages.description: Stopping and resuming work across sessions and workers from durable state, never a transcript.

pages.title: Use-case coverage
pages.description: Every public command, guaranteed claim and MCP tool against the use cases that name it, run it and carry evidence for it; the policy says which gaps fail.

pages.title: Deliver issues in waves the graph computes, and take the next one
pages.description: Validate the plan, read the execution waves the dependency graph yields, see which issues are ready and which are blocked on what, and take the one issue a worker should do now.

pages.title: Refuse a directory of the layer that documents nothing
pages.description: A directory added under the layer without a context document fails validation by name, nothing resolves against the tree until it says what it is for, and the same hierarchy is readable over MCP and the API without running the gate.

pages.title: Drift and reconciliation
pages.description: Detecting that policy, projections, state and git disagree, and putting them back in step.

pages.title: Extend what the executable serves by adding a file, never by rebuilding it
pages.description: Add a rule, a prompt or a knowledge node to .ai/ and have it appear as an MCP resource, an HTTP route and a reference entry, with the same binary.

pages.title: Extension
pages.description: Adding a kind, a rule, a command or a use case as data, with the checks that follow from it.

pages.title: Find an object of the layer without reading everything
pages.description: Search durable records literally across kinds from the shell, and ask the shared server the same question over MCP with majordomus_search and majordomus_get.

pages.title: Find out what has drifted since anyone last looked
pages.description: Ask what has moved, rather than whether anything is wrong.

pages.title: Follow a procedure the repository defines, and add another one
pages.description: Read the repository's skills, take one as it is written, and add a new one by writing its file — no registry, no code, and a check that says what it examined.

pages.title: Gate CI on the tool itself, with an exit code that is a contract
pages.description: Run the checks CI runs, read every finding with the command that reproduces it, and rely on exit codes that mean one thing each: no code means warn and continue.

pages.title: Hand the repository to someone who cannot clone it
pages.description: Take a snapshot that a model can read or a gate can run in, without sending anything untracked and without losing the file modes on the way.

pages.title: Hand unfinished work to the next session
pages.description: Stop mid-task and leave the next worker something to act on that is not a transcript.

pages.title: Install the tool in one command, on a machine with no toolchain
pages.description: Paste one line, get a verified binary for this machine, and run majordomus init — no git, no Rust, no Node, no Python, no root, and no way to install an archive whose digest does not match.

pages.title: Record a decision so the next worker can find it
pages.description: Write down what was decided and why as state, then find it again without reading a conversation.

pages.title: Keep every provider bootstrap thin, generated and within budget
pages.description: Regenerate AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the other provider files from one policy and prove they are stamped, point at the layer, stay under the line budget and resolve every reference.

pages.title: Keep what an episode learned, without a model and without a conversation
pages.description: Record a decision inside an episode, derive it into a candidate knowledge record from the ledger, read the evidence that the derivation ran, and watch a second derivation change nothing.

pages.title: Know whether the work in this checkout is finished
pages.description: Ask the repository you are standing in, and be told what is still owed by name.

pages.title: Check the version before trusting a diagnosis
pages.description: Print the version every other surface derives from, and see the argument it refuses.

pages.title: Repository knowledge
pages.description: What the repository declares about itself: sources, nodes, edges, the plan, and searching them.

pages.title: Have the session opened and closed without anybody remembering to
pages.description: Wire the provider's own session events, and the episode opens when the sitting begins, hands the worker what the last one left, records what a compaction is about to discard, and closes with a continuation record beside its envelope.

pages.title: Serving the layer to AI clients
pages.description: One shared server per repository, every client a peer, the same layer over MCP, HTTP and the command line.

pages.title: Move a repository from the pre-.ai layout to the layer
pages.description: See what a migration would move, move it with a backup, and prove the result is a layer the tool reads.

pages.title: Record what one worker did in one sitting
pages.description: Open a session, do the work under whatever tasks it touches, and close it into an envelope that references what it produced and copies nothing.

pages.title: Performance
pages.description: Benchmarks derived from the registry, baselines that are data, and budgets doctor reports against.

pages.title: Divide a working tree into commits, and hold every message to a policy
pages.description: Ask what this tree would commit and why, learn the scope vocabulary from the history rather than a table, and get a verdict on one message or on a whole range before a reviewer has to give one.

pages.title: Keep the plan as milestones and issues the tool can validate
pages.description: Declare milestones as outcomes and issues as execution contracts, and let the tool say what is ready and what is blocked.

pages.title: Policy and enforcement
pages.description: Declaring rules, proving they are wired, and reproducing a finding.

pages.title: Prove a rule is actually enforced, not merely written down
pages.description: Answer "is this rule real?" with a command rather than a reading of the source.

pages.title: Prove the tool is fast, not assume it, and refuse a regression
pages.description: Measure every public command and every capability of the executable against a committed baseline, and let the check fail on a regression rather than a reviewer noticing later.

pages.title: Prove what a task owed before calling it done
pages.description: A task declares what it owes, records evidence against each obligation, and is refused when that evidence no longer describes the tree it was taken over.

pages.title: Read back what happened, and keep the ledger within its cap
pages.description: Read the append-only ledger as operational history, filtered by task and event, validate every line, and rotate the oldest lines into an archive rather than deleting them.

pages.title: Read only the context that fits the budget, and know what was dropped
pages.description: Assemble the context a worker needs now in authority order, cut it to a line budget, and see every dropped section named with its reason.

pages.title: See which rules apply here and what enforces them
pages.description: List the effective rule set, read one rule as the tool reads it, and see which of them the tool enforces and from where.

pages.title: Record a decision as data, and prove the tool cannot accept it for you
pages.description: Read the decisions a repository holds, validate the whole set in one command, and watch the tool refuse to write the one status only a person may write.

pages.title: Close an episode whose client never came back
pages.description: A killed provider sends no end event. Close the episode it left open by evidence, exactly once, without claiming work it did not do.

pages.title: Start a session from a rendered framing, not a pasted transcript
pages.description: List the prompt assets the repository ships, render one against the durable state, and read the context it embeds.

pages.title: Resume in the right worktree, never against somebody else’s task
pages.description: Find the handover that belongs to this worktree and branch, and see a task record from another checkout reported as foreign rather than enforced here.

pages.title: Run several workers in one repository without them colliding
pages.description: Give each worker a declared scope, and find out immediately when two of them claim the same paths.

pages.title: Say what reached the remote and what did not
pages.description: The obligations that reach past the working tree are settled by asking git and the published site, so a report cannot call uncommitted work committed or unpushed work pushed.

pages.title: Say what your work is for, once, and have every surface say it
pages.description: Record an operational failure mode as one file and have the command line, the API, MCP and the website answer it without registering it anywhere.

pages.title: See what the repository holds, and run one of its capabilities, without reading a file
pages.description: Open the shared server in a browser and get the whole layer as pages: what exists, where each thing came from, what depends on what, what is failing, and a form that runs any capability.

pages.title: Serve the repository's AI layer to every AI client through one shared server
pages.description: Open the repository in any client the tool declares a provider for (docs/generated/providers.md) and have each of them read the same rules, prompts and knowledge over MCP from one process, seeing each other.

pages.title: Trace a change to the context documents it affects
pages.description: List the scoped context documents, resolve which apply to a path and why, and find out which documents a change set touches before it lands.

pages.title: Trust the policy and the profiles only after they are validated
pages.description: Prove that the canonical policy parses with every key it needs declared, that every profile parses and the default exists, and that what the policy declares as enforced is what actually runs.

pages.title: Use the tool as your own in a shared repository, and propose it to the team when it has made its case
pages.description: One flag installs the same layer as yours alone: no tracked file changes, nothing is added to .gitignore, git status reads the same — the command checks it — and one more command hands the layer to the team.

pages.title: Work on a branch in the one worktree it belongs to
pages.description: Start a branch without choosing a path, find every checkout of the repository from any of them, and bring a stray one home with its uncommitted work intact.

pages.title: Parallel workers
pages.description: Several agents or people on one repository: claimed scopes, overlap, and who touched what.

pages.title: Vložené zadání se stává plánem
pages.description: Zadání vložené do session je přání k jednomu dni, ne pokyn. Jak ho tenhle repozitář uchová přesně tak, jak přišlo, jak z toho, co chce, udělá záznamy, které může gate odmítnout, a co ten mechanismus ještě musí dokázat.

pages.title: Všechno v jednom proudu
pages.description: Zhruba tucet sessions na pěti strojích pracovalo na jednom repozitáři a žádná neviděla, co dělají ostatní, dokud si nenapsala vlastní polling smyčku. Co změnil jeden proud signálů, ze kterého je šum sbalený pryč, a co naměřil hned první den.

pages.title: Why you need this
pages.description: 38 operational failure modes AI-heavy teams meet, who recognises each, what actually causes it, and what Majordomus does and does not do about it.

pages.title: A worktree nobody can decide to delete
pages.description: Isolation is cheap to create and expensive to reason about: nothing records what a worktree was for or whether its work landed.

pages.title: The interface changed and its contract document did not
pages.description: A contract maintained by hand beside the code it describes goes stale on the first change that forgets it.

pages.title: Operational areas
pages.description: The parts of running AI-assisted work these moments fall under, each with the ones that fall under it.

pages.title: Context and continuity
pages.description: What a worker knows when it starts, and what survives when it stops.

pages.title: Coordination and ownership
pages.description: Who holds what, who is doing what right now, and what happens where two workers meet.

pages.title: Model, effort and cost
pages.description: What was spent, on which task, at which capability, and whether the choice was ever recorded.

pages.title: Decisions
pages.description: What was settled, why, and whether the next worker can find out before reopening it.

pages.title: Documentation and drift
pages.description: Whether what is written still describes what exists, and how many copies of it there are.

pages.title: Rules and governance
pages.description: Which rules apply here, whether anything loads them, and whether they still agree with each other.

pages.title: Observability
pages.description: What actually happened while nobody was watching, in a form that is not a transcript.

pages.title: Verification and evidence
pages.description: Whether "done" is a claim or a fact, and what would prove the difference.

pages.title: Work and its state
pages.description: What is in flight, what is finished, and whether the repository agrees with the tracker.

pages.title: Who this is for
pages.description: The audiences that recognise these moments, each with the ones it recognises. Membership is declared by every moment and never listed here.

pages.title: Agency or consultancy
pages.description: Many clients, many repositories, and context that must transfer between people in hours rather than weeks.

pages.title: AI-native development team
pages.description: Several people and more assistants than people, working the same repository at the same time.

pages.title: Engineering lead
pages.description: Accountable for what shipped, without having watched any of it being written.

pages.title: Enterprise engineering
pages.description: Answerable to auditors, not only to users: what was done, by what, under which policy, with what evidence.

pages.title: Open-source maintainer
pages.description: Reviews contributions from people and machines they have never met, against conventions only they know.

pages.title: Platform and developer productivity team
pages.description: Owns the rules, the tooling and the execution environment that everybody else works inside.

pages.title: Research and experimental engineering
pages.description: Many more experiments than results, and the expensive part is remembering which ones were already tried.

pages.title: Solo builder
pages.description: One person, several assistants, and no one else to ask what was decided yesterday.

pages.title: A change that no plan ever asked for
pages.description: Work arrives with no bounded contract behind it, so its scope, its acceptance criteria and its ownership are all decided after the fact.

pages.title: The instruction file that grew into a rulebook
pages.description: Everything important gets appended to the always-loaded file, so every session pays for every rule and reads none of them carefully.

pages.title: A fluent contribution that could not have known the rules
pages.description: Assistants let anybody produce plausible contributions at volume; the conventions that make one correct are still only in the maintainers.

pages.title: The decision exists, in a conversation nobody can find
pages.description: A decision that was reached in a session is stored where only that session can read it, so it is neither reviewable nor discoverable.

pages.title: A hard-won discovery that never became knowledge
pages.description: A worker learns something expensive about the codebase, uses it once, and it dies with the session because nothing turned it into a durable record.

pages.title: The documented command that no longer works
pages.description: Examples are written once, in prose, and nothing ever executes them again.

pages.title: Accepting "done" because the model said so
pages.description: A fluent completion claim is accepted as evidence because nothing wrote down, beforehand, what would have to be true.

pages.title: A rule enforced by a hook that never runs
pages.description: Every artefact of enforcement exists — the rule, the script, the test — and no path connects them, so the control is fiction.

pages.title: A failure that was seen once and never again
pages.description: A failure observed inside a session is described in that session and nowhere else, so the next one starts from the report rather than the evidence.

pages.title: A capability the documentation promises and nothing proves
pages.description: A sentence describing what the software does is written once and never connected to anything that would fail if it stopped being true.

pages.title: The first hour in a repository nobody can explain quickly
pages.description: What is conventional in a codebase is knowledge held by its regulars, so every arrival — human or machine — pays for it again.

pages.title: Green tests over stale generated files
pages.description: Tests exercise the code and say nothing about the committed outputs derived from it, so the build is green and the artifacts are wrong.

pages.title: The map
pages.description: Every moment with who recognises it, the area it falls under, and the commands, capabilities, claims, rules and use cases that answer it — derived from the moments themselves.

pages.title: Code that quietly contradicts a written decision
pages.description: The decision was recorded and the implementation went the other way, because nothing relates a decision to the paths it governs.

pages.title: The issue says done and the repository disagrees
pages.description: Completion is recorded as a state change in a tracker rather than as evidence in the repository, so the two drift immediately.

pages.title: Nobody can reconstruct where the milestone actually is
pages.description: Progress is an aggregate that exists only in people, because the parts it aggregates were never recorded in a form anything can add up.

pages.title: Nobody can say why that worker was chosen
pages.description: Provider and model selection is made implicitly, per session, and recorded nowhere, so it cannot be reviewed or repeated.

pages.title: One worker undoing another worker's change
pages.description: A worker sees an unexplained change in its path, judges it wrong, and removes it — correctly, on the evidence it had.

pages.title: The policy changed and its four copies did not
pages.description: A decision is updated at its source and the generated copies keep serving the previous version, with nothing reporting the difference.

pages.title: Re-arguing a decision that was settled last week
pages.description: A decision whose reason lived in a conversation cannot be reviewed, only re-argued — by a worker with less information than the first one had.

pages.title: Re-explaining the same context to a brand-new session
pages.description: Repository knowledge that only ever existed in a conversation has to be re-transmitted by hand to every worker that follows.

pages.title: A result nobody can reproduce, including its author
pages.description: The result is recorded and the conditions that produced it are not, so it is an anecdote rather than a measurement.

pages.title: The rule for that directory, in a README no session ever loaded
pages.description: A local rule is either in the always-loaded file, where every session pays for it, or beside the code, where nothing relates it to the path being edited.

pages.title: The same dead end, explored twice
pages.description: Negative results are the majority of experimental output and the part nobody records, so the search space is re-explored.

pages.title: Two sessions in one checkout, standing on each other
pages.description: Two workers in one working tree see each other only as unexplained file changes, and each treats the other as noise.

pages.title: A public page promising something nothing tests
pages.description: Public material is written by a different act from the code, so it drifts ahead of the behaviour and nothing brings it back.

pages.title: Spend that cannot be tied to anything accepted
pages.description: Consumption is measured per account and outcomes are recorded per person, so the two can never be joined.

pages.title: The strongest model, at maximum effort, renaming a variable
pages.description: Capability, reasoning depth, context size and verbosity collapse into one habit — everything on — because nothing ever named them separately.

pages.title: A task "in progress" that nobody has touched for three weeks
pages.description: A status that was authored rather than computed is true at the moment of writing and decays silently from then on.

pages.title: Three copies of one explanation, and no way to tell which is current
pages.description: Every hand-maintained copy of a fact drifts on its own schedule, and a reader cannot tell which copy is the current one.

pages.title: Three roadmaps, and none of them true
pages.description: A plan kept in prose is a snapshot, and every copy of it drifts on its own schedule; stored status is an assertion that stays true after the world moves.

pages.title: Two agents fixing the same bug in two branches
pages.description: Two workers spend a day each on one defect because ownership was implicit and neither could see the other.

pages.title: Two different rulebooks for one repository
pages.description: Each provider reads its own hand-edited file, nothing relates them, and which contract applies depends on which tool is open.

pages.title: A cheap worker deciding something expensive
pages.description: Capability is dialled down for cost and nothing distinguishes the tasks where that is prudent from the ones where it is expensive.

pages.title: Asking what the workers did last night, and getting a transcript
pages.description: A conversation log records what was said, not what happened, so the operational question has to be answered by a person reading prose.

pages.title: A change whose provenance cannot be reconstructed
pages.description: Attribution stops at the commit, so what authorised a change, what verified it and what governed it are unrecoverable.

pages.title: Finished work that never reached the trunk
pages.description: Workers produce far more than integration absorbs, and nothing distinguishes work that is done from work that is done and landed.
